text: Local metric and antisymmetric-tensor field redefinitions organize the string-amplitude-compatible action. Matching generalized-curvature invariants to a Gauss–Bonnet scheme uses integrations by parts, Bianchi identities, and dimension-dependent over-antisymmetrization identities.

A delta-functional Bianchi constraint introduces a pseudoscalar Lagrange multiplier. Gaussian integration over H, Wick rotation, a functional determinant, and an O(α′) inverse-kernel expansion generate the axion action and a divergent curvature contribution.

The condensate estimate uses transverse–traceless chiral tensor perturbations, the Bunch–Davies vacuum, and perturbative mode equations. The main text gives a heuristic rescaling argument, supplemented by a conformal-time treatment in Appendix D.

Sum spin-preserving modular images of vacuum characters, using thermal AdS or BTZ seeds according to boundary conditions. Fourier/Laplace transforms, Poisson resummation and restricted Kloosterman sums extract primary densities and fixed-spin correlations.

Use boundary bordism invariants to obstruct fillings and bulk cobordism classifications to organize invertible TQFT phases. Cut-and-glue constructions evaluate relative phases through lens spaces and mapping tori; the unitary Z2 analysis uses the Smith isomorphism.

Remove descendants with Zp=√y|η|²Z and subtract modular completions of light states. Decompose the remainder using hyperbolic-Laplacian Eisenstein series and cusp forms; Mellin transforms fix spectral overlaps from near-extremal input.

For a fixed 2π-periodic axial generator, test its invariant norm gφφ. Supplement gφφ>0 by ΔK=gttgφφ−gtφ²<0. In the assumed circular metric class and where gφφ>0, the latter is equivalent to gtt of the inverse metric being negative, making t a local time function.

Solve reduced radial equations for quadrupolar functions H and K. AdS uses horizon Frobenius data and outer least-squares shooting; dS uses two integrations matched across an internal regular singular point. Interpolate the response onto the exact Kerr–(A)dS diagnostic domain, then scan minima of gφφ and −ΔK.

Homotopy fibers implement constraints. Leray–Serre spectral sequences with integral and finite coefficients, cup products, Steenrod operations, spectral Steenrod operations and the universal coefficient theorem determine cohomology and resolve extensions.

Potential anomalies are organized by the Anderson-dual exact sequence involving Ext(Ω_{D+1},Z) and Hom(Ω_{D+2},Z). Ordinary and fiber-based Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequences compute bordism; Adams spectral sequences supply low-degree Spin inputs.

The massive quartic model adds approximate tadpole self-feedback while keeping the flow analytically tractable. A separate one-loop massive-scalar calculation compares derivative expansion with a non-local heat-kernel treatment of gravitational form factors.

Euclidean Wetterich flow evaluated analytically using harmonic gauge, an exponential regulator and xAct tensor algebra. The massless double-seagull diagram yields a first-order momentum-dependent flow; the main text omits its Newton anomalous-dimension term.

Complementary constructions use finite-order duality monodromies associated with Scherk–Schwarz reduction and automorphisms of even, self-dual Narain lattices. The lattice approach reaches examples outside the restricted duality-twist ansatz.

Classical moduli are obtained from the subgroup commuting with the orbifold action; dual orbifold pairs constrain quantum corrections. Brane projections use boundary states and massless Scherk–Schwarz gauge fields.

Construct the one-loop partition function as Z = (1/p) sum_{k,l} Z[k,l], use Poisson resummation and modular S,T transformations, then expand its lowest powers to extract projected spectra. Asymmetric modular phases require case-by-case treatment.

LIV probabilities use perturbative expressions retaining terms described as first order in α, sin²θ13, and LIV coefficients. Sterile analyses use approximate appearance probabilities at three benchmark splittings, numerical simulations, and bi-event plots.

Long-range constraints compare standard-oscillation mock data against nonzero-potential spectra using a Poisson χ² with normalization pulls. Channels are treated as uncorrelated; competing symmetries receive pairwise comparisons.

Long-range probabilities and reconstructed-energy event spectra are computed using GLoBES and a modified snu diagonalization library, including neutrino/antineutrino electron appearance and muon disappearance channels.

Differentiate the horizon condition under λ→λ+η at fixed q, imposing h=h′=0 on an extremal branch and converting geometric mass to AMD mass. Authors report centered finite differences with δη=10⁻⁷ and nearby solver seeds to maintain branch continuity.

Shadow brightness is obtained by numerical ray integration of redshifted emissivity. Extended thermodynamics uses equation-of-state inflection conditions, Maxwell equal area, Gibbs free energy, heat capacity and the isenthalpic derivative μJ=(∂T/∂P)H.

Photon spheres use 2h−rh′=0, effective-potential stability and winding numbers of a two-dimensional vector field. Lensing uses Bozza logarithmic strong-deflection analysis and an optical-metric Gauss–Bonnet integral with a straight-line weak-field trajectory.

Canonical normalization followed by Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization of the charge vectors implements sequential heavy-mode elimination. The projected vector ρ_i⊥ determines the approximate eigenstate direction and f_GS,i=1/|ρ_i⊥|. The paper reviews this hierarchical construction from earlier work.

Monte Carlo examples use N=200, Λ_i^4=M_pl^4 exp(−S_i), S_i uniform on [0,614], rounded unit-variance Gaussian integer charges, and (f_i/f_max)^2 uniform on (0,1). Three benchmarks combine f_max=4×10^12, 4×10^13, 4×10^16 GeV with H_I=10, 10, 10^−2 GeV and inflationary initial-condition sampling.

Gram-determinant ratios express squared projected lengths. Cauchy–Binet gives determinant expectations in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials of the angular second-moment eigenvalues. Replacing an expectation of a ratio by a ratio of expectations supplies the central mean-field estimate; the paper explicitly calls this approximation non-rigorous.

The combined likelihood is the product of input likelihoods, with common signal parameters. Inference uses profile likelihood ratios, nuisance parameters for systematic uncertainties, and asymptotic approximations.

Channel-level extraction includes BDT/DNN score fits in bbττ and parametric diphoton-mass fits in bbγγ, with CMS also fitting dijet mass. In bbττ, simulated background templates are supplemented by data control regions for misidentified hadronic τ candidates.

Signal-strength upper limits use modified frequentist CLs with the upper-limit profile likelihood statistic. Expected results use Asimov datasets with nuisance parameters at their best-fit values and signal parameters set to the assumed hypothesis. The collaborations report software cross-checks using HistFactory and Combine.

Choose FN powers through U(1)F invariance while imposing cancellation of six gauge and mixed gravitational anomalies; use the resulting effective Yukawa textures to estimate mass ratios and mixing angles.

Integrate out explicit FN mediators; enumerate gauge-invariant PQ-breaking operators and their loop-induced scalar potentials, estimating the shift in theta. Neutrino and baryon-asymmetry analyses use type-I seesaw textures, resonant or standard thermal CP asymmetries, and a semi-analytic efficiency factor.
Identify the axion by orthogonality to the massive pseudoscalar and gauge Goldstones. Rotate fermions to their mass basis to obtain derivative couplings and anomaly-induced gluon/photon interactions.

The analysis integrates out massive worldsheet fields to obtain metric and dilaton corrections. NS5 constraints use anomaly descent and inflow, together with a transverse cone whose S4 base contains the wall on its equatorial S3.

For type II, use Spin(8) triality and Spin(7)-preserving four-fermion interactions. Hubbard–Stratonovich linearization followed by promotion to supermultiplets supplies a (1,1) completion; integrating out heavier fields gives W_eff = −BΛΦ8² plus omitted terms.

For 0A/0B, integrate in a (1,1) multiplet with W ∼ μX², change the fermion mass sign through μ = 0, then integrate it out. A spacetime kink uses W ∼ X9X² with lightlike dressing. The authors elaborate a construction already implicit in earlier supercritical work.

Engineer a localized D0 through electric-flux sectors sourced by conjugate Wilson lines, whose infrared limits are reflective conformal interfaces. Use time-dependent irrelevant CFT perturbations and adiabatic switching to argue transmission and finite wall stress-energy.

Use state-operator correspondence and topological defect Hilbert spaces to retain projected parity-odd states. At finite coupling, impose transpose/charge-conjugation monodromies in the SYM description to discuss their loss of supersymmetric energy protection.

Relate free IIA and IIB worldsheets by gauging left-moving fermion parity, including projected and twisted sectors; apply this separately to N copies before gauging SN. Half-space gauging supplies the wall, with its zero-width limit interpreted as a condensation defect.

Use D=Δ0+g1²H+O(g1⁴), an oscillator representation and harmonic action to build closed operator sectors and diagonalize one-loop mixing matrices. Zero eigenvalues select candidates; conformal supercharges S identify their highest weights. Extend H to the interpolating quiver to track anomalous dimensions.

Compare the SCQCD single-trace superconformal index with the inherited-spectrum index. Sieve the mismatch order by order to obtain candidate short multiplets; identical index contributions leave a cohomological ambiguity. The Schur specialization isolates extra Ĉ multiplets.

Apply N=2 superconformal shortening and recombination rules when Δ approaches 2+2j+2R+r and/or 2+2j̄+2R−r. A schematic expansion Q(ǧ)=Q0+ǧQ1+… explains how descendants can contain free-sector, interacting-sector and mixed operators before decoupling.

Cosmological calculations reviewed use lattice-QCD input for temperature-dependent topological susceptibility and simulations of string networks and domain-wall collapse for post-inflationary production.

Higher-dimensional p-forms are expanded in harmonic forms to identify axion zero modes. Field-space kinetic metrics, canonical normalization and nonperturbative instanton potentials determine their effective masses and decay constants.

The paper reviews the imported algebraic classification of monopoles by Langlands-dual weights modulo Weyl transformations, distinguishing this classification from topological stability. It applies an imported domain-wall construction that transports monopoles between vacua with different discrete Wilson lines.

Explicit heterotic mass formulas, level matching, orbifold projections and Wilson-line momentum shifts determine charged spectra. Root inner products, Cartan matrices, representation branching and electric-magnetic Dirac pairings determine gauge algebras, global quotients and lattice relations.

Reviewed tools include superconformal tensor calculus for matter couplings, one- and two-loop renormalization-group evolution of couplings and soft parameters, Higgs-potential minimization, and loop corrections to the light Higgs mass.

Appendix C integrates out the hidden super-Higgs field and heavy visible fields using their stationary field equations, expansions in κ, and rescaled light, GUT and Planck-scale variables to organize the effective light-field potential.

Compact BF gauge theory, Chern–Simons descent and five-dimensional anomaly inflow implement the proposed gauging. The anomaly discussion also uses Fujikawa heat-kernel methods and characteristic-class descent.
Finite character averaging: ZN(θ)=(1/N)Σm ZYM(θ+2πm/N) projects integer topological charge onto Q∈Nℤ. A large-four-volume logarithmic saddle gives the lower envelope of the shifted energies.

Hamilton–Jacobi factorization F = e^(dA)f converts planar extremal wall equations into first-order flows. In seven dimensions the required identity is V = −3f²/5 + K^IJ(∂I f)(∂J f)/2. The imported positive-energy criterion requires a globally defined bounding function stationary at the vacuum.

The ten-dimensional analysis expands the bulk action and non-Abelian DBI/Wess–Zumino actions near an internal origin. Wess–Zumino couplings modify Ramond–Ramond Bianchi identities; DBI terms contribute to the potential and dilaton/Einstein equations.

Embedding-tensor methods encode closed-sector deformations and non-Abelian open-sector structure constants. Vacua are obtained by extremizing the scalar potential; scalar mass spectra test the BF bound, and fermionic shift matrices test preserved supersymmetry.

The wave-function analysis uses the Laplace–Beltrami Hamiltonian, Fourier modes in the periodic coordinate, a wave-function rescaling exposing a geometric potential, modified Bessel functions, and modular Eisenstein/Maaß forms. Near runaway-model effective minima, the authors use a harmonic-oscillator approximation.

Canonical quantization imposes [ti,πj] = iδi_j. The imported identity [F,dH/dx0] = i∇F·∇H translates gradient dot products into commutators and Robertson uncertainty bounds; the paper applies it to taxonomy relations and potentials.

Decompose higher-dimensional Ricci components into external curvature and internal-metric/warp derivatives, then impose either pointwise or integrated Einstein-frame constraints. Appendix A supplies an algebraic non-negativity argument for tr[(h⁻¹∇̄_l h)²] without assuming diagonal h.

Use vanishing leading-order worldsheet beta functions, transform to Einstein frame and contract with null vectors. A local null-vielbein frame expresses the antisymmetric-field contribution as a sum of transverse squares.

Identify matter directions through complex rank-deficient maps M satisfying MX=0 and pull back the magnetic kinetic form using (log s/2πi)²MᵀN⁻¹M. Compare the resulting directions and logarithms with BPS charges, heterotic masses and formal chiral-central-charge thresholds.

Use the nilpotent-orbit theorem, polarized mixed Hodge structures and integral symplectic frames to constrain periods, prepotentials and gauge kinetic matrices. Picard–Fuchs series provide explicit periods and higher-order corrections in the example.

Combine ten-dimensional Einstein and dilaton equations, impose magnetic flux quantization, and identify the charge-related tension of a D(8−n)-brane wrapped on an internal cycle. Compare this tension with the EFT cutoff.

Use four-dimensional F-term stabilization to relate nonperturbative contributions to W0; compare scale dependences and tabulated model parameters. A KPV-type polarization process and DBI/Wess–Zumino potential motivate the proposed light-field interpretation.

The calculation uses covariant dimensional regularization, a consistent measure and regulator for all fields, and known two-loop curvature expressions for Weyl-anomaly coefficients specialized to the isometric background. Local field-redefinition Jacobians are disregarded in this scheme, while zero-mode measure factors remain relevant.

Integrating out y or its dual gives determinant functionals W[x,λ] and W[x,−λ]. Their difference is odd under λ reversal and contains a computable Weyl-anomaly term plus a nontrivial Weyl-invariant remainder; the anomaly yields the leading dilaton shift.

Separate the massless Klein–Gordon equation using spherical harmonics, transform the radial equation to Schrödinger form, and calculate scalar QNMs with sixth-order Padé-averaged WKB. Fundamental-mode tables include WKB convergence diagnostics.

Use Hamilton–Jacobi null geodesics and unstable circular-orbit conditions to obtain photon-sphere and shadow quantities. Third-order WKB supports eikonal optical relations; emission is modeled using σlim=πRs² and a thermal denominator exp(ω̄/TH)−1.

The imported background-field method replaces flat spacetime by the gapped W_k CFT, preserving modular invariance while regulating the IR. Improved helicity/flavor partition functions generate selected curvature contractions; this method cannot probe covariant-derivative operators.

Low-energy scattering expansions, including contact terms and kinematic poles, are combined with modular spectral decomposition, Eisenstein regularization, asymptotic differential equations and Cauchy–Schwarz bounds.

A canonically normalized weighted-Laplacian basis, large-momentum WKB reasoning, Weyl asymptotics and weighted quantum-ergodicity averaging give the KK scaling. Scaling backgrounds also admit Bessel-function solutions. Quantum ergodicity is qualified as conjectural, and strongly curved regions can invalidate derivative suppression.

Dimensional reduction to lower-dimensional Einstein frame yields the moduli kinetic metric and mass scales. Codimension-one bulk equations are solved through logarithmic scaling profiles and a hyperbolic parameterization of the Hamiltonian constraint for more general solutions.

For an eligible effective B with D+B effective, the stated volume bounds are L(D)≤vol(Dmin)≤L(D)+2vol(B), with L(D)=1/2∫[D]J∧J. The upper bound uses holomorphic/antiholomorphic piecewise-calibrated representatives and is minimized over selected candidates B.

Toric cohomology uses Cox-ring monomials classified by pole patterns, lattice-point counting, and reduced simplicial cohomology of induced fan subcomplexes. Stanley–Reisner data filter contributing patterns; multiplication maps supply the remaining kernel calculation. Implementations use CYTools and Macaulay2.

The Koszul sequence gives h0(X,D)=h0(V,Dhat)−h0(V,Dhat+Khat)+dim ker Ftilde, where Ftilde multiplies ambient H1 classes by the defining polynomial. Ambient non-effectiveness together with H1(V,Dhat+Khat)=0 is sufficient, unnecessary, for a hole on X.

Analyze normal-crossing central fibers and their dual intersection complexes, construct invariant-coordinate Weierstrass models, inspect Kodaira vanishing orders, and apply base changes, blow-ups and blow-downs. Reviewed degeneration types II/III/IV correspond to dual-complex dimensions 1/2/3; fourfolds also admit type V.

Use F-theory to geometrize pure perturbative and nonperturbative gs corrections: identify MQ(V/Ω)=Mc.s.(W), recover the orientifold through the semistable Sen limit, and compare boundary degenerations.

For K3×T², perform two torus T-dualities to Type I and analyze previously computed, heterotic-derived D1-instanton corrections using modular invariance, Hecke operators and small-q expansions; these map to IIB D(−1)-instantons.

Use cymetric neural networks to learn ϕ via a complex Monge–Ampère loss, then fit section coefficients. The bicubic uses 100,000 sampled points per moduli value and a width-64, depth-3 GeLU network. Warm starts reduce subsequent training from the initial 240 epochs to 10; the second example uses the same architecture and continuation strategy.

PySR fits the coefficient functions using +, multiplication, exp, log, sin and cos. Each example uses 10 populations of 200 candidates evolved for 300 generations; expressions are selected from error–complexity Pareto fronts. The operator choices have no stated theoretical motivation.

Write K=KFS+ϕ and approximate ϕ by V(t)^(1/3) times a Hermitian bilinear in sections of OX(k), divided by the corresponding products of homogeneous-coordinate norms. Coefficients depend only on moduli ratios. The authors interpret the finite section space as a spectral truncation.

Regularize compact sums and noncompact integrals separately using dimensional regularization and analytic continuation of the Epstein–Hurwitz zeta function. Their difference removes the common radius-independent contribution and leaves sums of modified Bessel functions.

For d=4, reconstruct the relevant dimensionally reduced Einstein-frame action from transformed gravitational equations, matching radion and scale-factor Euler–Lagrange equations rather than directly evaluating the effective action.

Replace unknown exact compact-space modes by a WKB adiabatic expansion with discrete momentum n/r₀. Subtract the corresponding noncompact continuum expansion: the subtraction is required to depend on local geometry rather than global topology. The authors test finiteness, conservation and agreement in the calculable equal-scale-factor limit.

Uses freely acting orbifolds, momentum–winding T-duality, and quantum-symmetry twists. Appendix A presents a partition-function argument using discrete Fourier transforms and an order-dependent radius rescaling.

Reports a one-loop modular-integral evaluation, attributed to Eberhardt, with equal 0A/0B string-frame vacuum energies: real part approximately 11.36 M_s^10 and an imaginary contribution interpreted as vacuum decay. This is a reported calculation, not reproduced here.

Constructs field spaces using disconnected resolution properties (DRP) and strong smoothness properties (SSP). KK charge patterns are compared with D0-brane spectra: DRP gives (n,0)/(0,n), while SSP gives correlated (n,±n) charges.

Complementary diagnostics use worldsheet central charges, anomaly inflow and black-string IR/Higgs-branch constraints, versus instanton corrections inferred through heterotic duality or Type IIA contact potentials and c-map dualities.

Limiting mixed Hodge structures and growth theorems classify degenerations and determine classical asymptotic Kähler-potential scaling. Semi-stable geometry supplies additional information beyond this algebraic classification.

F-/M-theory duality maps candidate strings to wrapped-string EFT particles. Localised geometric modes and reductions of C3 and C6 determine a one-dimensional quantum mechanics, subsequently lifted to the string worldsheet.

Expand the BST membrane action in Riemann normal coordinates, using static gauge and fixed κ symmetry. Quadratic fluctuations determine one-loop determinants; zero modes are separated, and the examples organise into four complex scalars and four fermions.

Use the κ-projection and uplifted Killing spinors to identify supersymmetric embeddings and chiral fixed loci. Evaluate fluctuation determinants by ζ-function regularisation; the general AdS4 answer uses sine and double-sine functions.

For AdS7 giants, expand in spherical KK modes to obtain supersymmetric quantum mechanics. Sum multiwound particles, then represent the tower by a Schwinger-type contour with a Mittag-Leffler kernel to investigate its origin pole.

Enumerate relevant three- and four-point on-shell amplitudes using naive dimensional analysis, factorisation and helicity selection. Extract one-loop beta-functions from UV-divergent Passarino–Veltman bubbles using two-particle unitarity cuts, subtracting triangle and box contributions where necessary.

Construct fixed-t nonforward dispersion relations, strip helicity weights and symmetrise s↔u. Smear over p=√(−t), enforcing nonnegative UV partial-wave kernels with polynomial functionals, asymptotic analysis and an SDPB numerical grid.

Use Wigner-function partial waves, angular-momentum selection and BCFW deformations of cut legs to analyse the forward t-channel discontinuity. In IR-finite cases, relate the remaining cuts to finite exclusive cross sections to constrain the beta-function sign.

Estimate ambient detector emission using nµBH = ρDM/M, a single-object waiting time of order TH/|dM/dt|visible, and τdet = τobs/(V nµBH). This counts emission from the ensemble inside the fiducial volume.

Parametrize memory-burden evaporation by (dM/dt)MB = S^(-k)(dM/dt)SC, typically 1 <= k <= 3. The onset also involves the fraction q of mass lost and transition width δ, controlled by a microscopic parameter p. Modified entropy scalings are used to estimate lifetimes.

Analyze neutron-star capture through local energy and momentum conservation and geometric accretion. Estimate initial seeds from the core-collapse dark-matter flux, then compare stellar destruction times with observed lifetimes while requiring accretion to dominate evaporation.

Identify integer-spin simple currents through neutral monodromy charge QJ(i) = hJ + hi - hJ×i modulo 1. Group local primaries into orbit characters, retaining stabilizer factors. Fixed-point resolution supplies extra modular information when an orbit splits.

Use Sugawara decomposition into commuting gauge and residual stress tensors, then tensor-product KM and unitary minimal-model characters. Modular data for a11,2 are obtained through a11,2 + a1,12 ⊂ a23,1; e7,2 data use the diagonal coset (e7,1 + e7,1)/e7,2 ≅ M(5,4).

Write E = Σ Ciχi with integer Ci and solve PC = C, SC = C, where P selects integral left conformal weights. Match the first two q coefficients to the six-dimensional massless index. Factorization of S reduces the otherwise large linear-algebra problem.
Evaluates dilaton and radion values at black-brane horizons, integrates their field-space distance, and expresses leading temperature and entropy scalings in string, Planck and species-scale units.

Revisits the circle-flow uplift to an orbifold and extends toroidal reductions using integrable scalar geodesics. Diagonal representatives uplift to static Kasner metrics, whose generic curvature singularity is diagnosed through the Kretschmann scalar.

Uses one-dimensional effective actions, the lapse constraint and a blackening factor. For constant potential, the gauge N=A makes scalar trajectories affinely parametrized moduli-space geodesics; the blackening and scalar equations diagnose singular prospective horizons.
Constructs the family through double Wick rotation, a nontrivial diffeomorphism and reparametrization of known black holes, retaining a regular massless sector.

Uses asymptotic radial expansions and holographic renormalization with boundary counterterms to identify scalar sources, VEVs and the stress tensor. Eliminates interior parameters to express regular solutions in terms of boundary data.

Solves the STU Killing-spinor equations using a radial projector and constructs the type IIB metric and self-dual five-form uplift. Satisfaction of the five- and ten-dimensional equations is an author-reported check, not independently reproduced here.

Compare standard and dilaton Weyl superconformal constructions after integrating out auxiliary fields. Use integration by parts, Bianchi identities and leading two-derivative equations to remove redundant terms, yielding a common Riemann basis with no derivatives of field strengths and at most first derivatives of scalars.

Use heterotic dimensional reduction and circle reduction of a six-dimensional Riemann-squared-minus-Gauss–Bonnet combination. Dualize three-form flux and transform from string to Einstein frame; the latter construction is rewritten as a quartic anti-self-dual tensor-multiplet coupling before reduction.

Evaluate vector corrections and their equations of motion on the leading static harmonic-function BPS solution. Separately expand around constant scalar moduli and decompose gauge fields into graviphoton and orthogonal matter directions to investigate the rigid limit.

Fixed-point and Jacobian analysis, invariant-submanifold reductions, analytical thawing approximations, and numerical cosmological integrations. Nongeodesic stability regions are determined numerically because their eigenvalue expressions are cumbersome.

Modified CLASS background evolution with shooting, followed by Metropolis–Hastings MCMC in MontePython. Data comprise Planck 2018 distance priors, Pantheon+, 6dFGS/SDSS DR7 MGS BAO, and cosmic chronometers.

Democratic RR reduction with duality constraints imposed on equations of motion; axion canonical normalization from the Kähler metric; and two-form/axion dualization followed by integrating out auxiliary four-forms.

Phenomenological estimates use axion misalignment, approximate neutralino thermal-freeze-out formulas, and an axion–photon polarization-rotation estimate. The packet does not supply a model-specific annihilation-channel computation.
The imported quadratic four-form EFT gives ∂aV = μaX. For two axions, ∂aV = μaX + μ̃aY and ∂bV = μ⋆Y; nonzero μa and μ⋆ permit X = Y = 0 at stationary points.

Use zeta regularization, including the formal assignment sum over positive integers of 1 = −1/2, to motivate a finite-part prescription for the exponentially growing GV sum. Minimally subtract all divergent terms at the quantum-corrected conifold.
Start from the Gopakumar–Vafa one-loop Schwinger integrals over BPS D2–D0 states. Differentiate F0 three times and F1 once to isolate the relevant polynomial coefficients and simplify the sums.

Obtain conifold periods through Picard–Fuchs equations and analytic continuation from large complex structure; match logarithmic asymptotic expansions through the mirror map. F1 additionally uses period-derived Kähler data and the holomorphic-anomaly expression with singular-point boundary conditions.
Dimensionally reduce the Einstein–Hilbert action, perform a Weyl transformation, and introduce a canonical Einstein-frame radion. Brane matter then acquires radion-dependent couplings.

Compute one-loop Casimir stress energy using flat-space Green functions and the method of images, subtracting the uncompactified contribution. Express massive terms through modified Bessel functions and, in five dimensions, polylogarithms.

Numerically evolve homogeneous Friedmann and radion equations in the e-fold variable N, including energy exchange with dark matter. Compare Hubble and comoving angular-distance ratios with DESI DR2 using a diagonal χ².

Numerically solve the coupled TOV–scalar equations using a modified version of pyTOV-ST that includes the axion, its potential, and the kinetic coupling. The numerical approach replaces the earlier approximate adiabatic axion treatment discussed in the paper.

Model stellar matter through P(ρ)=Kᵢρ^Γᵢ in successive density intervals, using SLy-type adiabatic indices. Reference dividing densities are ρ₁=10^14.7 g/cm³ and ρ₂=10^15.0 g/cm³, with a lower-density matching region.

Assess screening through the exterior dilaton charge L relative to a no-axion-gradient reference L₀. The proposed effective coupling is g_eff=gL/L₀; quantitative evaluation from the numerical axion profiles remains to be performed.

Motivate the topological mechanism by narrative summaries of scalar–tensor and PT-symmetric wormholes, non-orientable BTZ constructions, and Möbius-strip or Klein-bottle analogies. The cited geometries are not independently established by this packet's discussion.

Use a phase argument based on e^(−iEt/ℏ) under t→−t and compare displayed positive- and negative-energy Dirac spinors. These are the explicit algebraic illustrations offered for the proposed spectrum reversal.

Review the canonical-algebra argument: with position fixed and momentum reversed, a unitary transformation leaves i unchanged and fails to preserve the displayed commutator. Introduce conventional anti-unitary T=UK, where K performs complex conjugation.

Apply Sen’s entropy function: insert the AdS₂, constant-electric-field and constant-dilaton ansatz, form E = 2π(eq − f), and extremize over v, e and ϕ₀. Restore the specific total derivative discarded in reducing the covariant two-derivative action; it affects entropy despite leaving the equations of motion unchanged.

Use the imported duality reduction and field-redefinition framework, with F(ρ) = −ρ²/2 + Σ(n≥2)c₂ₙρ^(2n). The paper states that only one Wilson coefficient survives at each derivative order in this reduced description.

Use the imported inverse-function parametrization f = F′(ρ), ρ(f) = −f[1 + h(f²)], and β(y) = ∫₀ʸh(y′)dy′. Asymptotic expansions identify mass and charge parameters; a separate near-horizon expansion determines the extremality condition Δ = 0.

Use W = XYZ, yielding V ∼ X²Y² + Y²Z² + Z²X². A nonzero coordinate makes the other two multiplets massive; all gaps close at the origin. Moving through this point implements branching while going up and down RG flow. Adding Y³ lifts the Y-axis branches when allowed by the quotient symmetries.

Integrate out massive multiplets using one-loop bosonic and fermionic diagrams, a background/fluctuation expansion and Feynman parametrization. Supersymmetric determinant cancellation removes potential corrections, while derivative terms renormalize the target-space metric and dilaton.

Infer heterotic junction conditions from vertex-operator three-point selection rules in the common supercritical description, allowing tachyon-background insertions before removing gapped directions. Compare representations under shared gauge SO(8)³×SO(7) and Lorentz SO(7) subgroups. The IIB bouquet’s spectral routing is instead motivated by anomaly matching.

Scattering amplitudes are decomposed into ordinary-particle and continuum contributions. Euclidean bubble examples use spectral mass integrations, dimensional regularization and Cutkosky rules; ordinary terms receive Feynman continuation, while complex-pair terms receive average continuation.

Cauchy contour representations separate contributions from infinity, the origin, extra poles and branch discontinuities. The change of variable w=−z² converts the imaginary-axis discontinuity into a cut suitable for spectral integration. Appendix theorems classify poles and admissible sheets.
Single-field exponential quintessence is studied using dynamical systems: fixed points, their stability and late-time attractors organize cosmological histories and asymptotic behavior.

Dimensional reduction retains universal volume and dilaton fields ρ, τ, supplemented by source-direction fields σI. Power counting and canonical field redefinitions expose exponential contributions to the scalar potential.

Existence no-go arguments combine ten-dimensional equations to constrain R4, or construct canonical directional inequalities ∂φ̂V + cV/Mp ≤ 0. For V > 0 these imply Mp‖∇V‖/V ≥ c and εV ≥ c²/2. Hessian eigenvalues diagnose perturbative instability.

The author applies Buscher dualities to NSNS and RR fields, including dilaton-dependent Einstein-frame transformations, and extremizes the original and dual integrated superpotentials with respect to their eight retained scalar variables.

Invariant-form decompositions, Maurer–Cartan equations and intrinsic-torsion classes describe the dual geometry. Dimensional reduction supplies scalar potentials; the appendix explicitly matches the original NSNS potential contribution to dual internal curvature.

Decompose each independent solution as uα=rα exp(iθα), with complex vector rα. Fix the local rephasing redundancy by Im(r̄α·rα')=0; canonical normalization gives 2θα'|rα|²=1. Evolve real Nf×2 amplitude matrices without evolving auxiliary phases.

Initialize in instantaneous frequency eigenvectors with amplitudes proportional to 1/√(2ωα), vanishing initial amplitude derivatives, and θα'=ωα. Sequential injection at a common fixed physical wavelength avoids unnecessarily long integrations of larger-k modes.

Parallel-transport an orthonormal vielbein along the background and rescale Fourier fluctuations by a. The resulting canonical equations are v''+Ω²v=0, with Ω²=(k²−a''/a)I+a²M²; the projected mass matrix retains geometric effects.

Construct minimal top-Yukawa witnesses from an allowed Higgs-up entry and a neutral pair of 10 charges. Minimality is under deletion of stored charge data; repeated use of one 10 charge is represented by a singleton set.

Iterate admissible immediate super-spectra using accumulated and newly added multisets until no new spectra appear, then deduplicate. Separately prove an abstract completeness endpoint from soundness, witness-completion containment, and closure hypotheses, and specialize it to viableCharges I.

Complete each witness by adding a down-Higgs charge and a 5̄-matter charge, remove duplicates, and filter by dangerous-operator and regeneration predicates. These completed witnesses seed the subsequent enlargement procedure.

An illustrative one-loop RG estimate evolves un-Higgsed SU(5) below MGUT with heavy scalars omitted. Appendix B treats the inflaton as the mode controlling condensate scales and phase mixing, arguing that this changes axion mass and composition without shifting the CP-conserving minimum.

The analysis uses the damped homogeneous axion equation, an inflaton-dependent scalar potential, instanton zero-mode counting and schematic ’t Hooft operators. A two-phase effective description identifies the axion and its orthogonal heavy phase.

Warm-inflation backgrounds obey inflaton friction 3H + Υ and radiation production: ϕ̈ + (3H + Υ)ϕ̇ + V,ϕ = 0 and ρ̇r + 4Hρr = Υϕ̇². A thermal bath has ρr = CR T⁴. Inflation ends at εH = 1; slow roll gives εH approximately εV/(1 + Q).

The authors use the Mathematica package WI2easy, employing deterministic Fokker–Planck evolution for perturbations, to compute backgrounds, the scalar spectrum and G(Q). Spectral tilt and tensor-to-scalar ratio are evaluated at horizon exit; entropy matching determines the relevant e-fold interval without a separate reheating epoch.

The potential is separated into KKLT and brane-dependent contributions. The angular expansion retains one additional subleading term in ε/μ compared with the cited predecessor. The radial effective potential is written V(ϕ) = V0[Λ + C1ϕ − C3/2ϕ^(3/2) + C2ϕ² − D/ϕ⁴]; the negative fractional-power term is imported rather than derived again.

Most of the paper is a conceptual overview of earlier possifold work. It explains how reorganizing phase-space path integrals is claimed to reveal entropy bounds and the phase-space regions responsible for entanglement; the short black-hole application relies on that imported formalism.

Surface charges are integrals over codimension-two surfaces, with integrands determined by the canonical one-form Θ. The proposed route toward an explicit microstate inventory is to evaluate bifurcation-surface charges of solutions and identify the phase-space states distinguished by them.

The main application imports a generalized Ryu–Takayanagi prescription and applies the possifold flow ∂Σ → B to Φ, producing Φ(B) ∈ Γ(B). The leading entropy is read from K[Φ(B)]/ℏ. Near B, the diffeomorphism generated by K agrees with the Killing vector, permitting the stated extremization within the black-hole solution.

Analyze worldline Hamiltonians, Casimirs, κ-symmetry and Euclidean saddles; compute scalar and fermion determinants using Schwinger proper time, factorized AdS2/S2 heat kernels and Hubbard–Stratonovich transforms. Superconformal representations organize the Pauli-coupled hypermultiplet calculation.

Use the Gopakumar–Vafa proper-time representation, equivalently Borel resummation of the constant-map series; apply Poisson resummation and contour deformations to separate line-integral and residue contributions. Causality fixes the initial integration prescription.

Encode the F-term tower in a generalized homogeneous prepotential, solve higher-derivative attractor equations, and evaluate the Wald expression or its Legendre-transform form involving the free energy Im F.

Compare proper times along observer and computer trajectories; combine uniform acceleration with Unruh temperature. Higher-dimensional isometric embeddings supply temperatures in selected curved geometries, with explicit warnings that arbitrary embeddings need not work.
Use Bogoliubov mode mixing and boosted Casimir stress tensors for the cylinder, Boltzmann estimates for thermal survival, and conserved Kerr geodesic equations integrated between horizons.

Compute graviton two- and three-point and vector two-, three- and four-point flows. Project vertices at symmetric kinematics and expand around zero external momenta, using a Litim-type regulator, harmonic Landau gravity gauge and transverse-traceless gravity projections.

Use the non-perturbative functional RG equation for the infrared-regulated effective action, solve the truncated dimensionless beta functions for zeros, and linearize them to obtain stability eigenvalues and eigendirections.

Use the GVW superpotential W=∫(F3−τH3)∧Ω, expand around the Fermat point, and solve the supersymmetric Minkowski equations W=∂I W=0. The quadratic superpotential determines massive directions; higher coefficients test nonlinear constraints on its kernel.

Classify supersymmetric integral flux choices and compute quadratic ranks. Split fields into massive and massless sectors, solve the massive-field equations recursively, and substitute into the remaining F-term equations to test higher-order stabilization.

Determine e-folds self-consistently from the durations of moduli-dominated epochs and perturbative decay histories. Estimate ΔN_eff from hidden/visible decay-rate ratios and compare predictions with the observational analyses quoted in this version.

Use the N=1 F-term potential, large-volume minimization and a canonical inflaton transformation. Estimate loop effects using extrapolated torus-orbifold results and EFT arguments, then compute leading slow-roll parameters, perturbation amplitude, e-folds and spectral observables.

Integrate propagation speeds through Gaussian gravitational-wave backgrounds between asymptotically Minkowski regions. Compute GR through second order and dCS through first order; optimize the negative delay over amplitude, with the extremum satisfying |ΔTdCS|=2ΔTGR^(2).

Linearize the coupled metric–scalar equations in transverse-traceless gauge, Fourier transform on the restricted vacuum background, and extract propagation eigenmodes. Tensor manipulations are aided by xAct; Appendix A additionally presents a projected-polarization consistency argument.

Use scattering and loop-counting estimates for perturbativity and the species scale, together with chiral-anomaly matching for the dCS interaction. Additional higher-dimension operators are estimated by power counting rather than a complete renormalized heat-kernel calculation.

Euclidean proper-time/worldline representations separate winding sectors and their Aharonov–Bohm phases. Large-mass potentials use n=±1 saddles and classical approximations to a warp-dependent functional; fluctuation corrections are organized in inverse effective mass.

For fermions, reduce the determinant to a 2×2 monodromy matrix eiqθUh(p). Its eigenvalues e±ℓ(p) organize winding contributions weighted by e⁻ⁿℓ⁽ᵖ⁾. Tree-level boundary-source potentials instead follow from classical bulk profiles and their on-shell action.

Compute Casimir energy from axion-dependent KK spectral functions built from bulk Bessel solutions and boundary matching. Subtract the θ-independent vacuum energy, use contour integration, and approximate the large-mass momentum integral with a Gaussian spectral function.

Rewrite the cosmological equations as an autonomous ODE system in Hubble-normalized scalar velocity, trigonometric potential variables and fluid densities. Algebraic constraints bound the forcing term; differential inequalities then bound velocity growth and fluid dilution.

Translate duration inequalities into density-parameter and e-fold restrictions. Appendix B sharpens estimates by retaining damping and quantitative fluid dilution; Appendix A relates complex exponential coordinates to the real periodic system and compares with slow-roll estimates.

Estimate reheating using tree-level widths and one-loop Coleman–Weinberg slope/curvature restrictions at two field scales. Integrate an analytical decay-source Boltzmann equation for dark matter; use Casas–Ibarra neutrino parametrization, hierarchical CP asymmetry and sphaleron conversion for leptogenesis.
Transform to the Einstein frame with g̃µν=f gµν and VE=VJ/f²; canonically normalize through dζ/dϕ=√Π, where Π=1/f+(3κ/2)(f′/f)² and κ=1 for metric gravity or 0 for Palatini.

Use potential slow-roll observables, asymptotic analytical expressions and numerical benchmark scans in n and ξ. Normalize scalar perturbations and estimate horizon-exit e-folds using an assumed thermal history.

Introduce auxiliary scalars and impose their algebraic curvature constraints; then rescale the metric to obtain an Einstein frame for the pure model and an alternative Weyl-squared frame for the conformal model. Equivalence is restricted by singularities of these transformations.

Decompose perturbations into scalars, transverse vectors and transverse-traceless tensors under spatial rotations, fix a Newtonian-type gauge, and eliminate constrained fields. For the anisotropic calculation, the proceedings also describe reducing higher derivatives to second order before solving and substituting constraints.

Study clustering using basis-dependent ℓ1 coherence and overlaps after one or two SU(∞) generators. Torus-basis differential generators and Fourier-mode estimates are used; the overlap discussion assumes an L² wavefunction with finite first and second derivatives.

Use quantum speed limits based on relative purity to associate state variation with ds² = κ²[tr(ρ dρ)]², then apply Cauchy-Schwarz and purity bounds. Trace out discrete internal-symmetry states when constructing this continuous-parameter path.

Impose vanishing functional variation of the metric-dependent action density with respect to the arbitrary parameter metric. Construct Lagrangian superoperators by removing traces from the effective functionals, and define Hamiltonian components through the corresponding energy-momentum operator.

Construct GNS representations from positive limiting polynomial functionals and take double commutants. The enlarged-algebra argument uses spectral projections of compact q^{Δ n_tot} to recover chord operators and show that its commutant is scalar.

Rewrite KM correlators as unnormalized traces with projector Pω. Gaussian Wick contractions give oriented M-chords and additional dashed chords connecting insertions to Pω; crossing weights and forbidden orientations determine polynomial correlators.

The proposed infrared identification combines an imported nonperturbative factorization result for generalized pinning defects, previously studied GNY boundary conditions, defect b-monotonicity, and discrete-symmetry anomaly matching.

The explicit large-N treatment uses the Gross–Neveu Hubbard–Stratonovich formulation, folds the interface into a doubled half-space boundary problem, and Weyl maps to H³. Fermion propagators and scalar Schwinger–Dyson kernels are analyzed through boundary conformal blocks, harmonic spectral inversion, and regularized free energies.

Impose functional equalities at Chebyshev nodes in −1<t<0 or −1/3<a<0. Endpoint clustering resolves rapid variation while avoiding the graviton pole; fixed-t also excludes t=−1 because its kernel becomes singular at μ=1.

Map s′=μ=1/z, approximate the spectral integral by a Riemann sum, and truncate the even-spin expansion at Jmax. Spectral densities and EFT coefficients become linear-program variables, with positivity or 0≤ρ≤2 imposed directly.

Use twice-subtracted fixed-t improved sum rules and fully crossing-symmetric fixed-a dispersion relations. Expansion at fixed a generates even-k sum rules whose tree-level low-energy sides involve finitely many EFT coefficients without constructing improved linear combinations.

Generalized loop corrections are motivated through heavy-mode contributions to modulus kinetic terms and a Coleman–Weinberg estimate. Post-inflationary predictions follow from modulus masses and decay widths, matter-dominated epochs, and branching fractions into visible particles and ultra-light axions.

The review uses four-dimensional supergravity F-term potentials, no-scale and extended no-scale cancellations, canonical normalization, and slow-roll observables. It organizes inflationary models by perturbative versus nonperturbative lifting and bulk/fibre versus local/blow-up divisors.

The author extends Wald's covariant curvature variation to the nonlocal action using horizon binormals, then estimates entropy scaling on quasi-Schwarzschild backgrounds. Renormalization and conformal-anomaly arguments are used to discuss quantum corrections and finite theories with killer operators.

The focusing argument uses the null Raychaudhuri equation, horizon-generator properties, and energy conditions. Modified field equations are contracted with k^μk^ν, expanded at low curvature, and examined for sign-indefinite terms and positivity of the inverse kinetic operator.

Reduce to a four-dimensional Einstein-frame potential, include the genus-one cosmological constant, and solve the background equations. Linearize the ten-dimensional equations and expand fluctuations in scalar, transverse-vector and tensor harmonics on both spheres.

Impose Lorentz-like gauge conditions, track residual diffeomorphisms and two-form gauge transformations, and extract physical masses from coupled harmonic-sector equations. Compare those masses with the appropriate AdS stability bounds.

Estimate decay exponents from Euclidean wrapped-NS5 DBI and Chern–Simons actions. Use calibrations to select minimum-volume internal representatives and optimize the effective charge-to-tension parameter over wrapping cycles.

Combine BBHL α′³ and logarithmic loop corrections to stabilize the volume perturbatively. Add winding-loop and higher-derivative F4 contributions to lift the remaining Kähler directions, together with a modeled uplift term.

Numerically integrate covariant multi-field background equations using e-fold time, the tree-level Kähler metric and the corrected scalar potential. Report trajectories, slow-roll observables, mass eigenvalues and evolving KK/string scales.

Seiberg–Witten periods, holomorphy and instanton selection rules, and Picard–Fuchs/Frobenius continuation organize the gauge discussion. The KKLT analysis minimizes over the axion and applies scalar stationarity and Hessian conditions.
Superspace component expansion, Berezin integration, and algebraic elimination of auxiliary fields organize the Lagrangian; localization introduces curved superspace and Kähler-covariant derivatives.

UV/IR asymptotic expansions classify endpoints and provide boundary conditions for numerical flows. Generalized dimensional reduction identifies the axion with an internal n-form and motivates γ=1/b for shrinking spherical compactifications.
First-order flow formalism uses S=φ̇, W=−2(d−1)Ȧ, T=R(ζ)e^{−2A}, and X=Y²ȧ²=Q²e^{−2dA}. Physical solutions require X≥0 and a fixed sign of T; φ ceases to be a global coordinate at scalar bounces.

Compare renormalized Euclidean on-shell free energies, including Gibbons–Hawking–York terms and counterterms, only at matching curvature and axion sources. The positive-curvature calculation chooses renormalization scheme ω=1; horizon-area and thermodynamic entropy expressions are also compared.

Construct topological operators by evaluating pulled-back U(1)-cohomology classes on closed submanifolds. Universal coefficients identify these classes with characters of integral homology; examples also use Hurewicz and Künneth.
Encode flux identities in Chevalley–Eilenberg differential graded-commutative algebras; use Sullivan models and Whitehead L∞-algebras to extract rational homotopy generators and cohomology ranks.
Quantize charged D0-brane fermion zero modes, impose a Z2 projection correlating spacetime and gauge-spinor chiralities, and combine representations under enhanced gauge symmetry.
Construct junctions by gluing interval/ouroboros branches, encode local joining data in trefoil diagrams, and trace chiral representations while allowing quantum superpositions of joining patterns.
Resolve boundaries from nearby identification points into ouroboric variants, then use local capacitor diagrams and type I′ exceptional gauge-enhancement intuition to formulate spectrum rules.

One-loop tools include splitting the spectrum above/below a threshold, modular bounds, asymptotic differential equations generalizing Narain Laplacian identities, modular-invariant IR regularization, harmonic zero-mode decomposition and integration by parts to isolate volume-like and Casimir-like terms.

Integrate reduced internal partition functions over worldsheet moduli spaces. The internal free energy F probes cutoff scalings associated with R⁴ corrections; vacuum amplitudes V additionally include the external partition function. F equals particular four-point low-energy amplitudes only in special settings.

WKB expansion of Schrödinger or Wheeler-DeWitt equations: the leading phase supplies a Hamilton-Jacobi function, while amplitude/current transport supplies a continuity equation. ADM constraints are deparameterised by selecting an internal clock.

Near stable attractors, expand the Euclidean Hamilton-Jacobi function quadratically, extract Gaussian covariances from its Hessian, and use Gaussian Wasserstein formulas. A locally flattened Jacobi coordinate incorporates a slowly varying potential-dependent metric.

Reviewed mathematical tools include Monge-Kantorovich optimisation, quadratic Benamou-Brenier transport, and shifted Tonelli/Mañé costs. A cited boundary-term relation between Mañé and Jacobi-Maupertuis costs is used to identify their optimal couplings.

Use imported chiral-perturbation-theory, nuclear, atomic and molecular calculations; supplement missing hadronic inputs with NDA. Include long-distance hadronic contributions to the electron–nucleon coupling CS.

Combine RG evolution and operator mixing with approximate linear UV-to-IR matching and linear IR-to-observable response matrices. Analyze source-dependent EDM ratios and invert selected systems when several sources contribute.
Adopt QCD sum-rule nucleon EDM expressions, calibrating their uncertain overall normalization against lattice tensor charges evolved from 2 to 1 GeV. This follows an imported normalization strategy.

Invoke semi-ampleness and Bertini smoothness/irreducibility arguments for multiples of the EFT-string divisor. The relevant linear-system image has dimension three for type IV and two for type III; type II fiber multiples require separate treatment.

Identify candidate EFT strings as NS5-branes wrapping orientifold-even nef holomorphic divisors, then lift them to M5-branes on coassociative four-cycles. Test whether their deformation spectrum permits the freely propagating gravitational string required by the classical decompactification.

Count M5 worldsheet zero modes using self-dual two-forms and apply the orientifold projection. Separately examine candidate light particle towers, their brane–antibrane instabilities, quantum mass corrections and the M-theory interpretation of KK modes.

Solve DIW=0, match vacuum values to the ten-dimensional solution up to stated field rescalings, evaluate the untwisted closed-string Hessian and scalar conformal dimensions, and test whether D-term gaugings could instead reproduce the new flux potential.

Circle-reduce the known four-dimensional Kähler potentials and supplement the superpotentials with proposed holomorphic flux terms. Compare V=eK(gIJ̄ DIW D̄J̄W̄−4|W|²), at vanishing axions, with direct reduction of flux energies and smeared source actions.

Solve ten-dimensional Killing-spinor conditions recast as differential-form bispinor equations, together with Bianchi identities. These initially establish at least one three-dimensional Killing spinor; the stronger supersymmetry claim is then supported through the effective theory.

Apply two independent TsT transformations, (x+, y4; γ1) and (φ2, y3; γ2), to the D1-D5 seed, evaluate conserved flux charges, and take an anisotropic near-horizon scaling r → λr, x+ unchanged, x− → x−/λ², followed by λ → 0.

A TsT transformation consists of T-duality, a coordinate shift with parameter γ, and a second T-duality. For E = G + B, the supplied transformation is E′ = E(γE + 1)^−1, with γ an antisymmetric two-by-two matrix; the dilaton changes by the determinant, and R-R polyforms transform through Spin(2,2).

Warp a three-dimensional geometry using a Killing-dual one-form A and the deformation g → g + ϖA⊗A, equivalently rescaling a Hopf fibre. The left/right one-forms satisfy opposite-sign Beltrami equations, ★3dA = ±(2/ℓ)A.

Construct cyclic quotients using actions (z1,z2)→(ωz1,ωz2) and (ωz1,ω−1z2). An alternative construction excises polar neighborhoods and glues truncated Gibbons–Hawking ALE spaces along lens-space boundaries, imposing induced-metric and extrinsic-curvature matching.

Use Wilson-loop analogies with fractional gauge instantons, combinatorial state counting, a nonlinear sigma model on the proposed moduli space, curvature-induced masses and semiclassical periodic potentials to motivate hairon properties.

Model cold neutrinos with an attractive contact interaction; apply a Hubbard–Stratonovich pairing field, Nambu–Gorkov variables and a one-loop fermion determinant. A uniform saddle gives a gap equation, followed by a Ginzburg–Landau description of amplitude and phase fluctuations.
Asymptotic power/exponential ansätze in Laplace eigenvalue equations, Eisenstein-series expansions, and genus-one topological-string free energies for vector-moduli dependence of the species number.

Coleman–Weinberg supertraces include light and massive tower states up to the species cutoff. Tower sums are approximated by integrals; a tower-induced metric correction is expressed as a superspace D-term whose auxiliary-field component contributes vacuum energy.

For inflation, numerically integrate covariant multifield equations using e-fold number N, the field-space metric estimated from the tree-level Kähler potential and a specified corrected scalar potential; evaluate reported observables at horizon exit.

Use GLSM charges, SR ideals, intersection tensors and c2(X) to classify divisor topology. The review gives χ(D)=∫(D³+c2(X)D) and χh(D)=∫(2D³+c2(X)D)/12, supplemented by cohomCalg or CYTools computations of divisor Hodge numbers.

Collider estimates sum KK propagators at amplitude level, replace the sum by an integral using dimensional regularization, estimate multiplicity as MBH/(2TH), and propose fitting log temperature against log reconstructed mass.

Uses horizon, entropy, and temperature scalings; a leading-term near-horizon Schwinger estimate; and phenomenological lifetime relations. Rotating emission is expressed through greybody mode sums and spin-down plus Schwarzschild phases.

The BKL argument invokes symbolic dynamics of the Kasner map, modular-group transfer operators and tropicalization. Reported numerical support uses normalized-Laplacian spectra of critical Erdős-Rényi graphs with N = 2000, averaged over 100 realizations; this is an author-reported test, not reproduced here.

Apply Eynard-Orantin residue recursion to (XG, x = z, y = w, B). Theorem 3.3 identifies distinct graph eigenvalues with multi-cut matrix-model endpoints, possibly after scaling. The subsequent qualification requires additional filling-fraction data and leaves a graph-derived effective potential unresolved.

Use the double cover XG → P1 and Riemann-Hurwitz, including a branch point at infinity for odd polynomial degree. The displayed differential basis is zj−1 dz/w; periods over symplectic cycles produce a period matrix, with an appendix proposing numerical integration and ΩG = A^−1B.

Assess circular timelike curves through the sign of gθθ and compute their proper-time period. Separately estimate a relative Minkowski-to-Gödel probability using a Euclidean no-boundary wavefunction and saddle-point approximation.
Construct entire functions through H(x)=α∫₀^{p(x)}[1−g(w)]dw/w, specializing to g(w)=exp(−wⁿ). Analyze the sign and stationary points of H2 to select form factors admitting the vacuum solution.

Substitute the Gödel ansatz into the vacuum equations in an orthonormal coframe. Reduce the tensor equations to three algebraic conditions using x=ω²/Λ*², z=(m²−4ω²)/Λ*² and the form-factor combination f.

Slow-roll background and spectral-index expressions are evaluated by integrating backward from the end condition ε=−Ḣ/H²=1 to CMB horizon exit. Parameter scans translate observational ns–r contours into α–β regions.

Post-inflationary scalar evolution is solved numerically using the full field equation. The instantaneous pressure-to-density ratio is averaged over an oscillation period to obtain the reheating equation of state.

GW forecasts combine a power-law primordial tensor spectrum with a reheating-dependent transfer spectrum. Extra radiation is constrained using the integrated GW energy density and the adopted ΔNeff≤0.17 bound; quartic detectability maps use signal-to-noise ratio greater than 10.

For gravity, matter is integrated out in Weyl gauge. The WZW conformal anomaly controls the leading metric dependence; timelike Liouville theory with bc ghosts organizes the large-Nf fluctuation expansion.

Hartle–Hawking hemisphere path integrals construct states and overlaps. Gauge fields are decomposed into instanton, transverse and pure-gauge parts; compact zero-mode integration supplies selection rules. Background gauge fields determine counterterms for smeared topological operators.

Abelian bosonization expresses the interacting model as a compact scalar coupled through a BF term, with scalar and Maxwell kinetic terms. On the fixed sphere the fluctuation action is quadratic, making Gaussian integration exact. The preliminary BF analysis is explicitly reviewed material.

Identify mass hierarchies using tower/species taxonomy or species counting. Introduce instanton vectors Si=−∇log Si and express the proposed window along a canonical unit direction u as |Si·u|≤(αlightest−Λsp-vector)·u.

Evaluate BPS-constrained Schwinger sums after selecting light towers. Solve Diophantine charge constraints, split charge sectors, Poisson resum appropriate integers and identify instanton actions through modified Bessel functions or exponential expansions.

Treat divergent integrals by minimal subtraction and divergent integer sums by ζ-function regularization. In eight dimensions, modular invariance fixes regulator dependence; the paper states that lower-dimensional analytic continuation removes the corresponding ambiguity.

Combine modular covariance of the flavored torus partition function with chemical-potential periodicity to obtain spectral flow. Apply this to the internal identity operator to generate charged states throughout the period lattice.

Use a spherically symmetric electric black-hole solution and a mass functional in a two-derivative effective action. Choosing the auxiliary mass function proportional to a particle mass relates an everywhere-valid self-repulsion inequality to a black-hole mass bound.

Factorize worldsheet correlators and extract exchange forces from normalized three-point functions and propagators. Current Ward identities fix gauge contributions; a Sugawara decomposition separates current and neutral sectors to evaluate scalar couplings.

Estimate PQ breaking from NS5 instantons and gauge-coupling running across SUSY thresholds. Analyze heavy-axion entropy injection using misalignment abundances and instantaneous decay, supplemented by thermal freeze-in/out estimates.

CYTools constructs favorable KS triangulations and cone data. Differential evolution searches the stretched Kähler cone at fixed total volume for acceptable compactifications and maximal effective curve volumes that could suppress MD instantons.

Compute the Kähler kinetic matrix and worldsheet-instanton potential. Approximate the MD mass basis using the h¹¹ leading instantons, integrate out states heavier than 10⁴ m_MI, then diagonalize the remaining matrix including QCD.
Scalar–tensor dualisation introduces an auxiliary curvature variable χ, sets φ=F′(χ), and uses a Weyl transformation and canonical field redefinition to obtain the Einstein-frame scalaron potential.

Superspace construction uses the chiral projector −6P(R̄), whose lowest component contains scalar curvature, together with D/F-density identities. Introducing T, C and X linearises the action; X is eliminated algebraically around C=0.

Dualize the axion to a higher-form field, compute real fixed-integer-flux saddles, and Fourier-sum flux sectors with weight exp(imΔa) to obtain Dirichlet amplitudes, even without a real Dirichlet saddle.
Laplace representations and an ensemble interpretation translate positivity into Stieltjes moment constraints. For connected cumulants, the useful inequality is κ₁κ₃≥κ₂(κ₂−κ₁²).
Use a radial FRW wormhole ansatz and renormalized on-shell actions; extend to axio-dilaton profiles through timelike geodesics in a Lorentzian moduli-space metric.

Siegel modular covariance and stabilizer representations constrain zeros and gradients. The authors vectorize the bipartite transformation law into a Kronecker-product eigenvalue problem, requiring a common invariant vector for every stabilizer generator.

The F-term calculation uses the covariant derivative ∇Mχ=∂Mχ+kχ∂M ln Y and the dilaton/geometric block structure of the Kähler metric. Their Mathematica package SMFs.m supports fixed-point Hessian evaluations and a limited numerical search away from fixed points.

Dimensional reduction relates scalar wormholes to Schwarzschild double cones and charged black holes. String examples use instanton actions, Eisenstein-series R⁴ coefficients, and Poisson-dual Narain lattice representations; modular-integral unfolding separates winding sectors and exposes divergent instanton sums.

Spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar solutions, traced Einstein equations, asymptotic boundary terms, and scaling arguments determine wormhole actions and displacements. AdS actions are renormalized relative to empty AdS; fixed-charge sums motivate the extension of the AdS bound to spherical boundaries.

Diagonal tail moments are evaluated through incomplete Gamma functions. Sector-canonical evolution equations and full diagonal-population simulations, including noncanonical initial mixtures and truncated tails, supply analytical and numerical model evidence.

Imported SEAQT constrained entropy-gradient flow with a positive dissipative metric. The new scalar-temperature calculation differentiates energy–entropy covariance, using the Fréchet derivative of log ρ for noncommuting states.

Motivate bounds using the local horizon condition hT_zz≥0; compare with dimensional reduction to a codimension-one description and with finiteness of the on-shell action. Finite action reproduces the scalar bound but restricts the higher-form region further.

Insert logarithmic scalar and warp-factor profiles into the equations of motion and balance leading powers near the singularity. Separate cases where the potential and form both contribute, or either is subdominant; impose Q²≥0 and the proposed leading-potential condition C_V≤0.

Encode geometric flux by dΥA=N_A^I ΦI, dΦI=M_I^J ΨJ and dΨJ=Q_J^A TA. Nilpotency and integration by parts give NM=0, MQ=0, Q=−Nᵀ and symmetric M. Appendix C uses rank-one inversion to obtain contraction identities for the physical moduli metric.

Expand ten-dimensional fields on internal form bases, reduce overlap integrals and curvature terms, impose democratic RR duality constraints, and dualize eligible three-dimensional vectors or external fluxes. Organize the scalar potential by V=G^{MN}(∂M P)(∂N P)−4P².

Construct scalar potentials from G₂ supersymmetry conditions or the four-dimensional N=1 Kähler potential and superpotential. Canonically normalize fields, diagonalize the Hessian, and expand potential and kinetic terms to cubic order in mass eigenstates.

Build larger finite orbifold groups preserving the lattice, metric, and Maurer–Cartan equations. Their invariant forms determine scalar projections; analyze orientifold conjugacy classes, fixed loci, and a local A₁ blow-up to interpret the altered O-plane geometry.

Compute group homology by Künneth and the Spin-bordism AHSS with E2_(p,q) = Hp(BG; Ωq^Spin(pt)). Separate primes 2 and 3, replace modular groups by p-local cyclic models, and use imported oriented-bordism and ko-homology inputs.

Use a conformal metric on the two-dimensional base, the divisor of a U-duality invariant holomorphic density built from Dedekind eta functions, and Gauss–Bonnet to count puncture contributions to the curvature.

Combine Einstein, dilaton and Bianchi equations into currents required to be globally exact. The imported GKP example uses α = e^(4A) and imaginary self-duality; the Model C calculation instead identifies 2A = ϕ.

Use the stability matrix and its mixed eigendirections to characterize phase-dependent focusing. Determine a critical initial quartic coupling delimiting regular UV-reaching trajectories, with an asymptotic expression at large initial f1.

Use proper-time functional RG with an integer regulator parameter m > 2 in four dimensions, locate an interacting fixed point and follow trajectories toward it. Prior full-function scaling solutions motivate the local parametrization, as summarized by this paper.

Apply a Jordan-frame weak-field, static scalar-tensor reduction to map RG initial data into Yukawa parameters. Compare the result with published 95% confidence exclusion envelopes, without reanalyzing experimental datasets or combining their likelihoods.

The appendix uses continuous least squares to fit A sech(√2 x) to an exponential over x ∈ [0.3, 0.7], optimizing A through vanishing derivative of the integrated squared error and reporting RMSE inside and beyond that interval.

The review reports imported cosmological likelihood analyses using CAMB with COBAYA MCMC for DESI constraints, and CLASS with COBAYA for fading-dark-sector fits. Dataset combinations and model choices determine the quoted statistical preferences.

For finite-distance limits, use a different normalized system, monotonicity of the axionic variable, Barbalat's lemma and asymptotic integration. Trajectory length is then assessed through an integral weighted by √G(s).

Review an asymptotic-Hodge-theory classification: boundary mixed Hodge structures determine asymptotic periods, which reconstruct Kähler potentials, superpotentials and flux potentials. This classification is attributed to earlier work, not newly established in these proceedings.

Rewrite the infinite-distance background equations as autonomous systems using normalized saxion and axion velocities and a/s. Introduce kinetic fraction S and variable T; the stated Lyapunov function L = (T − Tλ)² supports the asymptotic reduction.

Dimensional reduction relates gauge couplings and the Planck scale to compactification radii. Bundle topology, Green–Schwarz couplings and quiver charge assignments are used to assess tadpoles, abelian symmetries and proton-decay selection rules.

Proposed one-loop Schwinger representations are evaluated using Gaussian momentum integration, UV regularization, Poisson resummation and modified Bessel functions. A comparison uses the N=1 supergravity F-term potential with trial Kähler and superpotentials.
Use covariant tangent/normal turn geometry, two-field perturbation transfer matrices, a Cauchy–Schwarz bounce shape factor, and comparison of the entropy mode equation with Bessel form.
Reexpress canonical scalar speed as distance per growth of the comoving Hubble scale; combine this with shear-to-scalar density scaling to obtain separate smoothing and BKL suppression requirements.

Sugawara decomposition separates the current algebra from a residual sector. Explicit heterotic state counting and character decompositions detect holomorphic currents; elliptic-genus character decompositions supply evidence for extensions in rational hyperplane-string models.

Simple-current fusion, monodromy charges and modular S-matrix identities constrain CFT multiplicities. The monodromy charge is Q(J)i = hJ + hi − hJ(i) mod 1; for center-associated KM currents it equals the representation's center charge.

Fisher forecasts use parameters (log10 M, f_PBH, sigma, p), numerical five-point derivatives, analytical detector-noise fits, and inverse-Fisher covariance; the paper reports 10^4 Monte Carlo samples.

Greybody-weighted Hawking emission supplies coupled mass and angular-momentum evolution coefficients. An implicit mass–normalized-spin relation is numerically inverted to describe spin-down before a nonrotating evaporation phase.

Gaussian Press–Schechter collapse estimates use beta(M)=erfc[delta_c/(sqrt(2) sigma(M))]/2. The associated SIGW spectrum is computed using a radiation-era double convolution of the primordial curvature spectrum, then redshifted with today's radiation density.

Pair production is expressed through a multimode squeezing operator exp[½ΣIJ GIJ a†I a†J − h.c.]. With sufficiently long interaction time, the GR amplitude is summarized as GIJ ≈ −2iκ²Nb FIJ T, using a mode correlation function computed in earlier work.

The calculation summarized in the essay expands gμν = ημν + κhμν in transverse-traceless gauge, canonically quantizes weak gravitons, and retains terms through quadratic order in h. Linear coupling to the axion stress tensor produces coherent radiation; quadratic interactions produce correlated pairs.

Topology is analyzed using relative integral homology, Lefschetz duality, the universal coefficient theorem, and the Leray–Serre spectral sequence with monodromy-twisted coefficients. Smith normal form computes the fiber coinvariants.

Geometric estimates combine Weierstrass discriminant divisors, a Calabi–Yau condition, and a Euclidean bubble-of-nothing action with a Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term. Gauss–Bonnet and estimated axio-dilaton image areas supply genus and monodromy scaling.

Finite lattice-symmetry classification and Mathematica subgroup/orbit enumeration implement the searches. In 6d, pure-spinor stabilizers are tested for singlets in the linearized (5,5) moduli representation.

Search stabilizers of symmetric points in the original moduli space for subgroups having no invariant tangent vector, fixing a nonzero phase shift, and satisfying the geometric-orbit quadratic equations; then transform the shift into a geometric frame.

The orbit argument uses minuscule highest-weight representations, Chevalley integral models, a projective G/P embedding, and integral quadratic generators whose reduction characterizes the mod-2 orbit.

The authors replace R̃² by 2φ²R̃−φ⁴, use the scalar relation R̃=φ², and vary the action with respect to metric and Weyl vector. Generalized Friedmann equations are combined to derive an energy-balance equation.

Dimensionless background ODEs are integrated numerically with Friedmann/vector constraints on initial data. Parameters are scanned while κ is adjusted to normalize the scalar spectrum; standard warm-inflation expressions supply ns and r.
The embeddability proof restricts rational coordinate denominators using integral pairings, then constructs even or odd unimodular lattices in cases distinguished by k modulo 4, where nV=12k+8.

A Mathematica search is supplemented by representation-theoretic variables Qi and Δi. Positivity/divisibility conditions prune individual factors; mixed anomalies and realization by actual product representations then eliminate most remaining branches.
Cancel irreducible gravitational and gauge quartics, factorize I8 as ½ΩαβY4αY4β, and solve the resulting pairings of anomaly vectors. For one tensor, the anomaly matrix has rank at most two.

Heegaard handlebody fillings produce bouquets of monodromy defects. A proposed junction-free link must satisfy each defect’s ordered-crossing closure condition [d_n⋯d_1,x]=1 and the ordered product conditions reproducing every filled handle’s monodromy.

Hopf’s imported formula H2(BG;Z)≅(R∩[F,F])/[R,F], for G=F/R, translates relation words expressed as products of commutators into surface representatives. Bundle consistency requires the product of the handle commutators to equal 1 in G.

The low-degree Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence gives 0→H1(BG;Ω1ξ(pt))→reduced Ω2ξ(BG)→H2(BG;Z)→0. Oriented two-bordism is determined by H2; Spin bordism permits an extension by H1(BG;Z2), besides the purely gravitational summand.

Regularized singular theta lifts of Narain lattice sums yield Borcherds products. Atkin–Lehner transformations relate cusps and determine constant terms from principal parts; genus-zero cases also admit explicit Hauptmodul and eta-product ansätze.

Cancel the composite U(1) anomaly with moduli-dependent gravitational counterterms, then constrain their meromorphic functions by interior massless-vector singularities and cusp asymptotics matching ten-dimensional effective couplings.

Character-valued asymmetric-orbifold partition functions with Spin(8) fugacities compute one-loop gravitational thresholds and abelian F4 and F2R2 couplings. Supersymmetry Ward identities constrain the gauge-field couplings.

Reviews the formal vacuum-projector construction P0 = limβ→∞ exp[−β(H−E0)] and rank-one operators XnP0Xm†. It then tests sector-preserving observables using their commutators with central multiplication operators Zf.

Uses a finite-dimensional Bell-pair diagnostic: pull sectorwise physical states back to a common auxiliary code space, average over α, and compare with one Bell state defined by a sector-independent unitary V. A unitary one-design supplies a limiting depolarization example.

Decomposes the charge-space identity into irreducible-representation projectors in each fusion channel. Fixed-t contour dispersion relations then relate the graviton pole to weighted sums of massive s- and u-channel residues; missing representations are excluded by contradiction.

Constructs an auxiliary odd-residue sum using an imaginary-axis integral of the crossing-odd amplitude after subtracting its linear term. For democracy, replaces high-energy pole towers by Regge discontinuities and compares energy-averaged residues with the identity tensor.

Spherical reduction uses the dilaton X=r² and a Weyl transformation removing its kinetic term. A Polyakov action for conformal matter supplies anomaly backreaction; conservation of the stationary Killing current and two-horizon chiral regularity determine the flux.

Combines horizon first laws with a horizon-local Schwinger current to obtain an adiabatic dynamical system for (M,Q). Root factorization proves the neutral surface-gravity ordering; phase-space analysis distinguishes heat-flux nullclines from invariant trajectories.

Uses a conservative island estimate Sfine=min{Sno-island,Sisland}, with Sisland approximately πrb²/G4+O(Neff). The proposed Page estimate is the branch-crossing condition on the dynamically evolving background.

Numerical integration of an autonomous background system tracks radiation, matter and scalar evolution, with the Friedmann constraint eliminating the matter density variable. The authors explicitly do not perform a new fixed-point stability analysis.

Bayesian inference uses P(θ|D,sw)∝L(D|θ)π(θ)πsw(θ). Uniform-prior COBAYA MCMC chains require Gelman–Rubin R−1<0.01 and are analyzed with GetDist; V0 is tuned at each sampling step to satisfy the density budget.
Best fits use the MINIMIZE sampler. Model comparisons report Δχ² relative to non-flat ΛCDM and AIC=−2 ln Lmax+2k, where k here counts free parameters.

A complementary method bounds logarithmic action gradients using canonically normalized volume and dilaton components: ||α||² ≥ αρ² + αφ². Additional shape-modulus contributions can strengthen the bound.

For homogeneous Kähler potentials, the authors establish positivity of a modified Hessian h through κ = h + ξ, then contract with charge-related vectors to obtain instanton and magnetic-string inequalities.
