The imported geometric-WGC approach transfers higher-form particle/string WGC bounds into cycle-volume inequalities, then translates those inequalities into instanton bounds by compactifying another string theory on the same manifold.

Leading large-volume canonical normalization is followed by rotation into volume and transverse coordinates, mass-matrix diagonalization, and extraction of modulus–gauge-boson couplings. Thermalization is assessed by comparing scattering, decay and inverse-decay rates with H.

Stationary points are approximated using Lambert W functions and numerical minimization. Reality of the branches constrains uplift and temperature; finite-temperature extrema are obtained by re-stabilizing the coupled potential.

The thermal potential retains two-loop gauge and modulus interactions. A volume-direction Hawking–Moss analysis estimates the critical regime and tunneling exponent; transverse thermal transitions are discussed without a full multi-field bounce calculation.

Interpret the horizon constraint f(r+,Q,φ)=0 as an alternative equation of state, replacing the usual thermodynamic variables (P,T,V) by (φ,Q,r+). The scalar-dependent effective pressure is P=−3V(φ)/(8π).

Use dG=−S dT+Φ dQ+V dP, with Φ=Q/r+, and the generalized isothermal Clausius–Clapeyron condition dGℓ−dGs=0. An imposed phase-radius identification reduces the resulting differential equation for Q(φ).

Classify E8×E8 shifts using Kac’s algorithm and extended Dynkin diagrams. For Spin(32)/Z2, separate integral and half-integral 4w classes. Equivalence uses gauge-lattice translations and Weyl transformations stabilizing the fixed v.

Construct the one-loop partition function from g^c h^k-twisted traces with insertions g^d h^l. Mixed-sector phases enforce modular covariance; the 64 terms organize into eight modular orbits, one of which vanishes.

Analyze sector-dependent mass formulas, solve level matching, branch SO(8) representations to the six-dimensional little group, and impose projection phases to obtain surviving states and multiplicities.

Specify the sampling measure explicitly: ambient Fubini–Study random-line sampling supplies a known integration measure. Adaptive quadrature varies auxiliary Hermitian data or sampling regions to populate undersampled, often high-curvature regions.

The proposed correction pipeline linearizes corrected field equations around numerical metric/bundle seeds and solves sourced elliptic equations order by order. Gauge fixing, zero-mode subtraction and corrections to the B-field and dilaton are part of the unfinished numerical program.

Use metric-dependent Hodge theory, coupled harmonic representatives, overlap integrals and Laplace/Dirac spectra. Green operators enter higher-order effective couplings, while spectral determinants enter threshold corrections.

Horizon regularity and scaling transformations reduce the regular finite-horizon branch to a canonical initial-value problem. A numerical canonical solution is fitted at large distance to the analytic zero-Casimir family.

The one-loop Casimir term is obtained from fluctuation determinants with twisted Kaluza–Klein modes, dimensional regularization and Bessel-function sums. The radius-independent divergent contribution is removed with a cosmological-constant counterterm.

Weyl transformation and scalar redefinitions reduce the higher-dimensional equations to radial Einstein–scalar equations. Without Casimir energy, first integrals for AR′ and A′R yield power-law metric functions and logarithmic scalar profiles.

For irreps, use Weyl orbits, connected subsets of λ-extended Dynkin diagrams and fundamental-weight Gram matrices to calculate face distances. Match these to ESC rates, classify spherical polytopes through simplex/orthoplex facets, then identify Lie-algebra and representation realizations.

The imported framework uses rational parabolic subgroups to organize boundary geodesics and superrigidity to extend charge representations from Γ to G. With the spectral assumptions, the leading rate is the support function α(H) = max_w ⟨w,H⟩ of the weight hull.

Combine BPS no-force identities with bounds on string–string and string–particle gradient products; analyse homogeneous polynomial and metric-essential-instanton cases separately. Apply Laplacian and Ricci-operator identities to string tensions.

Use the imported nilpotent-orbit description of periods near unipotent-monodromy singularities, separating polynomial periods from exponential corrections. Polynomial periods determine the approximate shift-symmetric Kähler potential.

Locality uses the spacelike branch symmetry of g, invisible zero-charge insertions, contour backtracking, and an algebraic ideal identity. Potential exchange differences require a forward timelike chain between spacelike endpoints and therefore vanish.

Analytic continuation separates free and Coulomb factors, partitions screening times into ordered sectors, and reparametrizes them on time-independent domains. Smearing estimates use light-cone distance majorants and affine-arrangement power counting.

Finite-torus construction uses a spectral ultraviolet cutoff, a Gaussian zero-mode regulator, and imported wrong-sign Gaussian technology replacing coefficients by i times ordinary Gaussian coefficients. The zero-mode limit selects exactly w screening insertions.

Construct conserved off-shell graviton and photon currents from heavy charged-scalar worldlines glued to bulk connected trees, then Fourier transform to obtain classical fields. Classical terms use no contractions between worldline emission vertices; scaleless integrals vanish in dimensional regularisation.

Determine entropy by integrating the first law using surface gravity and horizon electric potential, and separately evaluate Iyer–Wald entropy. Estimate shadows from the corrected metric's photon sphere.

Solve modified Einstein–Maxwell equations perturbatively in the higher-derivative couplings using ds²=−N²f dt²+dr²/f+r²dΩ². Impose asymptotic boundary conditions fixing mass and charge, then transform to de Donder coordinates to compare with the worldline expansion.

The gravitational Cardy limit combines a large horizon radius with coordinate rescalings. A consistent Sasaki–Einstein truncation retains the NSNS and RR two-forms absent from minimal gauged supergravity.
The field-theory review uses circle reduction to a three-dimensional supersymmetric EFT and an elliptically extended holonomy matrix model, with complex holonomies on a torus.

Reduction of the two-form sector on D2 gives a three-dimensional model. Canonical quantization and energy minimization with kinetic terms are compared with ground-state counting in the one-derivative BF sector.

Count multiplicative KK towers using Λsp=MP/√N, represent the two radius sectors by an effective tower, and impose MSUSY≤Λsp. The resulting upper bound on n is combined with coupling-dependent perturbative inequalities.

Use single-modulus scaling and homogeneity of the volume: degree 3/2 in IIB four-cycle moduli and degree 3 in IIA two-cycle moduli. Substitute V∼Vp^α into the logarithmic Kähler-potential terms, then compare asymptotic KK and gravitino mass powers.

Compute oscillations in PISA using a 12-layer PREM Earth density profile. Forward-fold collaboration MC events, reweighting atmospheric fluxes, cross sections, oscillations, and detector response to predict reconstructed distributions.

Scan one texture's potential at a time, profiling nuisance parameters through Δχ²mod=χ²mod(V fixed)−χ²mod(V free). Extract 90% limits using one degree of freedom. Expected-profile bands and goodness-of-fit distributions use 500 statistically fluctuated pseudo-experiments.

Fit ten reconstructed-energy bins and ten zenith bins over cosθreco∈[−1,0.1], with two PID categories: mixed [0.55,0.75] and track-like [0.75,1]. Use a frequentist modified χ² including finite-MC statistical uncertainty and Gaussian nuisance penalties where priors are available.

Choose radial gauges adapted to analytic integration, using Appell or Gauss hypergeometric functions and a separate error-function solution at D=3. For generic axion-free potential slopes, integrate the second-order equations numerically in conformal gauge B=A.

Reduce the field equations to a one-dimensional effective Lagrangian with a Hamiltonian constraint, then express the dynamics as autonomous first-order equations. Constant state variables give algebraic fixed-point equations; Jacobian eigenvalues describe radial perturbations.

Use Hamiltonian-constrained shooting for massive IIA and compare numerical endpoint profiles with D8/O8 scaling. Independently solve local Taylor expansions through sixth order for IIB AdS9 and massive IIA dS9, tracking residual radial-coordinate freedom.

Continue to Euclidean time, evaluate bulk and Gibbons–Hawking–York terms, and analyze the holographic central-charge integral by continuity and endpoint behavior. The finiteness argument uses boundedness on a closed interval rather than a closed-form integral.

Integrate the IIB axion equation to χ′=Qe^(−9f+h); choose h=9f to make χ′ constant, use the Hamiltonian constraint to decouple the remaining equations, and subsequently introduce an angular radial coordinate for the explicit solution.

Expand the thermal partition function around the free theory: ΔF=T⟨ΔS⟩₀+… . Wick-contract one four-point interaction into a two-loop vacuum diagram, discard analytic terms that cancel propagator denominators, and identify the remaining vertex with the forward on-shell amplitude.

Convert thermal loop integrals to Bose-weighted on-shell phase-space integrals. Expand the crossing-even forward amplitude in s, evaluate positive phase-space moments, and transfer dispersive coefficient bounds to temperature-expansion coefficients.
Use Mellin–Poisson summation for hyperbolic multiplicative-lattice kernels, Fourier/Poisson summation for parabolic Gaussian additive-lattice kernels, and Jacobi–Anger expansion for elliptic blocks.

Classify candidate flop reflections using configuration-row patterns and integral u-vectors; certify diffeomorphism by matching triple intersections and c2 under the divisor-lattice identification, invoking Wall’s theorem where required.

Construct invariant bilinear forms, complex quotient geometries and Laplace–Beltrami operators; separate variables and impose kernel regularity or asymptotic conditions to select the relevant Bessel solutions.

Worldsheet CFT junctions in the RNS framework; one-loop integration of massive superfields using heat-kernel/Seeley–deWitt expansions and partial resummation to extract kinetic corrections and induced dilaton gradients.

The emergence prescription evaluates D0-brane one-loop Schwinger integrals with minimal subtraction and zeta regularization. Corrected proper lengths estimate winding contributions and Euclidean D0-instanton actions.

Reduced complex K-theory, the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence and Mayer–Vietoris analyze charges. Discretized graph Laplacians provide complementary spectral evidence. TMF and Witten genera test deformation obstructions after viewing the models as (0,1) theories.

Small Gram matrices are separated into Hodge blocks by exact searches over integral unimodular transformations. SageMath's Fincke–Pohst implementation enumerates short vectors; the paper describes these enumerations as exact within the constructed lattices.

Griffiths residues and Movasati's Fermat period formulas give a Hodge-compatible basis. Gamma-function normalization is separated from the cyclotomic matrix over Q(ζ_d), which carries the arithmetic constraints used in reconstruction.

Expand cyclotomic periods in a rational field basis, solve ΨX=P using the vanishing-cycle intersection matrix, impose the non-(2,2) period kernel, and saturate the rational subspace in integral homology using Hermite/Smith normal forms. Restricting Ψ gives the lattice Gram matrix.

Use fermionic normal coordinates Y A=(0,θα) to expand χ,fA and g covariantly. Successive Grassmann-odd derivatives are obtained recursively from the current constraints and background torsion, curvature, flux and dilaton data.

Apply BRST transformations and worldsheet equations of motion to a covariant current ansatz. Superspace Bianchi identities and the pure-spinor constraint are used to reduce the resulting conditions to a conservative independent set.
Gamma-matrix identities determine the scalar and two-form decomposition of the ghost coefficient gαβ, rather than assuming that decomposition at the outset.

Backward survival equations, Feynman–Kac killing weights and finite-horizon Doob transforms. For autonomous inputs, ∂τh=(L−κ)h, with absorbing boundary data and h(ϕ,0)=1 inside. Explicit time dependence or moving domains require H(ϕ,N;Nf); substituting an arbitrary state-dependent horizon into h does not automatically define consistent conditioned dynamics.

Image-method heat kernel for the normal half-line benchmark. The killed Ornstein–Uhlenbeck simulation uses exact finite-step endpoints and an approximate short-step Brownian-bridge crossing correction. An implicit finite-difference backward solve uses a far-interior Neumann condition for the long-horizon numerical test.

Covariant phase-space reduction fixes δΞ=0 and removes a phase-space-exact gravitational contribution to the presymplectic potential. Pullback to right null infinity retains the right-moving scalar symplectic form after treating chiral endpoint terms.

Algebra-completeness arguments use positive-energy analyticity, an edge-of-the-wedge density argument and a vacuum projector, or charge-generated translations with isotony, additivity and von Neumann closure. The one-sided projector argument is explicitly rejected as insufficient.

Four-dimensional on-shell super Ward identities reduce selected amplitudes. Contour dispersion relations express EFT coefficients as positive heavy averages; crossing supplies null constraints. Improved gravitational sum rules are smeared with wavepackets to handle the forward pole.

Convex spectral constraints are implemented with SDPB using finite wavepacket/null-constraint sets and mass/spin sampling. Extremal spectra are cleaned by imposing spin-dependent lower mass bounds that leave the optimized bound unchanged, without imposing upper mass bounds.

The authors project known N=2 instanton corrections into an N=1 orientifold description, analyze instanton zero modes, and estimate Kähler- versus superpotential-induced potentials. One-loop gauge running with intermediate incomplete multiplets tests large-threshold scenarios.

Dimensional reduction of the 7-brane Chern–Simons action determines universal and flux-induced nonuniversal axion couplings. Holomorphy relates these couplings to threshold corrections in the gauge kinetic functions.

Effectiveness arguments use Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch, Serre duality, positivity and vanishing theorems. Worldsheet anomaly inflow supplies central charges; Cardy entropy motivates, but alone does not establish, the needed effectiveness inequalities.

Example calculations determine divisor occupancy through h0(X,O_X(D)) and particle occupancy through nonzero genus-zero Gopakumar–Vafa invariants. The latter are extracted using Picard–Fuchs periods, mirror maps and coefficient matching of prepotentials.

Supersymmetry projectors define compatible sectors. First-order attractor flows and extremization of electric or magnetic central charges on constant-volume moduli slices identify regular black-brane charge regions.

Integrate over S², eliminate the classical Maxwell field with the fixed-charge boundary term, and Weyl-transform to remove the dilaton kinetic term. The resulting nonlinear potential retains curvature, cosmological-constant and electric-field contributions.

Expand Maxwell fields in scalar and vector spherical harmonics; introduce Stückelberg fields and Faddeev–Popov ghosts. With gauge parameters ξ=1, evaluate Gaussian determinants using a small-proper-time heat-kernel expansion and zeta-regularize the infinite KK sums.

Solve general-potential dilaton gravity using a prepotential W′=V. Compute the Euclidean saddle action with a √W boundary counterterm, then compare equal-temperature free energies using a signed-area criterion and examine heat-capacity signs.

A separate leading-operator estimate sets |c_D|=c⋆=0.1 without a coefficient probability distribution. Writing r=f_a/(√2 M_Pl), the QCD requirement is 2k c⋆ M_Pl⁴ r^D<θ_max χ_QCD; the ALP requirement is 2k² c⋆ M_Pl⁴ r^D/f_a²<m_a². These give logarithmic dimension bounds under the stated assumptions.

Unknown complex Wilson coefficients are marginalized statistically. For QCD axions, the Bayes factor compares the probability of satisfying |θ_eff|<10^−10 against an SM-like input-angle model. For ALPs, an input-mass comparison uses the Barbieri–Giudice sensitivity at fixed coefficients and averages its inverse over coefficients.

ALP fine-tuning maps on the (m_a,1/f_a) plane average 100,000 Monte Carlo realizations of Wilson coefficients. Separate maps assume the first unsuppressed operators occur at D=5 or D=10; another map finds the protection dimension needed to keep the ALP tuning penalty below 100.

Flux backtracking switches off f7 and f31,f32,f33, solves flat-sliced three-dimensional domain-wall BPS equations obtained by completing squares, and uplifts using explicit metric and dilaton formulae.

Direct ten-dimensional construction uses harmonic superposition, radial H-functions, and integration of the KK5 relations at constant metric flux. The authors report checking the resulting equations of motion and Bianchi identities with source contributions.

Stochastic coarse graining uses kσ=σaH with σ≪1 and a step window. Langevin equations yield approximately white field noise of variance (H/2πϕ)² per e-fold; a Fokker–Planck treatment gives accumulated phase variance and Gaussian tail estimates for crossing θ=π.

Numerical background evolution is combined with a spatially flat ADM perturbation expansion. Lapse and shift constraints are eliminated to obtain ALP mode equations; Appendix A additionally includes radial fluctuations and their mixing with the phase.

The GW extension models a lognormal wall mass window, adjustable abundance and nonsphericity, emission efficiency proportional to e² times a collapse factor, and a broken-power-law spectrum with causal f³ low-frequency behaviour.

Lift the ordinary ’t Hooft–Polyakov monopole to a five-dimensional string, then match its nonabelian core, local abelian Coulomb region and compactified global-string tail. The imported BPS solution gives TM=4πmW/g5,2²; away from BPS an order-one function B(mρ/mW), with B(0)=1, modifies this tension.

Use the massive-fermion parity anomaly and anomaly inflow to obtain the mixed Chern–Simons coupling. On the orbifold, analyze the projected KK determinant with Pauli–Villars regularization to include boundary-condition contributions to its phase.
Apply imported exponential-potential scaling results: ȧ=4FH, Vexp=4F²H² and Ωa=4(F/MPl)². Imported superhorizon perturbation decay on the attractor supplies a suppression factor √(T2/T1).

Estimate QCD departure by comparing potential slopes, capture by comparing velocity with QCD barriers, and abundance through entropy conservation. Estimate vacuum decay using a thin-wall Euclidean bounce and σ≈8mafa².

Relate worldsheet fermion anomalies to three-dimensional reduced eta invariants through Dai–Freed/APS methods. Subtract pure target and pure chiral-Z2 contributions, evaluate a line-bundle generator on RP³, and extend to real vector bundles using characteristic classes and the splitting principle.

Use the Smith isomorphism to identify the mixed degree-three spin bordism group with reduced degree-two pin− bordism of X. Compute its low-degree AHSS and resolve the extension using Z4-valued quadratic refinements on pin− surfaces.

Hierarchical supergravity-potential minimisation: α′³ corrections to K and del Pezzo non-perturbative terms fix the overall volume; canonical normalisation identifies the remaining saxionic direction; winding-string loops and higher-derivative F⁴ terms subsequently lift it.

Toric hypersurface geometry and stable degeneration of the parameterised family construct Tyurin limits. Period integrals over fibred 3-cycles and gluing of asymptotically cylindrical CY pieces support the geometric stretching interpretation.

A sourced continuity equation estimates the KK relic density during radiation domination. Averaged scalar oscillations determine the expansion history, while partial decay-width estimates compare inflaton reheating of brane matter with bulk-graviton production.

Dimensional reduction and Weyl transformation relate 5D, 4D Einstein and brane/Jordan frames. Scalar and tensor spectra include the inflaton KK tower; their amplitudes and transition scale are combined with the causal-horizon condition.

The localized-source calculation Fourier sine transforms linearized bulk metric perturbations, uses modified Bessel solutions, and combines junction matching and interior regularity with mixed boundary conditions containing boundary Hilbert and cosmological terms.

Israel junction conditions and the projected Gauss–Codazzi equations determine effective four-dimensional gravity. Cosmological evolution also uses full junction conditions with brane radiation and exterior AdS–Schwarzschild backreaction.

Fixed points are characterized by stability-matrix eigenanalysis; functional f(R) studies also use Sturm–Liouville analysis. Complementary methods include the epsilon expansion near two dimensions, perturbative and large-N calculations, dynamical-triangulation simulations, and tensor-model pregeometric RG.

Functional RG calculations use the Wetterich equation with truncations organized through curvature invariants, functional f(R) ansätze, graviton vertices, or form factors. Vertex and form-factor approaches retain physical momentum dependence, including in the physical limit k → 0.

Numerically select Kreuzer–Skarke reflexive polytopes and random triangulations with CYTools. Evaluate four proxy ratios at the approximate stretched-cone tip and near selected facets, maximizing over generating charge sets of toric Mori and effective cones.

Classify BPS instanton and axion-string charge subspaces by their asymptotic norms and actions near boundary types; extract exponents defined by ρ² ∼ L^α. The paper imports scaling results from an analogous M-theory analysis after accounting for the overall rescaling.

Use the triangular decomposition κ = UDUᵀ and sequential integration of fields under a hierarchical potential to motivate effective decay constants from D. The discussion uses det κ = det D and tr D ≤ tr κ to constrain effects of kinetic mixing.
For X=aχ, evolve modes with ωk²=k²+a²mχ²−(1−6ξ)a″/a from subhorizon Bunch–Davies initial conditions. Extract Bogoliubov occupations after adiabatic convergence and integrate a³nk=k³|βk|²/(2π²).

Convert the integrated comoving spectrum into today's abundance using reheating dilution. For the nearly flat light/minimal IR plateau, impose the authors' observable cutoff k0=a0H0; its contribution is approximately C N0 with N0 around 55.

Numerically evolve covariant background equations and the coupled adiabatic/entropic perturbations; extract scalar and tensor observables after superhorizon evolution rather than applying single-field slow-roll predictions to turning trajectories.

Use the mechanical form Ṙb²=cos²ψb−F(Rb) and asymptotic mass behavior for closed boundedness. Analyze Bardeen turning points and expansion duration using x=Rb/g and the first-order scale-factor equation.
Test affine completeness through radial null lengths Δλ∝∫A(τ)dτ. The explicit flat de Sitter-like past and open A∼τ−τ0 endpoint both have finite past affine length despite curvature regularity.

Apply both Darmois extrinsic-curvature conditions and induced-metric continuity. The angular condition gives Ṙb²+F(Rb)=β²; with m(R)=R[1−F(R)]/2 this becomes a Friedmann equation determined by the parent Misner–Sharp mass.

Evaluate the scalar-density tadpole and perturb the 6×6 neutrino mass matrix to first order. Appendix B separately evaluates finite-density exchange self-energy, whose ultralight limit lacks the tadpole's inverse-scalar-mass-squared enhancement.

Point-source spectra use an unbroken source power law from 100 GeV, topology-dependent effective areas, and Gaussian migration widths σlog10E=0.30 for tracks and 0.15 for cascades. Poisson deviances profile each source's normalization and index before summing sources.

Average diffuse fluxes over source evolution and emitted energy, then normalize active flavor fractions. Spectral predictions fold flavor-dependent fluxes through effective areas and approximate energy smearing; SPL/BPL nuisance parameters are profiled using reconstructed binned likelihoods.

Constructs electric and axion-shift defects using integral right-coprime factorizations of rational coupling matrices, worldvolume topological theories, and half higher gauging. Smith and Smith–McMillan forms provide an explicit factorization algorithm; allowed factorizations differ by unimodular transformations.

Uses anomaly inflow to constrain string and monopole sectors, axion/two-form duality to relate fixed-charge and imaginary-Dirichlet wormholes, and fermionic zero-mode profiles and long-distance bilocal couplings to infer possible D-term or superpotential corrections.

Uses regulated Gauss-law field energy, a gauge-invariant higher-form Stückelberg ansatz, flux-induced Wess–Zumino charge, DBI shell tension, and a spherical thin-wall Euclidean bounce estimate to separate endpoint possibilities and conditional discharge energetics.

Varies the tachyon action and expands around a Q-symmetric flux background, separating branch-even and branch-odd perturbations. Stress-tensor cancellation tests whether the odd subsystem sources metric or dilaton at first order.

Evaluating the sourced homogeneous scalar equation today gives the signed relation MPl V′/V ≈ (Ωb,0 βm + Ωc,0 βc − x − y/3)/ΩDE,0. The paper constructs conservative absolute Gaussian envelopes and proposes a joint local likelihood sampled in (d,x), followed by a map to potential diagnostics.

Conformal transformation and local canonical normalization establish the field coordinate used for swampland diagnostics. A linear Damour–Donoghue dilaton basis, QCD-subtracted mass couplings and nuclear charges map one microscopic vector d to material charges, visible coupling βm, clock sensitivities and Planck-mass running.

Separate the charged Klein–Gordon equation into temporal, radial, and spherical-harmonic factors; scale r=r_++ερ and t=τ/ε; use Whittaker solutions and gamma-function coefficients to identify the retarded response B/A and pole condition 1/2+μ−κ=−n.

The authors report symbolic reconstruction of closed forms, zero simplification residuals, and numerical evaluation grids agreeing with analytic expressions to approximately 10^−12. These are reported checks of formulas, not independent verification in this record.
Expand 3d N=1 superspace two- and three-point functions and project onto normalized bottom and top conformal primaries to derive relations among component OPE coefficients.

Use intermediate bases adapted to the Kähler geometry. In Model V, package six Kähler moduli into a symmetric matrix with volume det M; a Cholesky decomposition of the positive-definite vacuum matrix removes flux dependence from kinetic normalization, leaving a flux-independent orthogonal mass diagonalization.

Solve supersymmetric F-term equations, canonically normalize the vacuum kinetic metric, and diagonalize the axion and saxion Hessians. Explicit mass eigenvectors are required: cubic interactions are transformed using three copies of the field map, with derivative couplings obtained from the metric and potential couplings from third derivatives of V.

Represent red and green/blue curves by F(Z,X̃)=0 and G(Z,X)=0, with selector XX̃=0. If F(Z,0)=G(Z,0), use H=F+G−F(Z,0) and superpotential W=ΛH+Λ̃XX̃. The compatibility condition makes the two curve systems share their junction endpoints.

For efficient descriptions of selected graphs, replace the selector by fn(X)X̃=0. Distinct roots Xi provide multiple X-sheets. Their graph criterion organizes red edges into n-tuples and factorizes the red matching as P=Q⊗Q′, with Q′r1r2=1 precisely when r1+r2=n−1.

Encode a compact graph by an ordered red perfect matching and closed alternating green/blue paths. Each path records a cyclic ordered list of red-edge labels, alternates black and white vertices, and uses every encountered vertex exactly once across the collection of paths.

Apply imported Doplicher–Roberts reconstruction to the baby universe category: existence and uniqueness of fiber functors produce the QFT, while representation-category reconstruction identifies its symmetry and invariant states.

Linearize bordisms, represent them on two-boundary universal Hilbert spaces, take a double commutant, then complete at the object level by sums and subobjects. The trace inequality yields atomic type-I endomorphism algebras; multi-boundary spaces supply the fusion structure.
The universal construction uses reflection positivity in an OS/GNS construction to obtain Hilbert spaces of manifold-prepared states. Its resulting unitary functor need not be symmetric monoidal.

A factorized hybrid prescription uses Pauli–Villars regularization for single-mode diagrams and a proper-time cutoff for the tower. Propagators are combined with Feynman parameters before imposing the proper-time cutoff; the auxiliary momentum regulator is distinct from the provisional physical cutoff.

Poisson resummation and Mellin-transform contour analysis extract the tower asymptotics. Appendix G uses fixed-order Euler–Maclaurin summation, a Gaussian saddle and a relative remainder estimate for the simplified string spectrum.

Scalar heat-kernel and derivative expansions provide a comparison with the diagrammatic prescription. The paper reports agreement for scalars; fermions are treated diagrammatically because a radion-dependent Dirac mass complicates naive operator doubling through a possible multiplicative anomaly.

Posterior inference uses a conditional normalizing flow implemented with normflows in a 13/14-dimensional parameter space. Invertible mappings connect a standard normal distribution to model parameters, conditioned on training data and model observables; the authors describe posterior sampling through a single forward pass after training.

The background calculation couples scalar evolution to the dark-matter continuity equation and integrates the latter. For AdS-EDE the present field value must be obtained dynamically. Synchronous-gauge perturbation equations are attributed to an earlier derivation rather than reproduced here.

Mean-field minimization of U_eff(f)=U(f)−λf classifies possible phase structures. Appendix A introduces sources of finite support to argue that correlation functions inherit the same dominant α-critical point.

The one-dimensional ensemble toy integral is analyzed by stationary phase at nondegenerate saddles and integration by parts at derivative discontinuities or endpoints. The displayed contributions scale as V^−1/2 for a simple saddle and V^−1 for a first-derivative discontinuity.

Construct free thermal partition functions from single-letter contributions using a plethystic exponential, then project onto gauge singlets by Haar integration. Weyl characters become power sums; in the stable N→∞ limit these are independent variables and the matrix integral becomes Gaussian.

Unfold mixed classical quivers by converting complex variables to real ones; symmetric/antisymmetric matter produces related graph-doubling identities. Apply the imported Cartan spectral sine formula to thermal determinants, and Rayleigh-quotient bounds to hyper/vector multiplicity ratios and distance rates.

Hanany–Witten brane engineering, orientifold/orbifold projections, flavor-brane additions, brane rotations and 'glued' NS5-branes; elliptic interpolating models permit T-duality to D3-branes probing singularities. Partial ungauging relates interacting SCFT sectors.

Use the imported fake-superpotential formalism: kN M² + Gij-inverse ∂iM ∂jM = Q² generates quasiextremal gradient flows with ADM mass M evaluated at the asymptotic moduli. Different attractors can have overlapping basins.

Implement Π_Q by integrating e^[iμ(Q̂−Q)] over μ ∈ [0,2π]. The bulk implementation uses a Wilson-line defect around the BTZ horizon, producing Φ(t_E+β)=e^(−iμq)Φ(t_E) and Matsubara frequencies ω_n=(2π/β)(n+μq/2π).

Use leading large-N factorization to isolate the channel pairing operators across imaginary time. Perform the charge-projection integral with a spectral-flow sum μ→μ+2π, required for integer-charge periodicity, to obtain long-distance correlator bounds.

Gauge-rotate the charged scalar equation to a Klein–Gordon equation, solve its radial part with hypergeometric functions and horizon regularity, and extract boundary Green functions through GKPW and holographic renormalization. Fourier transforms use the poles of a digamma function.
A Fisher-matrix calculation forecasts constraints from an LSST Y1-like 3×2pt survey, including nonlinear matter-power modelling and a baryonic-feedback parameter.

Nonlinear predictions use the Bucko et al. emulator based on N-body simulations. It models the ratio of nonlinear decaying-dark-matter power to ΛCDM power using decay rate Γ, kick velocity vkick, and decaying-to-total dark-matter fraction f.

Differentiate the boundary energy to obtain thermodynamic conjugates, apply weighted homogeneity to obtain an Euler relation, and compare closed expressions with finite-difference derivatives. Horizon locations, extrema and censorship contours are obtained by root finding.

Separate the charged Klein–Gordon equation into spherical harmonics and radial modes; impose the ingoing near-horizon solution in tortoise coordinates and compute stress-tensor/current fluxes. Test censorship using a first-order Taylor expansion of f at its minimum, where f′=0.

Use Kruskal coordinates and a conformal-sector entropy formula, extremize generalized entropy over island time and radius, and match the no-island growth to the island plateau. Thermodynamic critical points are sought through pressure inflection conditions and used to normalize Page-time curves.
Sampling oscillation-fit inputs generates allowed two-zero Yukawa matrices, CLFV bounds and branching-ratio correlations. Reported 3σ intervals contain 99.7% of sampled outputs.

Perturbative tools include tree-level/one-loop matching to CLFV operators, RG evolution with charged-lepton re-diagonalization and leading-log texture corrections, and symmetry-guided identification of DFSZ two-loop contributions.
Gravitational anomaly matching constrains possible infrared spectra and symmetry-breaking patterns; SO(10) phenomenology instead uses RG trajectories toward infrared fixed points.

Numerical homogeneous trajectories feed linear Hill equations and H=0 Floquet maps, including both tachyonic and parametric amplification. The α-attractor discussion is semi-analytical and refers to prior work for full growth calculations.

A tachyonic-only estimate integrates Re√(-k²-V''(φ̄(t))) over a cycle and compares ln G with γT. This estimate omits parametric resonance and interference bands; γ/H and ln G/(HT) provide heuristic expansion comparisons.

Stochastic growth is modeled with products of cycle transfer matrices. Coarse-grained tower backreaction is separated into a deterministic mean mass shift and a centered fluctuating contribution, approximated through cycle-dependent random parameters.

Dimensional reduction and Einstein-frame Weyl rescaling determine radion dependence of axion kinetic terms; perturbative worldsheet counting constrains dilaton exponents. The resulting volume density enters the Laplace–Beltrami operator.
Examples use restricted roots and representation weights for symmetric spaces, ambient-space Laplacians projected onto the 5d F=1 hypersurface, and Kähler scalar Laplacians in 4d.

For homogeneous polynomials, use leading monomials in hierarchical growth sectors as local building blocks. Match tower arrangements across shared interfaces. Varying a finite impact parameter slides tower vectors perpendicular to the asymptotic trajectory, preserving their exponential rates along that trajectory.

In each monomial sector, construct the nonnegative-integer span of elementary EFT-string vectors, retain points with permitted KK/string norms, and enumerate consistent convex polytopes. Recursive decompactification constrains simplex pericenters and KK bound states, beyond checking individual vertices. The constraints become computational Diophantine problems.

Match successive constant-equation-of-state epochs and intersect the TCC, horizon and large-scale spectral-transition inequalities. The imported KK-summed perturbation calculation gives r=4HI^3/(π^3 As M*^3) in the approximately scale-invariant 5D regime, with quoted As≈2.1×10^-9.
Dimensionally reduce to the Jordan frame, perform a Weyl transformation, canonically normalize the radion, and solve the resulting Einstein–scalar equations with an exponential potential.
Test αstr·(2αtow)=w|αstr|^2 along candidate flows. Recursively analyze facets and pericenters as lower-dimensional frames, capturing candidates missed by a generic higher-dimensional lattice scan.

In top-down examples, identify approximately flat asymptotic regions or single-monomial growth sectors, compute tower and wrapped-brane α-vectors, and match populated sites and neighboring frames to the classification.

Enumerate allowed geometric and stringy frame simplices, construct their taxonomy lattices, and select string sites with |αstr|^2=2/ne. Use Gram matrices to recover scalar products from lattice projections; Mathematica performs the higher-dimensional finite scan.

Evaluate the scalar Gaussian determinant with a proper-time heat kernel. A locally constant electric field produces proper-time poles whose residues yield an imaginary effective action and vacuum decay; Appendix C compares this estimate with a reviewed global AdS2 spectral treatment.

Analytically continue the grand-canonical partition function to obtain the return amplitude; take fixed-μ β derivatives of log Z to obtain cumulants, then use moment–cumulant relations and Lanczos recursion to construct early-time spread complexity.

Entanglement entropy is obtained from a Euclidean partition function differentiated with respect to a horizon conical deficit. The imported one-loop logarithmic coefficient is calculated through the conformal anomaly after renormalizing Newton's constant or Planck area.

Wald–Iyer–Jacobson–Kang–Myers Noether-charge entropy gives the reported spherical expression Sbh=F′(RS)AS. Taylor expansion near RS=0, followed by the proposed curvature–area identification, produces area, constant and inverse-area terms.

LQG horizon-state counting uses SU(2) Chern–Simons states and their correspondence with WZW conformal blocks. A modified It-from-Bit calculation instead counts SU(2) singlets among many spin-1/2 punctures and applies a large-number approximation.

CMB bounds are recast using third-moment injection weights relative to an isolated graviton tower carrying all DM at the same reference peak mass: λ²=εh+(5/4)(gaγγMP)²εa. This separates fragmentation effects from the imported isolated-tower constraint.

Mode abundances follow a production-only Boltzmann equation dominated by inverse decays, integrated over a continuum KK spectrum. Temperature-dependent bath degrees of freedom enter the yield integral; the QCD transition is treated by a simplified pion versus quark/gluon prescription.

Mass-conserving fragmentation is formulated as coupled loss-and-gain integral equations. Scale-invariant profiles are solved by iterative quadrature with total-mass normalization; uniform single-tower fragmentation also has an analytic Laplace-transform solution.
Numerical Boltzmann integration produces C_l^EB and C_l^EE spectra for step-function rotation after last scattering, comparing suppressed and ordinary reionization.

Kinetic/mass-matrix diagonalization and hierarchical limits model axion mixing. Photon propagation uses a commuting two-component Hamiltonian in the adiabatic limit and Lippmann–Schwinger scattering for an ideal delta-function wall.

Covariant Mukhanov–Sasaki perturbations are projected into adiabatic and isocurvature directions, including the curved-field-space mass matrix and turn-rate coupling. Separate two-field examples explain the transfer mechanism; numerical spectra and observables, including the successful three-field case, use PyTransport.

The effective theory is developed from the Kähler potential and W=W0+ΣAi exp(−aiTi), expanded in the large-volume hierarchy. Numerical Friedmann and field equations track axion energy, individual kinetic contributions to ε and covariant field-space turning.

State-operator correspondence maps dimensions to cylinder energies. Calculations use homogeneous helical saddles and Gaussian fluctuation determinants; large-N calculations additionally use fixed-charge Fourier projection, collective/Hubbard–Stratonovich fields, saddle equations and a Legendre transform.

For canonical scalar fluctuations with antisymmetric A and symmetric M≥0, the authors compare the quadratic Hamiltonian with a Gaussian reference having squared masses given by eigenvalues of M−A². A variational inequality and an asserted finite difference of regulated Casimir sums yield non-positive scalar α0. Projected ground-state minimization supplies M≥0.

The authors combine previously published classical cascade simulations with black-hole entropy comparisons. For d≥4 and D≥5, their entropy scaling favors fewer localized higher-dimensional holes; the closed-system comparison assumes gravitational radiation can be reabsorbed.

Hawking production is estimated by integrating a normalized power-law daughter-hole spectrum, restricting to holes evaporating on the GL timescale, and bounding each hole's contribution to species-energy quanta by its mass at cutoff-sized radius.
Compute heavy/light eigenmasses from the temperature-dependent mass matrix and equate their splitting at T → 0 and T → +∞ to obtain the quoted reference factor 1/2 for separated crossings.
Canonicalize the kinetic matrix, diagonalize the transformed Hessian, and rotate the quartic tensor to extract perturbative decay constants. The definition absorbs the Taylor-expansion factor.
Effective excursion is computed as trajectory length ∫sqrt(Gab Φ′aΦ′b)dN=∫sqrt(2εH)dN. Individual comparison distances are obtained by varying one modulus with the other two fixed at their minima.

The potential combines BBHL α′³ and logarithmic loop terms, a phenomenological uplift Cup/V^p, winding-loop corrections, and higher-derivative F4 terms. Analytic stepwise stabilization is explanatory; numerical minima are obtained by treating all four volume fields simultaneously.

Inflationary trajectories are obtained from curved-field-space Einstein–Friedmann equations in e-fold time, using the metric and Christoffel connections derived from K=−2ln V. Reported inflation runs retain three fields and hold the overall volume fixed.

Integrate the background relation between H and field displacement, compare the declining Higuchi threshold with the exponential tower-mass envelope, and convert the resulting field interval into a classical traversal time.
Use stochastic coarse-graining, Langevin/Fokker–Planck evolution, and the reflection principle for one-sided first passage. A Brownian time change supplies a comparison bound for varying H.

The imported critical-point algorithm exploits sparse charges and hierarchical amplitudes, analytically removes separable directions, searches a reduced fundamental domain using its lattice structure, and classifies roots by a rescaled Hessian. Smith normal form is used for the lattice basis.

The search uniformly rescales divisor volumes, τi(k)=kτi(1), from the stretched-cone tip. A change in critical-point count diagnoses possible catastrophes; the location is refined by solving the critical equations while tuning a Hessian eigenvalue to zero.

Canonical axions are evolved with adaptive slow-roll gradient-flow equations dϕi/dN≈−MPl²∂iV/V. The authors monitor ε, longitudinal η and transverse Hessian eigenvalues, counting inflation only until ε or |η∥| reaches one.

Construct non-toric threefold bases as hypersurfaces in toric fourfolds. Adjunction, intersection theory and Lefschetz arguments determine relevant geometric data; toric stratification, Newton polytopes and Hodge–Deligne numbers provide additional divisor-counting tools.

Expand vertical flux as G4^vert=Σϕiα[Di]∧[Dα], analyze Cartan commutants and Stückelberg constraints, and integrate flux over matter surfaces to obtain chiral indices. Quadruple divisor intersections are organized as M(IJ)(KL); the authors describe the resulting breaking and chirality formulas as resolution-independent.

F-term conditions W=∂T W=∂S W=∂U W=0 define the Minkowski baseline. Stability and uplift shifts are treated using potential second derivatives and linearized coupled real-modulus/axion extremum equations, with anti-D6 energy represented by a nilpotent-superfield potential.

Democratic Type IIA formulation, harmonic-form dimensional reduction and equation-of-motion Hodge duality; auxiliary four-forms are integrated out, followed by term matching between the string flux potential and the low-energy QCD four-form description.

Darmois–Israel matching, together with the conserved Killing energy of the dust surface, relates the exterior metric to the interior Hubble rate. Hawking temperature follows from surface gravity, and entropy is obtained by integrating the first law.

The endpoint is located using f(r0)=f′(r0)=0 in the untruncated metric. Parameter differentiation and fixed-entropy chain rules produce the thermodynamic response; accretion uses fluid conservation laws and a conserved mixed-component energy flux.

Use the conformal-mode Friedmann balance −3M_P²H²+ρ=0 as an illustration of negative gravitational contribution. Summarize a cited CFT/BRST implementation in which physical states satisfy conformal constraints.

Rewrite the classical gravitational equation as vanishing total energy-momentum tensor, then apply the metric Schwinger–Dyson identity to obtain ⟨√−g Tμν⟩=0. The author interprets this identity as the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints.

Cayley–Menger signed volumes characterize simplex realizability. The dihedral construction projects orthogonally to a bone, samples a realizable triangle, then uses rotations or boosts to construct the higher-dimensional embedding. Separate large-edge constructions analyze asymptotic spine and spike families.

New sampling algorithm constructs individual simplex embeddings sequentially around bone circuits, inheriting shared geometry and sampling missing vertices or projected lengths. Inconsistent assignments trigger deletion of affected edge-star embeddings; some constructions are postponed.

Universal scaling equations follow by varying external length L, internal volume parameter ρ and dilaton directly in the reduced action. Calibration forms organize flux couplings; auxiliary-field elimination embeds the reduction in real 2D N=(1,1) supergravity.

The authors separately reduce ten-dimensional Killing-spinor equations and match them to the 2D supersymmetry conditions. Orbifold-cycle periods give necessary Page quantization constraints; Cauchy–Schwarz applied to the Cayley form yields the general volume bound.

Reconstruct anti-kT wide jets with R=0.8 and soft-drop grooming, zcut=0.1 and β=0. Combine the leading groomed jet with the two leading photons, requiring photon–jet separation >0.8 and 11<mγγ<16 GeV.

Expand the complex scalar about its VEV; introduce explicit U(1)ϕ-breaking Higgs and colored-scalar interactions; integrate out heavy colored scalars for effective gluon/photon couplings. Estimate ALP mass corrections with separate quadratic Higgs-loop and logarithmic colored-scalar cutoffs.
Collider chain: FeynRules/UFO → MadGraph5_aMC@NLO with NNPDF23_nlo_as_0119_qed → PYTHIA8 showering, decays and hadronization → DELPHES CMS/ATLAS cards → ROOT selection analysis.

For tachyon-free entries, numerically integrate the full orbifold partition function over the modular fundamental domain. For entries without shifted-sector massless scalars, compute the physical Hessian g^{ac}∇c∇bΛ using the Narain sigma-model metric; at stationary points it reduces to g^{ac}∂c∂bΛ.

Reconstruct roots from PL² = 2 and PR = 0, then simple roots, fundamental weights and affine Kac marks. For order two, choose one node per simple factor with mark κ = 1 or 2 and contribution ω/κ; retain only candidates admitting consistent full Narain-lattice lifts.

Use Cauchy–Schwarz bounds to make the winding, gauge-lattice and momentum search finite. Shifted O8 scalar candidates satisfy 0 ≤ PR² ≤ 1, PL² = PR² + 1 and m² = 2(PR² − 1): strict inequality gives tachyons, equality gives massless boundary states.

For RN, replace the proper-distance prescription with k̃r⁴=χ⁴KRN(r), using the classical Kretschmann scalar. Analyze the extremal condition |e|=M and infer a temperature from the scaled photon energy in the stated large-mass regime.

Evaluate Hawking temperature by surface gravity and separately by identifying it with a near-horizon scaled photon energy. Derive heat capacity from ∂M/∂T, entropy from ∫dM/T, and photon-dominated mass loss from a Stefan–Boltzmann estimate. Surface-gravity entropy is evaluated numerically.

Use the imported momentum-dependent metric to define m²=gμν(x,k)kμkν and derive a modified dispersion relation. Introduce scaled quantities ω̃²=ω²/f and k̃r²=kr²f, then identify k̃r=ξ/d(r) for Schwarzschild, with d the radial proper distance.

WKB plane waves with random phases and Rayleigh amplitudes construct the expanding scalar field. Gaussian-field Wick contractions reduce density correlations to field correlators; the retained slow modes are Fourier transformed into a density power spectrum.

The binary calculation combines a decaying two-level Landau–Zener system, parabolic-cylinder-function solutions, TT quadrupole radiation and a stationary-phase Fourier spectrum. Detectability uses numerical saturated cloud masses and relativistic final-state decay rates.

Numerical integration of the string-emission spectrum is supplemented by an analytic approximation taking Ωφ constant above its infrared cutoff. A Gaussian likelihood compares the additional isocurvature power with a fixed CDM background; exclusion uses 2 log(LS+B/LB)<−2.71, stated as one-sided 95% confidence.

Iyer–Wald covariant phase space: vary the symplectic potential and Noether identity through third order, integrate over Σ=H∪Σ₁, and separate gravitational, electromagnetic and dilaton contributions to horizon canonical energy and the third-order symplectic source.

Estimate discharge using uniform-field Schwinger production multiplied by tower multiplicity and integrated over V_nh∼(2M)³; add estimated tower radiation entropy to the earlier hoop-radius merger entropy budget.

The gauge-theory argument imposes vanishing one-loop beta functions node by node, restricts matter representations through large-N Dynkin-index scaling, and relates representation dimensions to indices and quadratic Casimirs. Matter counting then bounds the central charge and tower decay rate.

The geometric analysis uses Fenchel–Nielsen lengths near nodal degenerations, estimates the scale of an M2-brane wrapped on a shrinking systole, and translates the Einstein-region field-range question into a Weil–Petersson diameter problem.

Computes universal bordism groups using the mod-2 Adams spectral sequence, including extension problems; in degrees below eight the calculation uses the Steenrod subalgebra generated by Sq1 and Sq2. Degree-two discrete torsion also uses AHSS and the Smith isomorphism.

Uses the Yamashita–Yonekura differential Anderson-dual model: an anomaly is represented by (h,ω), with h an R/Z-valued three-dimensional bulk phase and ω an anomaly four-form, modulo local counterterms. The realized sigma-model anomaly is pulled back along f:X→BO(10); universal degree-three bordism therefore suffices for anomalies, but not for discrete torsion.

Schwinger proper-time and heat-kernel evaluation of the one-loop KK determinant, approximating densely spaced KK levels by an integral. A complementary torus calculation uses real-analytic Eisenstein series; subtraction of the zero-temperature vacuum selects the thermal direction.

Numerical integration of static Einstein equations versus central density, exterior black-string matching, and entropy from dS=dM/T; separately, supersymmetric linear sigma models and protected indices, explicit bordism fillings, and sphere-product bordism decompositions.

Dimensional reduction of the democratic type II pseudo-action in ten-dimensional Einstein frame, imposing RR duality after variation. The resulting two-dimensional dilaton-gravity action retains the volume-dependent Ricci coupling; a real superpotential is constructed to reproduce flux, curvature, and source contributions.

Reduce the IIB ten-dimensional Killing-spinor equations using orientifold-compatible spinors in string frame, compare the resulting algebraic equations with the two-dimensional superpotential conditions, and obtain curvature from external-spinor integrability.

For IIA, introduce quantized metric flux through left-invariant forms with dη7=fη56. This gives dΦ1=−fΨ2, dΦ2=−fΨ1 and dΨ=0; the non-closed F4 components then support O4 tadpoles through their Bianchi identity.

Telescoping sums yield dot-product lattice rules against principal-tower and species vectors. For positive sums of potential terms, a common lower bound on projection along the unit species vector bounds the full logarithmic gradient through nonnegative convex weights.

Track each operator through iterative compactification using nonnegative integer Weyl weights wi, with w1=0 for a potential. For curvature/flux operators the weights are even; spacetime-filling brane contributions instead use wi=Di−Pi, the brane codimension, which may be odd.

The radion component is vρi=[(wi+1−2)(Di−2)−(wi−2)(Di+1−2)]/sqrt[(Di+1−Di)(Di+1−2)(Di−2)]. In stringy phases the additional component is vϕ=[wD−D−kg(D−2)/2]/sqrt(D−2), where perturbative operators have kg=2g+n−2.

An illustrative likelihood uses independent Poisson bins at 160–200 keV with zero events and 225–271 keV with one event. Counts include a 2.84 tonne-year exposure and a smooth efficiency interpolation constrained by published endpoints; background uncertainties are neglected.

Effective matching uses the zero-four-momentum boundary-to-boundary messenger propagator twice. Brane couplings, the distant symmetry-breaking insertion, cutoff factors and non-exponential normalization are absorbed into δUV.

Recoil calculations combine the endothermic minimum-speed function, the shifted truncated-Maxwellian mean inverse speed, coherent weak charge and a Helm form factor. Natural xenon and tungsten are treated with their isotopic abundances.

Published-limit reinterpretations use KATRIN mβ≤0.45 eV and KamLAND-Zen T1/2>3.8×10²⁶ yr. The conservative 136Xe conversion uses matched Argonne inputs p=183 MeV and mββ limit=62 meV, excluding only when the phase-minimised amplitude exceeds that limit.

Daya Bay is recast using its 3158-day sample, 26 far-hall energy bins over 0.7–12 MeV, baseline averaging and a correlated Gaussian likelihood. Oscillation parameters are fixed to NuFit 6.0 inputs; contours are quoted at 90% confidence.

KK expansion and mode rotations produce the 4D mass matrix. A block-matrix secular equation determines eigenvalues and eigenvectors; a Schur-complement resolvent resums the full tower contribution to neutrinoless double beta decay.

Numerical shooting tunes the initial scalar value, obtains the throat size from its constraint, and seeks finite asymptotically flat solutions satisfying ȧ(0) = ḟ(0) = 0 and f(∞) = fa. Dimensionless radial variables are used to scan single- and two-coupling cases.

Varying the independent connection gives algebraic torsion and non-metricity coefficients. Substitution reduces the wormhole problem to coupled second-order radial equations for the scale factor and scalar, with extra connection effects encoded in G.

Inflation is analyzed in the Einstein frame after eliminating the connection and canonically normalizing the radial field. Leading slow-roll observables and numerical e-fold counts are combined with MCMC sampling of parameter regions at fixed Ne.

A common-offset scan varies all three transient initial angles together over δ = 0.05–0.80 at fixed potentials. A separate least-squares CPL fit samples the late equation of state uniformly in ln a over 0 ≤ z ≤ 2.

Fractional-density maxima are located through positive-to-negative crossings of wtot − wi, selecting each field's largest maximum. The late potential amplitude is adjusted to H(0) = H0 including transient remnants. The authors report tolerance, step-size, peak-grid and earlier-start convergence checks.

The authors integrate the full periodic potentials as eight first-order equations in N = ln a, from z = 10¹¹ to today. Friedmann and Raychaudhuri quantities are computed from all fields and fluids at every step, retaining gravitational backreaction and resolved oscillations.

The reviewed horizon-entropy calculation combines a Lorentzian Gauss–Bonnet theorem with simplicial Regge calculus for the horizon deficit angle; recovering the stated entropy requires a particular physically motivated sign choice.

Veneziano's reviewed approach builds on an all-order string-cosmology reformulation: Hamiltonian/Routhian methods reduce the existence of regular bounces to an analytic criterion. Adding a nonperturbative dilaton potential supplies the reported late-time attractors.

The reviewed collapse treatment uses canonical quantization of a null dust shell and a Lemaître–Tolman–Bondi cloud, reduction to a self-adjoint Hamiltonian for the outermost layer, and exact normalizable wave packets. The homogeneous Oppenheimer–Snyder limit uses affine coherent-state quantization.

Multiply each internal graviton propagator by its own scalar weight, Wick rotate, and apply radial ultraviolet power counting. Vacuum counting instead uses three-dimensional phase space, two physical polarizations, and zero-point energy.

Evaluate a mode quantum's Newtonian potential at the center of a uniform Hubble sphere, infer a negative wavenumber shift, and use reciprocal absolute spacing to construct a continuum spectral density.

The spin-2 analysis uses transverse-traceless perturbations, the Lichnerowicz operator and Stückelberg helicity decomposition. Separation of variables gives a Sturm–Liouville problem for warped KK profiles, with Neumann endpoint conditions.

Group-manifold curvature is expressed through Lie-algebra structure constants; KK masses follow from internal Laplacian eigenvalues and lattice identifications. The Nil3 twisted-sector Casimir contribution is evaluated using a heat kernel and zeta-function regularization.

Pseudo-average examples are completed to all polynomial orders using Gaussian moment tensors and Schur complements. A symmetric tensor-product Hilbert-space construction with Poisson weights establishes positivity for the topological gravity model.

Open statistical tests use completely positive matrices and their copositive dual cone, including the Horn witness. Bootstrap applications combine moment-matrix positivity with Schwinger–Dyson or planar loop equations and additional non-SOS inequalities.

The authors formulate a multivariate moment problem and apply the imported Riesz–Haviland criterion. Motzkin and Choi–Lam nonnegative non-SOS polynomials give explicit statistical inequalities beyond closed-universe Gram positivity.

Semiclassical Euclidean partition-function expansion with V_eff=−log Z/Vol4; integration over translational and fermionic collective coordinates; flux insertions saturating universal E3 zero modes; locality estimates for correlated instanton/anti-instanton interactions.

Dimensional reduction and Weyl rescaling determine volume powers. Gauge running, dimensional transmutation and the Kaplunovsky–Louis relation provide complementary condensate estimates. A two-parameter logarithmic correction is then inserted into the four-dimensional F-term potential and minimized at large volume.

Circle reduction tracks the radion, Wilson-line axions and scalar zero modes. The c-map example uses central-charge identities and the hypermultiplet metric to evaluate cancellation of dilaton, complex-structure and axion exchanges for BPS instantons.

Expand mediating fields to quadratic order and probe couplings to linear order. Gaussian integration, equivalently evaluation on sourced classical solutions, gives the cross interaction after subtracting individual self-energies. Derivative counting determines the large-separation multipole hierarchy.

Flux backtracking identifies asymptotic moduli trajectories and potential steepness. The asymptotic radial wave equation defines an effective transverse dimension and phase-space factor. Formal sphere reduction is used to identify generalized Freund–Rubin potentials.

Solve the massless scalar s-wave equation using ingoing Hankel modes in the AdS throat and Bessel modes in oscillatory asymptotics. Match their constant zero-frequency branches in an overlap region, then form the ratio of conserved radial fluxes. Nonoscillatory asymptotics are treated through the effective potential.

Pfaffian functions are represented by finite triangular first-order differential chains with polynomial right-hand sides. Reviewed Khovanskii bounds connect this defining data to the number of non-degenerate zeros.

Non-perturbative methods combine differential chains with Borel-Laplace resummation. The supplied monomial-model excerpt expresses Borel transforms through generalized hypergeometric functions to establish summability and Gevrey-structure definability.
For wavefunctions, use the Riccati substitution ρ=ψ′/ψ, satisfying ρ′=2m(V−E)−ρ². Apply it separately between finitely many nodes and assemble the graphs with the isolated zeros.
Generalized Scherk–Schwarz reduction encodes internal dependence in an O(3,3) twist matrix whose generalized brackets yield constant embedding-tensor components satisfying Jacobi identities.

Tree-level three-vector worldsheet amplitudes determine gauge structure constants. Narain-lattice automorphisms, fermionic lifts, level matching, modular completion and character expansions constrain and test explicit orbifold constructions.
Brane production is added as S proportional to T^8/M, with an equal radiation sink. Introducing χ=H/M closes an extended autonomous system with normalized source s=3κΩr²χ.

Autonomous abundance equations in e-fold time, a Friedmann constraint, fixed-point enumeration and Jacobian eigenvalues determine existence, stability and spectator-driven exits. Numerical integrations accompany the analytic treatment.
Israel and Maxwell junction conditions give a radial potential and signed kinetic factors. Positive exterior kinetic factor at the final degenerate horizon supplies the finite-crossing criterion.

Fixed-incoming scalar quantization is dressed by Schwarzian-Maxwell boundary dynamics. A convergent Liouville K-Bessel overlap gives the four-Gamma kernel; source smearing then defines the leading-order transition amplitude.

U(1)Y′ charge assignments forbid ordinary dimension-four Yukawa couplings. Ordered mediator chains connect the ordinary left- and right-handed fermions through endpoint couplings and adjacent-link couplings to a Higgs singlet.
The construction matches renormalizable mediator chains to higher-dimensional Yukawa operators, then uses gauge invariance to identify a claimed leading Planck-suppressed PQ-breaking scalar operator.

Express the coefficient through target-space geometry; extend to product spaces of decoupled axio-dilaton pairs and formulate fragmentation using charge-to-action vectors, polar sets and a sufficient convex-hull condition.
Insert a probe Euclidean (−1)-brane with S(x)=S0 exp(−βϕ/2)−qθ. Use the background moduli geodesic to rewrite its action and radial derivative, then identify when its minimum is negative.

Combines flux quantization, intersection and tadpole constraints with toric reflection involutions and hypersurface singularity checks. The selected scan contains 11 manifolds, 28 orientifolds and 605 candidate T-brane models.

Uses the four-dimensional N=1 supergravity potential, expansions in small g_s and inverse volume, and vacuum-energy/Hessian conditions. Minimizes the combined D7 D- and F-term potentials and examines uplift normalization using dimensional reduction and the brane Kähler potential.

Uses Gauss–Codazzi decomposition, background Einstein equations, Israel junction conditions and GHY boundary cancellations to obtain the graviton action. A Weyl transformation maps non-minimal scalar couplings to Einstein frame and absorbs their background effect into the warp factor.

Expands the action to cubic order, applies on-shell mode equations and integration by parts, and sums massive-spin-2 polarizations. Large-mode WKB overlaps and zeta-function channel sums supply the tower scaling estimates.

Roelcke–Selberg decomposition organizes the weighted difference between theta functions and their Eisenstein averages into cusp forms, Eisenstein residues, and continuous spectrum. The review associates these moduli-dependent corrections with symmetry breaking; a tower-of-states interpretation is only suggested.

Choi doubling and Schwinger–Keldysh generating functionals formulate mixed-state symmetries. Group twirling and Hubbard–Stratonovich auxiliary fields express weak-symmetry restoration through averages; the auxiliary weight is a quasi-probability distribution.

The reviewed Siegel–Weil proof compares modular cusp asymptotics and a shared differential equation, then invokes uniqueness through absence of a square-normalizable Laplacian eigenfunction with the required eigenvalue. It avoids explicit moduli integration.

Use a canonical single-field effective superpotential W_n=λϕⁿ/(nMⁿ⁻³), a negative Hubble-induced mass, stabilizing higher-power potential, and A-term phase torque; estimate radial tracking and approximately conserved comoving charge after generation.

Classify gauge-invariant monomial types using simultaneous F- and D-flat configurations and the gauge-boson mass-matrix rank. Qualifying pairs have two independently variable amplitudes, rank 12 when both are nonzero, and lower rank when either vanishes.

Construct the weight-three Hodge decomposition from V=e^(K/2)Π, its Kähler covariant derivatives and their conjugates. Supersymmetry equations supply Griffiths transversality; the symplectic pairing supplies the polarization, and the Weil operator relates Hodge norms to gauge couplings.

For cubic prepotentials, use the supergravity r-map to a 5d projective special real parent. Import Hessian-signature and nonnegative-functional results to obtain a positive cubic basis, then lift the basis change back to 4d.

Apply imported nilpotent-orbit and Hodge-norm growth results without assuming quasi-unipotent monodromy. Jordan decomposition, limiting mixed Hodge structures and Deligne splittings classify degenerations and their coupling scalings.

Joint Cobaya MCMC uses DES-Dovekie supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO and Planck PR4/NPIPE CMB likelihoods. Uniform priors include ξ1, ξ2 ∈ [−1,1], without initial sign restrictions; convergence requires R−1 < 0.01. The supernova magnitude offset is analytically marginalized, leaving relative distances, while BAO calibration uses the computed drag sound horizon and sampled Ωb h².

Analytic background solutions follow by changing variable to ln a and solving a constant-coefficient two-component density system. For positive discriminant Δ, both densities are sums of modes proportional to a^(3λ1) and a^(3λ2), with coefficients fixed by present densities.

The perturbative treatment decomposes the transfer four-vector parallel and orthogonal to the dark-matter velocity, then develops scalar density and velocity equations in longitudinal gauge and Fourier space.

Use H=log M_q as a Lipschitz height function. Cauchy–Schwarz bounds its variation by Q_q/M_q times Weil–Petersson speed; integration gives a scalar bound on length without expanding individual metric components.

Construct one auxiliary charge for every growth sector. Deligne splittings and commuting sl(2) triples establish opposite weight-filtration bounds for the charge and limiting period; the Cattani–Kaplan–Schmid growth theorem supplies exact Hodge-norm estimates.

Bound cascade overlaps using profile completeness, then sum daughter channels. For cosmology, sum decay photons over the freeze-in tower, include survival and redshift, and compare bin-integrated signals with archival Galactic and isotropic gamma-ray spectra.

Express the surviving three-graviton vertex as the square of a color-stripped Yang–Mills vertex. Use massive transverse-traceless polarization sums for the width and a parent-rest-frame partial-wave argument for its threshold behavior.

Expand the gravitational action to cubic order and integrate profile-gradient overlaps by parts using the mode equation. On shell, L_□ cancels L_m. The field redefinition h=e^H−1 gives an alternative explanation of their removal.

Cancel irreducible quartic gravitational and gauge invariants, the separate D4 Pfaffian invariant, and any U(1)-G_i^3 term. Express the remaining anomaly polynomial as a quadratic form M; Green–Schwarz factorization requires rank(M)≤2 and the product of its two possibly nonzero eigenvalues ≤0.

First enumerate lattice-compatible anomaly vectors. For each class Σ, solve the linear multiplicity equations Dm=t_Σ with the dimension budget d^T m+s=n_H and nonnegative neutral-singlet number s. Charge-dependent rows impose quadratic, quartic and cubic mixed abelian constraints.

For n_V=96, spectra assembly deletes a simple factor, replaces its vectors by neutral drones, and converts representation dimensions into projected multiplicities. The paper gives an inductive completeness argument conditional on complete seed catalogues, preservation under projection, and exhaustive reconstruction of every compatible fiber; it reports exact integer Mathematica implementation.

Solve Picard–Fuchs equations using Frobenius series in conifold and large-complex-structure (LCS) patches, transform to a symplectic period basis, and locate extrema from multiple starting points. An initial O(10³) flux scan retained O(200) convergent solutions; approximately 50 series terms were found sufficient in the convergence study.

Diagonalize the metric-normalized covariant Hessian at partial extrema; integrate coupled scalar and Friedmann equations in flat FRW spacetime; measure trajectory length by s=∫dt√(Gᵢⱼφ̇ⁱφ̇ʲ). Analytic asymptotic expansions and volume-homogeneity identities supplement the numerical analysis.
The reviewed cosmological analysis uses a two-parameter fading dark sector model and MCMC fits to DESI DR2 plus CMB and several supernova datasets, including recalibrated samples.

Phenomenological scale matching combines conjectural tower–vacuum-energy scaling, experimental exclusions of light string towers and uniformly large multiple dimensions, and wrapped-brane winding versus momentum masses.

Enumerate allowed local counterterms and distinguish ultralocal, semilocal, and non-renormalisable anomaly structures. Tune coefficients in a derivative expansion built from □^m[ϕ_(∆₄)ϕ_(2)]□^n[ϕ_(2)ϕ_(2)], using perturbative field redefinitions to simplify the interaction basis.

Reduce contact amplitudes and correlators to integrals with the same meromorphic integrand. Extract the non-energy-conserving amplitude by the residue at the conformal boundary, and identify the same residue as the logarithmic-divergence coefficient using finite-cutoff holographic regularisation.

Invariant coset forms and explicit (co)homology determine harmonic fluxes and integral cycles. Replacing flux combinations by q1=f1², q2=f2², q3=f1f2 linearizes the internal Einstein equations; q3²=q1q2 then imposes a symmetric algebraic shape constraint Σ=0.
Homology-dependent closed calibrations reduce minimum-volume questions to maximizing a linear functional over a polygon defined by Σa βa=0 and |βa|≤αa².

A spherical Euclidean probe-M5 instanton supplies the nucleation criterion. Flux quantization and Dirichlet approximation tune near-extremality; dimensional reduction, a scalar-potential Hessian and the field-space metric assess a restricted perturbative spectrum.

In the intermediate description, integrating out entangled scalar matter induces a quadratic effective action. The calculation isolates a vector contribution in the large-distance stress-tensor two-point function and restores covariance through hij+∇iVj+∇jVi.

Killing equations and compactness arguments establish the absence of continuous isometries for d>2. An inverse vector differential operator constructs a separate geometry-based perturbative dressing; ADM constraints test its invariance.

Bulk linearized Einstein equations are decomposed into normalizable KK modes with brane boundary conditions. Extra-dimensional gravitational Wilson lines supply Stückelberg vectors, and the integrated Hamiltonian constraint determines admissible dressed operators.

Independent selection uses rational null boundaries and finitely many possible obstruction witnesses. Geometric arguments use nefness of f, surface Riemann–Roch and Serre duality to establish candidate effectivity, followed by irreducible-component analysis to identify Mori generators.

Enumerate integral candidates e²=−1, b0·e=1, d(e)=f·e>0 and e·Fa≥0. Organize them by pairwise nonnegative intersection; discard each candidate having a negatively intersecting partner of lower H-degree. Lorentzian causal differences and integral degree descent establish the ordering.

Resolve local C2/Z2 patches with truncated Eguchi–Hanson spaces, track orientifold lifts in affine charts, and determine global exceptional forms and their orientifold parities. A dimensional reduction of the F4 energy illustrates bulk–exceptional Hodge mixing.
Flux backtracking removes the D4-sourced F4 terms. The residual flat-domain-wall BPS equations admit an analytic solution; restoring F4 requires numerical integration of the coupled BPS system.

Expand the real superpotential to quadratic order in exceptional periods around the stabilized untwisted solution; add exceptional F4 fluxes qa, solve ∂uaP=La+Xaua+…=0, and integrate out these fields to estimate shifts of the bulk solution.

Use dilaton and volume homogeneity to balance superpotential sectors. Project the metric-raised superpotential Hessian onto the volume–dilaton plane, apply Cauchy interlacing for bounds, and test coupling to orthogonal directions before identifying exact eigenmodes.

Analyze axion-dressed gauge-invariant fluxes, Stückelberg quotients and matrix ranks; solve flux equations using inverses on their image and Sherman–Morrison identities. Physical large-flux directions are obtained only after Bianchi identities, tadpoles and axionic flux identifications.
Conformal transformation g̃μν=Ω²gμν with Ω²=ξϕϕ²/MP², followed by canonical normalization dφ/dϕ=√K(ϕ) and approximate integration in weak and strong non-minimal-coupling regimes.

EFT of dark energy parametrization using αM, αB, αK and αT; scalar kinetic and sound-speed conditions Qs>0 and cs²>0; slow-roll inequalities combined with potential-gradient and field-distance conjectures.

Estimate sterile production using scattering-assisted active–sterile oscillations, an un-backreacted Boltzmann equation, radiation-era temperature evolution and entropy-normalized yields. Replace densely spaced KK sums by integrals and append a Boltzmann-like heavy-mode suppression.
Estimate the Galactic signal through an extended NFW line-of-sight integral, a black-hole explosion rate per dark-matter mass, and mixing-induced Majorana-neutrino decay channels.

Use 5d Schwarzschild temperature–mass and evaporation-lifetime scalings, including an approximate greybody coefficient, and average isotropic emission over S3 to separate emitted KK rest mass from four-dimensional kinetic energy.
Lagrange inversion expresses horizon area in terms of logarithmically corrected entropy. Taylor expansions of the mass are evaluated through first and second order in the logarithmic parameter β.

For general entropy maps, the authors substitute the inverse map into the unchanged mass relation, differentiate by the chain rule, solve T=0, and substitute the resulting extremal entropy before comparing parameter derivatives.
Lagrange-multiplier implementation of the fixed metric determinant; metric variation, the contracted Bianchi identity and assumed matter conservation make the multiplier an integration constant.
Apply apparent-horizon thermodynamics, −dE = T_h dS_h + W dV with W = (ρ−p)/2; introduce H-normalized variables and N = ln a to construct an autonomous system and analyze Jacobian eigenvalues.

Build PSD state densities by paired normal-momentum shaking and boundary projection as congruence transformations. Test a separately defined common crossing-symmetric functional on conserving partial-wave probes and nonconserving ISO(1,2) absorptive blocks.

Analyze transverse Laplacian spectra and Green functions, eikonal phases and direct-minus-image propagation. Positive packet densities diagnose zero-mode ambiguities and distinguish zero-mode subtraction from geometric exclusion.

Apply a twice-subtracted dispersion relation, select low-energy contour residues and evaluate contact overlaps and graviton exchange in a mixed momentum–position representation. A string Regge example uses transverse diffusion to examine the UV dispersive tail.

Review scalar-representative functional integrals for metric, three-form and fermion sectors, including Gaussian integration and momentum/volume counting. Assumed factorial growth produces a Gevrey-l series, with l one fewer than the number of field sectors, treated by a principal-value Laplace–Borel integral.

Construct dynamical chains using dimensional reduction/uplift, T-duality and, for SO(32), type I/heterotic S-duality. The E8 × E8 chain additionally passes through a Taub–NUT description and specified blow-ups before reduction along the Hořava–Witten interval.

Fast scans evolve the full axion–SM Boltzmann system down to 60 GeV, then track WKB mode energies using singular-value decomposition and eigenvector overlaps. Trajectories classified as nonadiabatic are rejected except for the modeled nonlinear crossing. Resolved examples require parameter adjustments to recover the target relic density.

A limited 2+1-dimensional lattice ensemble tests fragmentation during monodromy–cosine crossing. It uses radiation-dominated expansion, Gaussian initial perturbations and no dissipation beyond Hubble damping; its energy-partition distribution is compared with homogeneous evolution.
