Extract local friction by an adiabatic expansion of temporal memory kernels using dressed propagators with thermal widths. Combine the resulting slow-roll equation with radiation balance, convert consistency requirements into parameter inequalities, and bound N = ∫H dt.

An intuitive Hartree treatment attributes dissipation to delayed relaxation of particle occupation numbers as their φ-dependent masses change. The departure from equilibrium is expanded using a relaxation time of order the inverse thermal width.

Reduce discrete charges using allowed MSSM superpotential and neutrino mass terms, then solve mixed SU(3)², SU(2)², and gravitational anomaly conditions. Repeat with a Green-Schwarz contribution, taking equal SU(3) and SU(2) Kac-Moody levels.

Construct alternatives using symmetry-breaking VEV insertions, matching elementary constituents onto a composite X, or introducing fractional-charge singlets so that X decay requires additional fields.
Enumerate lowest-dimensional superpotential and Kähler operators linear in X for selected SM representations and discrete charges, and estimate lifetimes from their cutoff suppression.

Piecewise renormalization-group running includes intermediate particle thresholds, coupling-normalization factors k_a, and corrections Δ_a containing higher loops and thresholds. Conventional and rational logarithmic unification are compared with mechanisms using large thresholds.

Compactification sizes are estimated by matching gauge and Newton couplings using perturbative Hořava–Witten volume profiles and tree-level Type I relations. Supersymmetry mediation is explored through order-of-magnitude soft-mass estimates.

Apply the slow-roll equation 3Hφ̇ = −V′ and flatness inequalities MP|V′/V| ≪ 1 and MP²|V″/V| ≪ 1 to individual terms in an effective potential containing a mass, quartic coupling and Planck-suppressed operators, excluding accidental cancellations.

Estimate supersymmetry-breaking contributions through the inverse Kähler metric: V contains MS^4 k(φ), with k expanded in powers of φ/MP. Holomorphy constrains the superpotential, whereas phase symmetries do not comparably constrain this real Kähler contribution.

Construct normalized mass eigenvectors and the mixing matrix U, then calculate gauge-neutrino survival probabilities as coherent sums over propagating eigenstates. Relativistic phases are approximated by λi²t/(2p).

Perform orbifold Kaluza-Klein reduction and canonical normalization, then study finite and infinite mass matrices using characteristic polynomials, eigenvalue sums and exact trigonometric summations. Integrating out sufficiently massive tower states gives effective one- or two-state mass matrices.

Represent communication of distant lepton-number breaking by the transverse Green function Δn = (−∇² + mχ²)^−1. A separate domain-wall construction illustrates how a higher-dimensional invariant interaction reduces to the component-selective brane coupling.

Normalize bulk KK wavefunctions, evaluate their overlap with wall-localized fields, and integrate out massive KK pairs at tree level. Canonically normalizing the induced neutrino kinetic term produces a corrected light mass and a cutoff-dependent upper bound.

Construct the interaction from localized-mode overlap, massive bulk exchange with Yukawa suppression, light bulk exchange with power-law behavior, and stretched-string tension. Localized interactions decay exponentially with separation; the light-mode force depends on the balance of tension and charge.

Use an effective four-dimensional scalar equation φ̈+3Hφ̇+V′=0, slow-roll conditions |M_P V′/V|≪1 and |M_P² V″/V|≪1, and n=M_P^−2∫V/V′ dφ. Inflation ends when either slow-roll condition fails; separate Yukawa-dominated and power-law-dominated slopes.

Use holomorphy and discrete PQ periodicity to constrain gauge kinetic functions and holomorphic couplings. Estimate axion-dependent Kähler corrections by deformation from an N=2 setting, and identify the exponential factors with stretched membrane or wrapped D1/D5 instanton actions.

Match compactification scales to moduli VEVs and gauge couplings; canonically normalize the axion; estimate classical damping, quantum fluctuations, and subsequent hilltop instability in a proposed late-inflation history.

Estimate Q-dependent potential variations from the supergravity tree potential, cutoff-sensitive one-, two-, and three-loop contributions of nonrenormalizable matter/gauge couplings, and QCD/electroweak instantons. The estimates constrain variations across Q's range, rather than merely the potential at one point.

Use the finite-temperature free energy of modes becoming massless at coincident branes to estimate a positive thermal mass. Follow dilution through thermal inflation and brane oscillations, then estimate reheating, frozen stretched-string density, and bulk-graviton relic constraints.

Analyze Yukawa and gravitational bulk-exchange potentials, supplemented by a density-dependent linear string-tension term. An alternative inverse-hierarchy toy model uses one-loop Kähler renormalization and running gauge/Yukawa couplings to generate a logarithmic potential with a distant minimum.
Solve the five-dimensional Einstein equations with ds²=e^(−2σ(φ))ημνdxμdxν+rc²dφ², imposing orbifold symmetry and matching the delta-function sources at both branes.

Identify graviton and radius-modulus zero modes, integrate the curvature action over φ, and canonically normalize visible-brane matter fields to read off four-dimensional gravitational and mass scales.

Calculate Higgs-mediated nuclear scattering using neutralino mixing and effective Higgs–nucleus couplings. Antiproton and positron forecasts instead rescale previously published flux calculations; these are not independent propagation calculations.
Numerically evolve coupled Boltzmann equations for modulus number density, LSP number density and radiation energy density, from modulus domination through reheating and LSP freeze-out.

Use instantaneous decay for analytic estimates. The final mass-to-entropy ratio is approximated by the minimum of a production-limited yield and an annihilation-limited yield; numerical solutions determine the abundance contours.

Match mixed anomalies to twisted-modulus gauge kinetic couplings. With one effective twisted field, fα=S+sαM and Cα=−δX sα; for the all-Yukawa class with Ng=3, ND=1, cancellation requires 2s3=s1+s2. This is a constraint on candidate string models, not a construction.

Classify family-independent charge assignments by Yukawa and anomaly constraints, then test coupling invariance by summing charges. Tables enumerate superpotential terms and supersymmetric F-term/D-term B- or L-violating operators through dimension six.

Use the imported instanton-generated superpotential W_dyn=2Λ⁵/(ε_ij Q^i Q^j), together with an approximately minimal quark Kähler potential in the weak-coupling region. Integrating out X and Q gives W_eff=(κΛ⁵/V²)exp(−Φ/F_A).

Introduce the gaugino mass through the F component of a gauge-coupling spurion. The appendix also presents a component instanton calculation: integrate fermionic coordinates and instanton size, use the low-energy local-profile approximation, and sum instanton and anti-instanton contributions.

Uses holomorphy and discrete Peccei–Quinn symmetries to constrain gauge kinetic functions and superpotentials, identifies exponential suppressions with brane-instanton actions, and inserts the resulting symmetry breaking into the supergravity scalar potential.

Uses the scalar equation of motion and order-of-magnitude slow-roll estimates, then estimates potential variations from Q-dependent QCD and electroweak parameters. Integrating out matter in the metrical case instead uses covariance with respect to its conformally related metric.

For the quadratic potential, estimate the end of inflation and the field value approximately 55 e-folds earlier, impose the historical COBE normalization, and compare the high-energy approximation with numerical slow-roll solutions.

Use the gauge-invariant curvature perturbation ζ and local energy conservation to propagate adiabatic scalar perturbations outside the Hubble scale, with field fluctuations evaluated at Hubble crossing.
Apply potential-dominated, friction-dominated slow roll: H²≈(8π/3M₄²)V[1+V/(2λ)] and φ̇≈−V′/(3H). Define modified slow-roll parameters and integrate Hdt to obtain the number of e-folds.

Bosonize J³ and use parafermions to construct flowed vertex operators and a reflection amplitude. Separately sum spectral-flowed affine characters and analytically continue a Lorentzian partition function to compare with the Euclidean H₃ model.

Classify classical solutions by monodromy conjugacy classes, then spectral-flow timelike and spacelike geodesics into short and long strings. A quadratic Nambu-action expansion near a collapsed string exhibits spectral asymmetry and changing oscillator vacua.

Extend the no-ghost argument by expressing physical states, modulo null states, as representatives annihilated by positive J³ modes. The proof uses a Virasoro/J³ basis and imports the positivity result for the resulting SL(2,R)/U(1) sector.

Vary the coupled FRW scalar equations and use the averaged equation of state of coherent quartic oscillations. For homogeneous C and f = g, p_C = ρ_C/3 and the pressure-dependent dilaton force can be integrated into an effective potential.

Use a numerical cosmological example, energy-redshift arguments and estimates of the first-oscillation time to assess capture. Estimate the fraction of initial conditions using an adopted Kähler-weighted phase-space measure.

For slowly varying Φ in thermal equilibrium, canonically rescale C by √f, giving quartic coupling ε_eff = εg/f². A perturbative finite-temperature expansion then yields the Φ-dependent contribution governed by g/f².

Use the D=5 attractor condition α_I proportional to X_I, expressing normality to the cubic hypersurface, and special-geometry Hessian identities at supersymmetric critical points to classify extrema and argue for their separation.
Analyze first-order Killing-spinor equations for static, flat-sliced domain walls and linearize scalar and warp-factor flows near supersymmetric endpoints to determine asymptotic geometry.

Represent B-flux by freely acting half-lattice shifts with discrete torsion. Their Chan-Paton matrices obey γ_iγ_j=Δ_ijγ_jγ_i, with B_ij=ln(Δ_ij)/(2πi) modulo integers, producing noncommuting Wilson lines.

Use Klein-bottle, annulus and Möbius amplitudes with loop/tree modular transformations and careful relative proper-time normalization; supplement tadpole tests with Chan-Paton projections, explicit mixed-sector vertex combinations and Higgsing/anomaly diagnostics.

A Z2 quotient of Euclidean eleven-dimensional Schwarzschild supplies a bounce. Its surviving negative mode and Lorentzian continuation are used to interpret vacuum decay and the expanding boundary wormhole.

Poincaré invariance, stress-tensor conservation and asserted flat-background one-loop tracelessness determine the tensor structure. Einstein equations with homogeneous scale factors then give the initial backreaction.
Kaluza–Klein reduction and a Schwinger proper-time sum evaluate the one-loop vacuum energy. Jacobi-theta modular transformation establishes convergence and positivity of the constant J.

Use the standard 4D N=1 supergravity F-term potential and analyze extrema through the Hessian in real and imaginary modulus directions. Separately compare gauge and gravitational couplings, including compactification-scale factors and Hořava–Witten threshold corrections.

Estimate Euclidean wrapped-brane instanton actions as tension times wrapped volume and contributions as exp(−action); match BPS branes and action scalings across S- and T-dual descriptions. Dominance is assessed through dependence on coupling and compactification radius.

Adapt previously developed odd-spin-structure one-loop amplitude methods to Klein bottle, annulus and Möbius strip contributions. Canonical anomalous amplitudes contain N gauge and M gravitational insertions with N+M=D/2+1 and one longitudinal polarization.

Use the modular-invariant Witten-index-weighted channel dictionary and completeness of boundary reflection coefficients to express the anomaly polynomial through boundary/crosscap one-point functions, then factor its reducible part to identify generalized Green–Schwarz couplings.
First-order superspace dualization of each charged-field phase replaces a chiral multiplet by a neutral periodic twisted chiral Y, coupled to gauge field strength as a dynamical theta angle.

Holomorphy, theta periodicity, R-symmetry and semiclassical asymptotics restrict possible corrections. A unit vortex with two fermion zero modes gives a nonzero two-point function detecting the exponential twisted-superpotential term.

Landau–Ginzburg periods ∫γexp(−W)dx1…dxn encode chiral-ring structure through derivatives in flat coordinates. Charge constraints generate differential equations for periods, rewritten as Picard–Fuchs equations in FI parameters.

Construct a finite covering by maximal polytopes using combined weight systems (CWS), then enumerate IP subpolytopes and all lattices on which they are reflexive. The working covering uses 308 r-minimal CWS, reduced from 201,346 relevant CWS. The embedding x_i=〈V_i,X〉 describes the polar by weight-system linear constraints and x_i≥−1.

Use the vertex-pairing matrix X_ij=〈V̄_i,V_j〉 to determine possible reflexive lattices. Integral X is necessary and sufficient for some such lattice; integral row/column transformations give X=WDU. Intermediate lattices correspond to subgroups of the finite quotient M_finest/M_coarsest.

Calculate hypersurface Hodge numbers with the imported lattice-point formulas involving l(Δ), interior-point counts l*(θ), facet subtractions, and products for dual codimension-two faces. The resulting Hodge data are computed from polytopes rather than used to identify polytopes.

Construct boundary states and transform tree-channel annulus amplitudes to the open-string loop channel to extract zero modes. For the orientifold, compute Klein-bottle, annulus, and Möbius amplitudes and their tree-channel tadpoles.

Conjugate a symmetric rotation by T-duality, or apply opposite rotations directly to left- and right-moving fields. The D0→D1 at an angle→mixed D2 chain translates geometric angle data into background-flux boundary conditions.

Rotate the left/right contributions to the Dirichlet disc propagator and tachyon OPE to recover mixed-boundary correlators and the noncommutative product. Oscillator quantization of strings between T-dual angled branes gives endpoint commutators.

Embed the target toric diagram in that of C^k/(Z_n)^(k−1), choosing a sufficiently large parent orbifold. Tune FI parameters, solve linear equations in x_i=|p_i|², and identify fields acquiring nonzero VEVs. Remove their columns and take row combinations of the parent charge matrix that vanish on those columns.

Split the resulting Q_t into F-term charges Q and D-term charges Q_D using the FI column. Compute T=ker(Q), K=Dual(T^t), and Δ=Q_D(T^tK^t). The authors argue that T^tK^t is invariant under changes of nullspace basis.

Read candidate binomial F-relations from the integer nullspace of K^t. Integrate them into a gauge-invariant superpotential by choosing charge-compensating fields, iteratively checking other derivatives; additional fields may be needed. This step requires informed choices rather than only linear algebra.

The stability exponents are g_ijk=1+p_i−p_j−p_k for distinct indices, e^(p)=Σ of p selected metric exponents − λ_p p_φ/2, and b^(p)=Σ of d−p−1 selected metric exponents + λ_p p_φ/2. Maxwell equations with spatial derivatives neglected give time-independent electric densities and magnetic components.

BKL consistency analysis restores terms discarded in the Kasner approximation and compares them with leading t^−2 terms. Dangerous gravitational, electric and magnetic contributions scale as t^(2g), t^(2e) and t^(2b); stability requires every corresponding exponent to be strictly positive.

The M-theory electric criterion is treated by constrained maximization with two Lagrange multipliers. Other models are handled through maps between Kasner spheres or, for the heterotic model, by replacing Einstein-frame exponents with string-frame exponents.

For the gravitational potential, the authors separate H_3 Laplacian eigenmodes into spherical harmonics and radial hyperspherical Bessel functions, then integrate continuum Yukawa contributions weighted by their values at the source.

New backgrounds are generated by timelike T-duality of U(1)-fibered AdS metrics, and by combining an SL(2,C)/SU(2) WZW model with other conformal models and a timelike linear dilaton. S-duality and field redefinitions reinterpret imaginary fluxes in type II* theories.

A Freund–Rubin four-form ansatz reduces the eleven-dimensional field equations to Einstein conditions on product factors. Supersymmetry is tested by Killing-spinor equations and their Weyl-tensor integrability conditions.
Generalized Dirac quantization uses single-valued membrane amplitudes; the M theory argument quantizes the dual seven-form integrated over the internal manifold.

A J-dimensional flux lattice is counted within a thin spherical shell representing the allowed vacuum-energy interval. Shell volume, lattice-cell volume, and degeneracy D estimate typical level spacing.
Cosmological evolution is modeled with semiclassical Euclidean membrane instantons and stochastic inflaton evolution, comparing de Sitter fluctuations against classical restoring drift.

Treat the F-term relations as an associative polynomial algebra A over C; find its center using ordered monomials and solve for finite-dimensional irreducible representations. For general deformations, standard ordering and center calculations become finite linear-algebra problems at each polynomial degree, subject to possible parameter poles.

Irreducible representations modulo conjugation define points through maximal two-sided ideals with A/I isomorphic to a matrix algebra. Characters define topology on formal positive sums of points; coherent bimodules and exact sequences supply the proposed extended-brane and algebraic K-theory structures.

Closed-string chiral operators are studied through traces. Cyclicity makes the single-trace map factor through the vector-space quotient A/[A,A]=HH_0(A). Links between quantum-group representations and closed-string fusion rules are suggested rather than established.

Torsion-flux averaging implements a torsion Gauss-law constraint; finite quadratic Gauss sums introduce an Arf invariant. SU(5) bundle embeddings into E8 and ordinary index formulas relate the M-theory and K-theory phase factors.

APS boundary index theory, η-invariants, mod-two Dirac indices, spin bordism, and the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence supply the phase identities and cohomological obstructions. Circle-bundle η-invariants are evaluated by Fourier modes and zeta-function continuation.

Apply imported Takhtajan–Zograf variation results to the on-shell Liouville action: moduli derivatives give coefficients of the Schwarzian in a quadratic-differential basis, while mixed variations are related to the Weil–Petersson metric.

Evaluate the on-shell Einstein action through hyperbolic volume, boundary area and local counterterms. A planar cutoff exposes area and logarithmic divergences; the canonical cutoff z = ε exp(−φ) makes the rescaled induced metric approach the canonical boundary metric.

Schottky uniformization describes bulk identifications and boundary conformal structures. Fuchsian uniformization supplies a covering map J whose inverse determines the uniformizing Liouville field and its Schwarzian stress tensor.

Implement thermal winding through twisted boundary conditions labelled by two integers. Integrate the quadratic transverse fields, express the determinant through fermion determinants, and use a chiral gauge transformation and anomaly to obtain the effective shift k → k−2.

Use modular transformations of the winding pair to unfold the nonzero sectors from the fundamental domain to a strip. Separate the invariant zero-winding term, interpreted as the zero-temperature vacuum contribution.

Expand the oscillator products separately in successive τ2 strips, impose level matching through the τ1 integral, introduce an auxiliary Gaussian variable and shift its contour. Pole residues yield discrete states; the remaining integral and regulated zero-mode sums yield the continuum density.

Extract the spectrum from the non-decaying super-Hubble solution μ = Ca, so n³PΦ = n³|C|². Small-cutoff-ratio and large-Bessel-argument expansions simplify the matching; an adiabaticity diagnostic is used to interpret the results.

Solve separately below the cutoff, between cutoff and Hubble radius, and outside the Hubble radius. Match μ and μ′ across transitions; use powers for the saturated de Sitter case and ordinary or modified Bessel functions for the polynomial families.

Replace n² in the mode equation by neff² = a²F²(n/a), yielding μ″ + [neff²−a″/a]μ = 0. Quantize through a time-dependent Hamiltonian and Bogoliubov transformation, and choose initial data by extremizing the initial energy density.

Insert gas energies and pressures into homogeneous dilaton-gravity equations; use classical world-volume intersection counting for annihilation and a two-dimensional phase portrait in l=λ̇ and f=ϕ̇ to investigate loitering.
Expand the DBI action for small transverse and gauge-field fluctuations, then average individual brane stress tensors to obtain homogeneous winding and non-winding equations of state.

Analyze partial breaking through gravitino mass matrices, spin-1/2 fermion shifts and supersymmetry Ward identities, using the de Roo–Wagemans formulation including its phase parameters. Solvable Lie algebras and projective disk coordinates describe scalar cosets and their embeddings.

Perform an Einstein-frame reduction retaining four SU(2)R-singlet shadow scalars: breathing, squashing and two internal three-form modes. Compute their kinetic metric and scalar potential; the four-form flux coefficient must vary as required by the eleven-dimensional Maxwell equation.

Expand linearized eleven-dimensional fluctuations in internal harmonics and diagonalize their masses. Combine quadratic mass/eigenvalue relations with Bose–Fermi harmonic maps generated by Killing spinors to construct shadow multiplets.

Replace the foliating S3 by a cyclic lens space through a NUT, or use the extremal-BTZ form of AdS3 through a semi-localised wave. Kaluza-Klein reduction or Hopf T-duality along its U(1) fibre produces warped AdS backgrounds; some IIA solutions are lifted to eleven dimensions.
Use sphere and AdS foliations: dΩ²_(p+q+1)=dα²+cos²α dΩ²_p+sin²α dΩ²_q, and ds²_AdS_(p+q+1)=dρ²+cosh²ρ ds²_AdS_p+sinh²ρ dΩ²_q. Select an S3 or AdS3 factor for the subsequent operation.
For D3/NUT, solve Δ_z H+KΔ_x H=0 in the restricted NUT background, then transform x1=r cosα cosθ, x2=r cosα sinθ, z=r²sin²α/(4QN). This exposes H=1+Q/r⁴ and the foliated internal metric.

Reduce to four-dimensional Einstein frame and canonically normalize form-field kinetic terms to infer physical charge densities. Wrapped-brane tensions follow cycle volumes, whereas charge scaling requires the moduli-space metric, examined near degeneration.

Use the BT Euclidean membrane instanton and gravitational bounce action. For k coincident membranes replace ρ2 by kρ2 and τ2 by kτ2, then model the probability as P∼exp(D−B), with D=k^β A T² and bubble area A=4πb².

Superconformal tensor calculus, auxiliary-field elimination and gauge fixing. Writing X^I=Y x^I(z), imposing N=-3 M_P^2 and quotienting by U(1) produces an n-complex-dimensional Kähler scalar manifold.

Supersymmetry identities yield a master gravitino equation and constraints. Spatial momentum and helicity projections separate transverse and longitudinal modes; special cases reduce to coupled first-order equations or oscillator-like second-order equations.

Encode curvature, R-symmetry connections and scalar-operator sources in gauged-supergravity boundary conditions; solve vanishing fermion variations in five- and seven-dimensional truncations, then uplift using imported formulas.

The no-go argument establishes positivity of T̃=−T^μ_μ+dT^L_L/(D−2), then integrates the warp-factor inequality by parts. Massive IIA instead combines Einstein and dilaton equations into an integrated positivity identity.
For the D3 (2,2) theory, count fermion zero-mode differences by an index theorem, match R-symmetry anomalies, and compare with c=3R_AdS3/(2G₃) after dimensional reduction.
Contrasts Wilsonian radiative-correction reasoning with the UV/IR correspondence: super-Planckian excitations can be extended black holes whose spectrum depends on the cosmological horizon.

Proposes a thermodynamic estimate of SUSY-breaking mass terms, proportional to [∫dM e^(S(M)−βM) Δm(M)]/[∫dM e^(S(M)−βM)], using black-hole entropy, inverse de Sitter Hawking temperature β, and an unknown virtual-black-hole contribution Δm(M).

Canonical oscillator quantization and Virasoro physical-state constraints organize the spectrum. Modular invariance of partition functions requires additional sectors, illustrated by the twisted sectors of the circle orbifold.

T-duality constructs worldvolume couplings; anomaly arguments constrain curvature terms. Open-loop/closed-tree cylinder duality relates gauge and gravitational descriptions, while low-velocity probe actions extract moduli-space metrics.

Solve a radial first-order flux system: f′=(1−F)tanh²(τ/2), k′=F coth²(τ/2), F′=(k−f)/2. Determine the warp factor by integration, imposing regular small-τ behavior and h→0 at infinity; extract Wilson-loop behavior from minimal string surfaces.

Use the imported Affleck–Dine–Seiberg superpotential and supersymmetric vacuum equations for an SU(M+1) theory with two flavors as a single-D3 probe of the quantum geometry; extend partially to SU(M+p)×SU(p).

Apply Seiberg duality to the strongly coupled SU(N+M) factor with 2N flavors, integrate out massive mesons, and match holomorphic scales and invariants to recover a quartic theory with ranks reduced by M.

Analyze Nambu–Goto string probes near flat and spherical D5 stacks, locating the curvature cutoff and the disappearance of smooth large-separation worldsheets. This analysis explicitly neglects the NS-potential contribution.

Study a fictitious minimally coupled scalar in the Einstein-frame background, impose normalizability and smoothness boundary conditions, separate its zero-momentum equation, and estimate masses by the scale r0²/R4.

Combine five-brane worldvolume charge singlets and D3-ball baryon vertices with SL(2,Z) transformations. Classify screened subgroups of ZN×ZN using modular arithmetic, the Chinese remainder theorem, and totient/divisor counting.

For singular instantons, regulate the potential at large φ, translate boundary constraints into canonical fluctuation variables, and compute eigenmodes numerically. The authors test matching prescriptions placed well beyond the onset of runaway behavior.

Use Sturm–Liouville operators, freedom in the positive eigenfunction measure, constant trial fluctuations, and Schrödinger-form transformations to identify negative directions. Spectral flow relates Hawking–Moss thresholds to new instanton branches.

Begin with the Lorentzian Hamiltonian action, impose gravitational constraints, integrate out gauge degrees of freedom, and analytically continue physical variables. Choose a retained linear combination of canonical coordinates and momenta that gives positive Euclidean derivative terms.

Adopt stress-tensor fluctuations as stochastic sources in Einstein's equations. Compare fluctuation energy with its Schwarzschild radius, impose a lifetime longer than the region's light-crossing time, and assess classical consistency by comparing Hawking evaporation and black-hole timescales.

Compute the regional Hamiltonian variance as a convolution of a fluctuation density F(x) and a geometric factor D_V(x). Evaluate a spherical region using exponential momentum regulators exp(-p/Λ) and exp(-q/Λ).

Split the boundary action into local and nonlocal pieces, then match independent curvature and scalar structures in the HJ equation. The displayed local ansatz includes U, κ and curvature-squared coefficients A, B, C.

Radial canonical decomposition, Legendre transformation and the Hamiltonian constraint are used to obtain an HJ functional equation by replacing canonical momenta with derivatives of the induced action.
Construct the small resolution using Wλ=0 and a patchwise Kähler potential K=F(r²)+4a²ln(1+|λ|²). Ricci-flatness reduces to an equation for γ=r²F′, integrated as γ³+6a²γ²−r⁴=0 after choosing γ(0)=0.
Alternatively reduce the radial ansatz to a one-dimensional action with a zero-energy constraint. A superpotential satisfying V=(1/8)G^ab∂_aW∂_bW−W²/3 generates φ′a=(1/2)G^ab∂_bW and A′=−W/3.

Derives the D-bound through a generalized-second-law process: the observer moves into an asymptotically empty de Sitter region, losing access to matter while cosmological horizon entropy increases by (A₀−A_c)/4.

Imports the covariant entropy bound S ≤ A/4 on orthogonal null light-sheets whose cross-sectional area is everywhere nonincreasing. Sheets terminate at or before caustics; truncation at area A′ permits the strengthened bound S ≤ (A−A′)/4.

Classifies spherical diamonds by maxima on their top and bottom cones. Auxiliary asymptotically de Sitter extensions allow the D-bound to constrain normal-side portions; the covariant bound controls remaining light-sheets, with complementary area terms giving S ≤ N.

Intersection-pairing test for D6 charge Q = Σa Na[Πa]: vacuum cubic anomalies test only [Πa]·Q = 0 for occupied cycles. D4 fat strings wrapping a complete supersymmetric three-cycle basis [Λi] test [Λi]·Q = 0 for every i, which the paper uses to infer Q = 0.

Compute probe zero-mode spectra from probe–probe and probe–background open strings, including Chan–Paton and orientifold projections; impose two-dimensional chiral gauge anomaly cancellation or four-dimensional USp global anomaly cancellation.
Quantize open strings with angle-dependent boundary conditions, apply GSO and geometric/Chan–Paton orbifold projections, and count replicated states through wrapped-cycle intersections.

Obtain RR constraints through one-loop factorization and homological charge cancellation. Compute triangle anomalies and factorize them using dimensional reductions of RR world-volume couplings and discrete Fourier transforms.

Solve the photon radial equation approximately in three overlapping exterior regions and match their solutions to obtain the unit-angular-momentum absorption probability; integrate this probability against the Hawking thermal spectrum.
Estimate positron emission by integrating the Schwinger pair-production rate over the exterior electric field, then compare its reciprocal with the neutral Hawking-cooling time.

Infer a semiclassical partition function from E(T) and S(T), use an inverse Laplace transform to obtain a density of states involving Bessel functions, and compare canonical thermodynamics for alternative discrete spectra.

Analyze a classical Geroch process: lower matter toward a much larger Schwarzschild black hole, evaluate the near-horizon redshift at proper distance R, and combine the resulting horizon-entropy increase with the generalized second law.

Use Birkhoff's theorem to define an equivalent Schwarzschild–de Sitter black hole for spherical matter. Eliminate the empty-de-Sitter radius through the cosmological-horizon equation and expand in the small gravitational-radius ratio.

Determine local goldstino couplings by cancelling supersymmetry variations of the metric, dilaton, gauge field, gravitino and dilatino terms. Reorganize the result geometrically using a modified vielbein and dilaton.

Complete the Chern–Simons-modified action through additional goldstino terms and gamma-matrix identities, then compare the predicted θθH coupling with disk amplitudes using Chan–Paton factors and fermion kinetic normalizations.

Use the Volkov–Akulov construction: a shifting Majorana–Weyl fermion defines a modified moving basis and metric whose transformations are induced diffeomorphisms. Replacing the flat metric in a matter action generates nonlinear supersymmetry and energy-momentum-tensor couplings.

Kaluza–Klein reduction of the Pasti–Sorokin–Tonin M5 action determines brane kinetic terms. The N=1 F- and D-term potential is expanded in charged fields, geometric expansion parameters, and powers of the nonperturbative superpotential.

Supersymmetry-projector constraints determine membrane embeddings. Superembedding boundary conditions supply a membrane vertex operator; an instanton-sector fermion two-point function and holomorphy then determine the superpotential contribution.

Exploit a formal correspondence with N=2 black-hole attractor equations: identify the flux superpotential with the holomorphic central-charge function and fluxes with charges. Vector auxiliary-field equations correspond to central-charge extremization; imposing zero gravitino mass supplies an additional condition.
Use special Kähler period geometry, electric/magnetic hypermultiplet Killing prepotentials, and gravitino mass eigenvalues to relate gauging, the flux superpotential and supersymmetry conditions.

Solve Picard–Fuchs systems near degeneration loci and analytically continue periods to an integral large-volume basis. Monodromy, asymptotic expansions and numerical continuation identify which quantized fluxes generate each local superpotential.

Use Wess-Zumino consistency to relate consistent gauge and supersymmetry anomalies. Bosonic equations follow in the 1.5-order formalism, with the prescribed chiral-tensor duality conditions imposed after variation.

Construct supercovariant fermion transformations, then determine remaining fermionic terms by closure of the supersymmetry algebra. Closure on fermions is on-shell and determines their complete field equations; these equations determine the quartic fermion terms in the Lagrangian.

Uses homogeneous thermodynamics: combining ρ = Tσ − p, dE = T dS − p dV, and σ = α√ρ gives p = ρ when densities and pressure are volume independent. CFT entropy scaling motivates the proposed matter model.

Formulates a classical scattering analogue using complex field-equation solutions with past and future boundary conditions. Temporarily moves the initial boundary a few Planck times beyond the singularity; final configurations must allow finite-mass black holes as well as particles.

Use Seiberg-Witten periods to follow force coefficients through moduli space. Analyze whether proposed composites can split into constituent subgroups whose energy is minimized at infinite separation, supplementing the force analysis with semiclassical information about BPS saturation.

Sum electrostatic, magnetostatic and scalar massless exchanges using the two-derivative effective action. The prepotential determines propagators and τ; the Witten effect supplies electric/magnetic mixing, while derivatives of BPS central charges determine scalar couplings.

Vary Σ outward by a positive normal eigenfunction. The absence of outer trapped surfaces forces the first eigenvalue of L=−Δ+(Ŝ−S−|B|²)/2 to be nonnegative. A conformal deformation then produces nonnegative scalar curvature, followed by positive-scalar-curvature or Ricci-flat alternatives.

Derive area bounds from the second variation inequality for stable minimal hypersurfaces, compare it with the Yamabe functional, and apply Hölder's inequality. The argument also yields a purely Riemannian theorem independent of black-hole interpretation.

For stronger topology conclusions, minimize area in a homology class using geometric measure theory, then use the maximum principle and a local splitting rigidity result to exclude the exceptional case.

Holographic on-shell string correlators encode off-shell spacetime Green functions: two-point singularities identify states, and three-point functions determine physical couplings through LSZ reduction. The dilaton discussion separately uses radiative logarithms and a Weyl transformation to Einstein frame.

The reviewed holographic description replaces the linear-dilaton throat by a cigar SCFT, with background R5,1 × SL(2)k/U(1) × SU(2)k/U(1). Separating fivebranes on a circle implements the double scaling limit and cuts off the strong-coupling region.

Integrating the holomorphic three-form over the sphere fiber reduces its periods to integrals of ω = dx√(W′²+fn−1). Compact periods Si determine deformation coefficients, while regulated noncompact periods Πi = ∂F/∂Si determine special-geometry couplings.

Monodromies determine logarithmic period terms and cutoff dependence. Chebyshev polynomials construct rank-KN solutions from rank-N solutions while preserving the reduced curve; for cubic W, the corresponding low-energy superpotential scales by K.

The independent field-theory analysis deforms the exact N=2 solution. It minimizes Wtree on loci with mutually local massless monopoles, implementing double-root constraints by Lagrange multipliers and factorizing PN²−4Λ^(2N) = HN−n² F2n.

A circle reduction of four-dimensional supergravity with chiral and linear multiplets checks part of the proposed three-dimensional supergravity interpretation. Homogeneity removes the extra |W|² contribution in that comparison; Chern–Simons supersymmetrization motivates the vector-sector D-term.

Decompose F4 by Hodge type and apply the Lefschetz decomposition to its (2,2) component. Primitive-form Hodge identities separate self-dual and anti-self-dual pieces; complex-structure and Kähler-moduli identities convert the flux norm into superpotential gradients, using the tadpole condition.

Reduce eleven-dimensional supergravity together with A3∧X8 and the curvature-quartic combination J0−E8. Use the leading Ricci-flat Kähler metric, the vanishing integrated internal J0 contribution, and a Weyl rescaling to normalize the three-dimensional Einstein term.

The radial equations are solved with a warp depending on |r|. Integrating the scalar equation across an infinitesimal interval in the fifth direction supplies the wall jump condition, complementing the distributional Einstein equations.

The author reduces Einstein’s equations using the separated scalar and metric ansätze. A separable bulk potential introduces radial and temporal functions U1(r), U2(t), together with separation constants C and D; a quadratic time dependence then reduces the remaining equations.

Analyze commuting holonomies through centralizers and extended Dynkin diagrams; use bundle topology and Chern–Simons invariants to distinguish flat-connection components. The centralizer classification used here is imported from earlier mathematical work.

Implement continuous Wilson lines by Narain lattices and discrete holonomies by asymmetric orbifolds. Level matching, including stronger even-order conditions, and phases of winding states supply string consistency tests.

Classify flat RR line bundles using equivariant cohomology and spectral sequences; use relative cohomology and vanishing-cycle lattices for singular K3. RR flux phases are also computed through reduced eta-invariants, with an alternate algebraic K-theory quotient computation reported.

Combine AdS/CFT radius–flux relations with horizon-area scaling. Use the UV/IR relation and holographic renormalization-group reasoning to associate deep-interior modes with a long-wavelength CFT sector, modeled by spatial reduction to quantum mechanics.

Estimate interactions from localized wavefunction overlaps in spatial volume ∼L^k. Periodically identify AdS time at scale L and then continue it to Euclidean signature, giving an effective spacetime volume ∼L^(k+1).

Separate sphere harmonics and solve the resulting massive scalar equation on global AdS using hypergeometric modes. Ground states behave as exp(−iωt)(cosρ)^(2h+); increasing AdS angular momentum pushes modes outward, while higher sphere harmonics further localize the l=0 sector.

For generalized fermionic kinetic terms, use field redefinitions involving N=exp(2γ̄⁰Φ) and an orthogonal L satisfying (∂₀+M̂₂)L=0. Define the canonical Hamiltonian in the resulting standard basis, evolve spinor modes, and numerically diagonalize the remaining Hermitian H₀ matrix.

Diagonalize the bosonic frequency matrix with a time-dependent orthogonal C, expand canonical fields in matrix-valued modes, and evolve generalized Bogolyubov matrices. Γ=CᵀĊ generates additional mixing terms I and J, so changing eigenvectors supply nonadiabatic effects beyond changing eigenfrequencies.

Derive wall profiles both from field/Killing-spinor equations and from a BPS-type energy functional. The latter contains one positive and one negative square, plus total derivatives and explicit source terms. The nine-form equation cancels the distributional source contribution, and vanishing square expressions yields first-order flow equations.

Promote G⁽⁰⁾,G⁽²⁾,G⁽⁴⁾ to independent fields and impose their Bianchi identities through Lagrange multipliers A⁽⁹⁾,A⁽⁷⁾,A⁽⁵⁾. Solving the multiplier equations recovers the lower-potential Romans description; eliminating the independent field strengths instead implements full dualization.

Expand the bulk-brane action to quadratic order in position fluctuations, solve the approximate mode equation using Bessel functions with a short-wavelength Minkowski vacuum, and convert brane ripples into radiation density fluctuations through collision time delays and Olson variables.

Promote parameters of a static BPS solution to spacetime-dependent moduli, substitute into the five-dimensional action and integrate over the orbifold coordinate. Field redefinitions separate an Einstein-like scale factor from scalar moduli with nontrivial kinetic terms.

Use the characteristic polynomial det(X−x) to construct a spectral covering. For generic distinct eigenvalues, the eigenspaces define a line bundle L on the covering whose push-forward is E. Adjunction and Hodge duality also relate scalar and twisted-form descriptions for divisors.

Dimensionally reduce the proposed nonabelian deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills equation, replacing transverse covariant derivatives by matrices. Symmetrized form expansions are reorganized using contraction operators and graded commutators into dimension-independent exponential expressions.

For the linearized four-dimensional scalar equations, apply Weitzenböck identities and integration by parts to a holomorphic embedding of a line bundle into a rank-two bundle. Positivity yields a necessary inequality when the subbundle is invariant under every transverse scalar.

Use the zero-spatial-momentum Kubo relation for the thermal Txy commutator, equivalently η=limω→0(GA−GR)/(2ωi). The graviton-absorption dictionary converts this into η=σ(0)/(2κ²), reducing the transport calculation to classical absorption.

Solve the radial wave equation in overlapping near-horizon, intermediate and asymptotic regions. Select the ingoing horizon solution, match to the outer Bessel-function solution, and obtain the absorption probability from the horizon-to-incoming flux ratio.

Use the semiclassical Euclidean gravitational path integral and a regular, fixed-charge, one-parameter family of off-shell geometries satisfying the spatial constraint equations. Hamiltonian surface terms give I=βE−S, with S=A/(4G), connecting negative specific heat to an action-decreasing direction.

Fourier decompose longitudinal s-wave perturbations along the worldvolume, choose a conformal frame with unwarped flat directions, and gauge away mixed/worldvolume metric components. Relate static Lorentzian threshold modes to lower-dimensional Euclidean eigenmodes by removing the Fourier factor and Wick rotating.

For the supersymmetry argument, impose the superpotential stability form, expand W asymptotically in exponentials with leading term W₀exp(−ακφ), and compare the slope required by acceleration with the slope permitted by positive V near the supersymmetric limit.

Integrate the FRW conservation and Friedmann equations for constant w; conformally map the resulting geometries into the Einstein static universe to identify causal boundaries. Compute the event horizon using a(t)∫dt′/a(t′), and locate the apparent horizon by vanishing expansion of radial null congruences.
Future causal accessibility is tested through convergence of ∫ from t₀ to ∞ of dt/a(t), with conformal-time coordinates and Penrose diagrams used to describe the boundaries.
Analytical and numerical evolution of the coupled Friedmann equation and scalar equation φ̈ + 3Hφ̇ + V′(φ) = 0; imported linear stability and tracker results supplement the examples.

Relate Chern–Simons levels to NS flux and massive-fermion shifts. The seven-dimensional modified Bianchi identity dh=(N/2)Tr(F∧F)=(N/4)Fᵃ∧Fᵃ tracks removal of flux as the twisting connection becomes trivial.

Use the imported BPS solution, its radial asymptotics, and explicit uplift formulas. Compare ten-dimensional supersymmetry-spinor projectors with the projectors of additional wrapped branes and antibranes to determine which charge sign preserves supersymmetry.
Apply Bousso's imported D-bound, Sm≤S0−Sc, to the RN-dS cosmological horizon. Expand its area difference, then replace horizon radius rc by object size R and mass parameter M by proper energy E.

The BDL calculation solves the Maxwell equation, uses distributional Einstein junction conditions, averages the yy equation, and integrates the resulting brane evolution equation before comparing it with moving-wall dynamics.

Use a four-dimensional flux superpotential and conifold periods, including the logarithmic dual period G(z)=z ln(z)/(2πi)+holomorphic terms. Solve complex-structure and dilaton F-term conditions and estimate the infrared redshift from the resulting exponentially small deformation.

Integrate the Einstein warp-factor constraint and five-form Bianchi identity over the compact space. Their difference is a sum of nonnegative terms under a source stress/charge bound, constraining flux duality, the four-form potential and localized sources.

Classify wrapping numbers using signed intersection products, prescribed chiral multiplicities and RR tadpole equations. Homology determines chirality and net multiplicity; metric and background data determine masses and tachyons.

Dimensionally reduce RR Wess-Zumino couplings to two-form–field-strength and dual-scalar–F∧F terms. These implement generalized Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation and determine which Abelian gauge bosons acquire masses.

Estimate Yukawa couplings through triangular string worldsheets, Y ∼ exp(−A), and gauge couplings through wrapped-cycle volumes. These are geometric estimates rather than a completed simultaneous phenomenological fit.

A reviewed supersymmetric hybrid-inflation example illustrates the mass problem: supergravity corrections from a quartic Kähler term generate inflaton curvature of order H² unless its coefficient is small.

Use the large-distance bulk propagator and D-brane charge/tension relations to obtain the static attraction. Expand the brane action to obtain a kinetic term and translate separation into an inflaton potential.

Apply four-dimensional Friedmann evolution and potential slow-roll parameters, integrate V/V′ for e-foldings, and use the historical COBE fluctuation normalization to estimate the compactification scale.

Dimensionally reduce the low-energy bulk and brane actions, combining brane tensions with massless bulk exchange. The displayed long-range potential is V(y)=A−B/y^(d_perp−2), with attractive brane–antibrane interactions.

Apply FRW slow-roll parameters, e-fold integrals and scalar-perturbation normalization. At compactification-scale separations, sum torus image contributions and expand around a hypercubic cell center.

Reduce the Einstein-Hilbert action, perform a Weyl rescaling and canonically normalize the radion. Analyze radiative mass corrections separately below and above the compactification scale, using four-dimensional effective theory and six-dimensional covariance respectively.

Compute one- and two-loop Casimir energies with momentum sums, Schwinger parameters and Jacobi theta functions. Subtract the decompactified contribution and include mass/wavefunction counterterm insertions to obtain finite radius-dependent terms.
Use dimensional analysis and the Callan-Symanzik equation to identify the marginal cubic interaction and resum leading powers of α0 log(r/ℓ) through the running coupling.
Use D7 world-volume Chern–Simons couplings, quantized flux, ALE intersection integrals, and curvature-induced charge to fix D5/D3 charges and logarithmic source terms.
Expand wrapped D5 probe DBI plus Chern–Simons actions at low velocity and compare their kinetic coefficients with second derivatives of the gauge-theory one-loop prepotential.

Set dilatino and gravitino variations to zero for the type B spinor ansatz, separating terms proportional to ε and ε*. Impose three-form Bianchi identities and use the five-form Bianchi identity to determine the warp-factor source equation.

Model Regge multiplicities through oscillator counting and fixed-length integer partitions. Combine induced kinetic terms with production estimates, thermal emission, and comparison of brane evaporation against radiation-dominated FRW cooling.
Calculate Euclidean brane/bulk Green functions, use a Källén–Lehmann representation, and match delta-function mode equations to obtain continuum profiles, resonances, and localized massive modes.

Use matter vacuum polarization and a stress-tensor trace correlator to estimate an induced Einstein–Hilbert coefficient Mind²∼MSM². Matter-induced higher-curvature terms are compared with the terms suppressed by the smaller bulk scale.

Free-field states are constructed using a Euclidean sphere propagator and a hemisphere path integral with specified equatorial field values. Polynomial insertions generate perturbative excitations, subsequently restricted by gravitational invariance.

Boundary limits of a free scalar propagator illustrate meta-correlators. To account for relative past/future de Sitter transformations, future insertion points are integrated against a weight of conformal dimension (n+2)/2 in each variable; suitable convergent weights require s≥2.

Use Euclidean boundary operator insertions to deform the prepared state. Approximate scattering amplitudes can be expressed as overlaps of corresponding CFT states, equivalently through Euclidean analytic continuation.

For BTZ, construct Hartle-Hawking Green functions by summing global-AdS3 Green functions over quotient images. The quotient restricts allowed wavefunctions without changing the inherited positive-frequency prescription.

Glue half the Euclidean black-hole geometry to a time-reflection-symmetric Lorentzian slice. The boundary path integral over an interval of length β/2 prepares the doubled-CFT wavefunction and fixes the bulk Hartle-Hawking state.

Solve the de Sitter-invariant Hadamard Green-function equation in the embedding invariant P, selecting the hypergeometric solution singular only on the light cone. Insert its asymptotics into a rescaled bilinear boundary expression to obtain scalar two-point kernels up to normalization.

Find diffeomorphisms preserving past-asymptotic metric falloffs. Holomorphic spatial transformations are accompanied by time shifts; their action on the boundary stress tensor supplies the anomalous term used to identify the central charge.

Use the Brown-York boundary stress tensor from an Einstein action with gravitational surface term and local counterterm. After constraints and gauge fixing, express Virasoro generators as contour integrals Ln=(2πi)^−1∮dz Tzz z^{n+1}.

Combine junction equations into a Friedmann-type equation with a ρ² term, an energy-exchange equation and an equation-of-state constraint. For multiplicative coupling z=1, a Jordan-frame Weyl transformation gives ordinary brane-matter conservation.

Solve the bulk Einstein, dilaton and form-field equations with warped, constant-curvature spatial slices. Modify the harmonic-function signs to avoid noninteger powers of negative bases, then analyze horizons, singularities and static versus cosmological regions.

Embed a moving brane at r=R(τ), calculate its induced FRW metric and extrinsic curvature, and impose Israel and dilaton junction conditions. There is no gauge-field junction condition because the external brane does not couple to that field.

Noether deformation of the ungauged theory, with a Chern-Simons term, covariantized coset currents, scalar-dependent fermion couplings and a scalar potential. The displayed action and transformations omit higher fermionic terms inherited from the ungauged construction.

The embedding tensor Θ specifies the gauged subgroup. Dressing it with the adjoint coset representative gives T_A|B=Θ_MN V^M_A V^N_B. Decomposition into SO(8,n) and SO(8)×SO(n) representations converts supersymmetry identities into a covariant projection condition.

A heuristic boost analogy treats matter as a collective excitation of a Lorentz-invariant environment with vacuum energy ρV. A dominant term resembling a square root of a matrix Hamiltonian motivates, rather than derives, an action first order in matrix time derivatives.

Finite eigenvalue state counts are estimated by integrating a symplectic form over phase space. On the sphere, stereographic coordinates provide the symplectic form; quantization is related to a charged particle in a monopole background and then to SU(2) representations.

Estimate noncritical D-brane and orientifold tensions by generalizing the NSNS cylinder exchange calculation and matching its infrared exchange to a D-dimensional low-energy Green function. This calculation relies on an explicit assumption about how fixing the dilaton changes the exchanged spectrum.

Balance contributions at different orders in string perturbation theory. After reduction to four-dimensional Einstein frame, the dS analysis extremizes U(Φ) ∝ a exp(2Φ) − b exp(3Φ) + c exp(4Φ), with a,b,c>0. The displayed extrema obey exp(Φ±)=[3b±sqrt(9b²−32ac)]/(8c); the paper selects the plus branch under 9b²>32ac.

Use asymmetric shifts, reflections, orientifolding, and discrete torsion to project out compactification NSNS scalars. The paper examines untwisted and representative twisted sectors, then adds RR flux combinations invariant under the orbifold group, with integer flux integrals over surviving cycles.
Apply cosmological singularity arguments and compare Einstein-frame with string-frame curvature to assess whether a perturbative worldsheet beta-function treatment remains possible.

Rewrite scalar evolution as an equation for energy versus field position and test convergence of the comoving horizon integral ∫dt/a. For multiple moduli, use trajectory path length as the effective scalar variable.
Analyze vacuum bubbles using semiclassical nucleation, time-dependent wall tension and energy difference, Schwarzschild-radius estimates, and the local Guth–Farhi black-hole argument.

Dual potentials convert matter equations into a first-order system. The eleven-dimensional example uses E=exp(A₃T)exp(A′₆T′) and F=dE E⁻¹ to encode the equation of motion and Bianchi identity through a supergroup law.
Lie algebra cohomology organizes the deformation problem: the germ is a cocycle, ambiguity is a coboundary, and obstructions are cohomology classes. Field redefinitions can remove some ambiguities.

The Gupta–Noether construction simultaneously deforms a gauge algebra and an invariant action while preserving rigid symmetry. Minimal coupling to the rigid symmetry's Noether current supplies the initial interaction.

In the simplified one-matrix sector, diagonalization and a Vandermonde redefinition turn singlet eigenfunctions into antisymmetric fermionic wavefunctions in an inverted oscillator. Both singlet and nonsinglet sectors are described as infinite dimensional.

Inönü-Wigner contraction constructs Newton-Hooke symmetry. Centralizers are computed by solving linear conditions from [A,Π]=0, allowing null, timelike and spacelike choices of the fixed momentum combination.

Ordinary and generalized Noether methods construct conserved charges. For the higher-derivative particle model, Ostrogradski momenta, second-class constraints and Dirac brackets reduce an eight-dimensional phase space to six dimensions before quantization.

Build free actions using BRST generators and projections onto the appropriate ghost-number or Sp(2)-singlet sectors. Compare formulations through auxiliary-field elimination, partial gauge fixing, oscillator expansions, and reduction back to the original light-cone theory.

Construct light-cone Poincaré generators from transverse spin representations, eliminate gauge and auxiliary components, and extend transverse indices and coordinates by two commuting and two anticommuting directions. The resulting IOSp(D,2|2) algebra contains a manifest spacetime Poincaré factor and an OSp(1,1|2) BRST factor.

Separate planar single-factor cubic anomalies from nonplanar mixed anomalies, using triangle-current Ward identities and loop-momentum shifts. Nonplanar loop-dependent phases supply the regulator underlying the reported mixed-anomaly cancellation.

Regulate the D-brane annulus anomaly with a Pauli–Villars mass M. Track its closed-channel damping factor into the noncommutative field-theory limit; removing that factor produces a leading F∧⋆′F contribution used to motivate the proposed pre-cancelled anomaly.

Use anomaly descent for the commutative theory and its proposed ⋆-product generalization; construct nonlocal, gauge-invariant analogues of Tr F∧F with open Wilson lines and express the proposed cancellation through Seiberg–Witten variables.

In the low-curvature regime, choose RG coordinates giving metric Ricci flow and dilaton diffusion. For time evolution, use the Einstein-frame description as a massless scalar coupled to gravity; large-n, n→n−2 transitions permit linearized diffusion and wave analyses.

Project D-brane worldvolume fields into quiver theories, identify twisted scalar mass deformations, solve the classical Higgs branch and integrate out broken gauge fields to obtain a probe metric. Quiver annealing follows partial resolutions and the surviving scalar and fermion spectra.

Use a D1-brane linear sigma model and its twisted deformations as a route to worldsheet RG flow. Reaching the nonsupersymmetric orbifold CFT requires tuning away the quantum potential; at large deformation, the resulting nonlinear sigma model is studied through metric and dilaton beta functions.

Decompose the vector representation into adjoint, singlets and other nonsinglets. Supersymmetry requires the latter to become tensor fields, with CMNP=CIJM=0 and symplectic representation matrices. Compactness also makes these matrices orthogonal, giving a unitary representation description.

Construct gaugings from ungauged theories by selecting a gaugeable global subgroup, covariantizing derivatives and adding terms required to restore supersymmetry. The central classification task is reduced to algebraic invariance conditions on C.

Work in a canonical basis with C000=1, C00i=0 and C0ij=−δij/2. Compact generators act through Aij∈so(n), and the remaining cubic coefficients obey Cl(ij Ak)l=0; invariant tensors supply the constructive building blocks.
Use a warped metric and flux ansatz, first-order BPS equations obtained from a radial superpotential, and an integral representation of the warp factor with h→0 at large τ.

Construct SO(4)-invariant differential-form ansätze in the zi coordinates and compare them with angular-basis expressions using computer-assisted algebra. Wilson-loop minimal surfaces and wrapped-brane probes supply the infrared dictionary.
Normalize RR fields using D-brane charge quantization and explicit cycle integrals, then compare the B₂ period with the difference of inverse gauge couplings.
Dualize Higgs-type couplings to BF theories, track integral periods and large gauge transformations, and retain boundary terms and boundary conditions when quantizing singleton modes.
Reduce on S³, retaining C₃=χω₃+c₃ and C₁=c₁ while freezing H and neglecting metric perturbations. The reduced RR action contains |dχ+kc₁|² and a separate three-form Chern–Simons sector.
Use the M-theory lift, wrapped M2 instanton phases and D2-probe photon dualization to interpret D0 symmetry as translation around the eleventh circle.

Fourier decomposition along the wrapped direction identifies KK modes with matrix entries. Exponential bidifferential product formulas and partial integrations then relate ordered matrix trace-integrals to membrane integrals.
Melvin couplings are constructed by a Y-dependent coordinate and spinor rotation, followed by the winding shift Y → ρ + Y and the membrane-to-matrix dictionary with symmetrized traces.

Quantum reduction is examined by integrating nonzero KK fluctuations in background-field gauge, using Euclidean continuation and a strong-coupling expansion in L; bosonic fluctuations scale as L and fermionic fluctuations as √L.

Use Weyl transformations between Einstein, string and higher-dimensional metrics; solve the V=0 system analytically; and transform to finite variables a₀,a₁ or light-cone coordinates a± on minisuperspace.

Analyze the lapse/Friedmann constraint to characterize collision matching, solve an exponential-potential toy model, and test string embeddings through boost spinors, leading-order string equations and winding/T-dual behavior.

Construct superspace representations by induced representations on the super-Poincaré/Lorentz coset, using Baker–Hausdorff rearrangements to obtain coordinate transformations and differential generators. Chiral representations follow through nonunitary similarity transformations.

Impose constraints on covariant-derivative algebras and solve graded Jacobi/Bianchi identities. In the three-dimensional vector example, Fαβ=0 expresses the vector connection through the spinor connection, leaving a field strength Wα subject to DαWα=0.

Use Berezin integration and covariant-derivative projection for components; derive supergraph rules from functional integrals and reduce Grassmann loops by D-algebra and integration by parts. Background-field quantization organizes a manifestly gauge-invariant effective action.

World-sheet annulus, Möbius-strip and Klein-bottle amplitudes are factorized into boundary/cross-cap exchanges. Tadpoles become sums of squares, giving twisted conditions B_a + Σ_μ C_a^μ Tr(γ_a^μ) = 0 for a ≠ 1. Gauge two-point functions are compared in open-loop and closed-tree channels.

Gravity is studied by linearizing bulk-plus-brane Einstein–Hilbert equations, imposing harmonic gauge, Fourier transforming along the brane, and matching transverse radial solutions. A shell distribution f(r) = δ(r−ε)/(a_{d−1}ε^{d−1}) replaces the point source.

Use a Freund–Rubin product ansatz, linearize the field equations, and expand scalar fluctuations in sphere harmonics. The metric/flux stability analysis is borrowed from prior work; additional Kalb–Ramond, dilaton and tachyon fluctuations are treated separately.

For finite temperature, take the large-black-hole-mass limit and solve the τ-independent, sphere s-wave dilaton equation. Match power series normalizable at infinity and regular at the horizon by locating zeros of their Wronskian numerically after truncation.

Organize reduced fields and deformation parameters into duality representations; combine the three-form equation of motion with its Bianchi identity using a dual three-form. Generate backgrounds by SL(2,R) rotations, then uplift ordinary IIA configurations to eleven dimensions.

Generalized Kaluza–Klein reduction permits scalar components of RR potentials to depend linearly on torus coordinates, for example A_m=a_m−½m_mn yⁿ. Their derivatives, reduced action and field equations lose this explicit coordinate dependence.

Use heterotic/M-theory duality fiberwise between small T³ fibers and K3 fibers. Split the heterotic Dirac operator into fiber and base parts: generic fiber eigenvalues are O(1/α), while zero modes localize near simultaneous zeros of three monodromy angles. A separable local Dirac model determines chirality.

Apply Kronheimer's hyper-Kähler quotient construction to a partial ADE unfolding. Leave one moment-map triplet unconstrained: X̂=Hᵏ//K′ is eight-dimensional, and X=X̂/U(1)′ is seven-dimensional, fibered over the unconstrained triplet Q=R³.

For the second class, quaternionic reduction gives a positive-scalar-curvature self-dual Einstein orbifold M. Known metric constructions on its twistor-space cone X and anti-self-dual two-form bundle X′ supply G₂ metrics; the modulus r₀→0 degenerates X′ to X.

Analytic continuation of conventional sphere reductions supplies warped de Sitter uplifts and variant direct-product reductions. The paper argues that the structure of these continuations carries over consistency of truncation.

Interpolating E-brane geometries use harmonic functions on a Lorentzian transverse space, a conformally related dual-frame metric, and light-cone-adapted coordinates. For spherical angular sections, near-horizon regions give dS_{m+1} × H^n or H^{m+1} × dS_n.

Noncompact Kaluza–Klein reduction is formulated through internal Laplacian eigenfunction expansions. Interactions are expanded using products f_m f_n = Σ_p d^p_{mn} f_p with finite coefficients; the discussion extends conditionally to other spins and warped products.

Compute weakly coupled Unruh-detector transition probabilities from the Wightman function. Imaginary-time contour arguments give detailed balance; Euclidean continuation of SdS₃ supplies the energy-dependent temperature used in thermodynamic entropy integration.

Linearize the Brown–York boundary stress tensor using lapse, shift and extrinsic curvature. Require finite boundary stress and generators, then identify allowed diffeomorphisms modulo those whose generators vanish.

Use embedding coordinates and global, planar, static and Kruskal charts to describe causal patches. Reduce the invariant scalar wave equation to a hypergeometric equation in P(X,Y)=η_abXᵃYᵇ, fixing propagator normalization by its Minkowski short-distance singularity.

Identify the bulk generator of combined time translation and spatial rescaling with boundary dilatations; extend this geometrical identification to nonconformal boundary RG evolution by analogy with holographic flows in AdS.

Use combinations of Einstein equations to relate Hubble evolution to energy conditions. Import the dS3 central-charge relation obtained from Virasoro asymptotic symmetries, then discuss a higher-dimensional c-function scaling.

Adapt the Brown–York variational stress tensor to spacelike temporal boundaries, augmenting the gravitational action by local intrinsic boundary counterterms. Evaluate at a finite temporal cutoff and then take the boundary limit.

Construct dS3 defects as discrete quotients of SL(2,C)/SL(2,R), restricting to the diagonalizable identification class considered in the text. Formal analytic continuation l→il is also used to infer structures from AdS calculations.

For the RG interpretation, formally rewrite the bulk Hamiltonian constraint using an action split S=Sloc+Γ, obtaining a Callan–Symanzik-type equation. Relate a candidate c-function to extrinsic curvature and use Raychaudhuri evolution for conditional monotonicity.

Use the induced kinetic terms and large-N power counting to approximate the remaining gauge and gravitational integrations. Leading gauge-loop effects and the UV-dominated gauge contribution to Newton-constant renormalization are treated at one loop.

Integrate the quadratic matter fields exactly to obtain bosonic and fermionic functional trace-log contributions. Standard heat-kernel techniques organize the resulting effective action into local kinetic terms and higher-derivative, generally nonlocal terms.

Generate linearized supergravity couplings by coupling current superfields to potential superfields with compensating transformations. An extra chiral potential acts as a Weyl compensator; changing the couplings reproduces current improvements through supersymmetric analogues of nonminimal curvature couplings.

Localize global super-Poincaré/superconformal transformations while preserving chirality, relaxing the reality condition on their parameter superfield. For constrained N=2 fields, use an arbitrary symmetric Lij and constraint-preserving prepotential variations; the naive localized transformation need not preserve the Bianchi constraint.

Read supercurrent superfields from the localized action variation and obtain conservation equations by varying free transformation parameters. Project to the supersymmetry current and vary it in superspace to extract central surface terms, selecting the canonical representative for comparison with canonical charges.

Uses Friedmann, scalar, and fluid evolution equations obtained from a four-dimensional action. Fluids evolve with the effective scale factor â = aβ(φ); radiation's contribution is φ independent, leaving only matter in the direct scalar-source term.

Introduces a crunch-to-bang matching prescription reversing a weighted scalar velocity with factor −(1 + χ). χ parameterizes radiation production. Subsequent evolution uses kinetic energy dilution proportional to a^−6 and radiation proportional to a^−4.

Thermal occupation numbers are obtained from the spectral partition function, using auxiliary chemical potentials and expansion in |g|². A two-boson mixing model supplies a comparison for identifying effects specific to boson-fermion mixing.

Black-hole absorption/emission processes motivate effective quadratic couplings and dimensional estimates of their coefficients. These are heuristic operator-expansion estimates rather than controlled quantum-gravity calculations.

Polynomial creation-operator ansätze reduce the one-boson/one-fermion spectrum to 2×2 eigenvalue problems. Adding a second fermionic mode gives 4×4 problems; degenerate fermion frequencies permit factorization into quadratic secular equations.

The reviewed GLSM quotient gives C^r/Z_n as t→−∞ and O(−n) over WP_(k₁,…,k_r) at large positive t. Phase dualization gives a mirror LG superpotential W=Σu_i^n+e^(t/n)∏u_i^k_i, orbifolded by the stated monomial-preserving group G=(Z_n)^(r−1).

A prospective extension relates the flowing axial charge of chiral fields to a tachyon potential. The author suggests using tt* geometry and its integrable-system description to calculate this quantity; no such potential is calculated here.

F-term nonrenormalization and classical scaling yield t(Λ)=t+(Σk_i−n)logΛ. Mirror twist-field deformations and local scaling regions identify candidate infrared geometries, including separate orbifold patches when one dominant monomial does not fix all R-charges.
Separate graviton perturbations as ψ(y)h_μν(x), use the warped scalar wave equation, and study its self-adjoint radial problem through asymptotics and integration by parts.

Use SL(n,R)/SO(n) scalar matrices, coupling rescaling, and analytic continuation from compact gaugings. Here n=8,6,5 for D=4,5,7; ξ=−1 produces SO(p,q), while the stated D=4 ξ=0 limit produces a contracted gauging.
Introduce polar coordinates on R^p×R^q, transform the radial coordinates, and restrict to the constraint hypersurface to obtain its intrinsic metric and large-radius asymptotics.

Expand KZ conformal blocks using hypergeometric functions, combine branches to obtain monodromy invariance, and integrate over the worldsheet cross ratio. Regulate the small-u region before exchanging the modulus and intermediate-spin integrals.

Analytically continue normalizable H3 correlators from j = 1/2 + is toward physical real spins. In the four-point representation, deform the intermediate-spin contour and retain residues of poles crossing it.

Construct flowed correlators by bosonizing J3, applying spectral flow in the m basis, and transforming to the x basis. An alternative w = 1 construction fuses with the j = k/2 spectral-flow operator, whose null descendant supplies additional differential equations.
Study corrections by evaluating a probe Dp-brane DBI action in a source Dp′-brane metric and dilaton background, and by reviewing the heterotic Calabi-Yau expansion of bulk fields in ε = T/S.

Use extended supersymmetry to fix the leading Kähler potential and use T-duality and type-I–heterotic duality to relate brane realizations. For Hořava-Witten/T6, the potential is a logarithm of a determinant involving moduli and both branes' matter bilinears, plus the dilaton logarithm.

Trace effective brane couplings to Chern-Simons-squared interactions: wall sources for the eleven-dimensional three-form generate bulk four-form strength, while a type-I′ description uses exchange of the bulk Ramond two-form.

Estimate gauge couplings by dimensional reduction, 1/g_a² ∼ vol_a/(g_S l_S³), and Yukawa couplings by minimal stretched-worldsheet areas, exp(−A/l_S²). A discrete computer search is reported for the Higgs content of selected orbifold models.

Extract disc-level dilaton and complex-structure tadpoles from the long-tube annulus limit. The inferred scalar potential equals the D6-brane volume contribution minus the O6-plane contribution, agreeing with the DBI interpretation.

Use T-duality between magnetic open-string backgrounds and rotated branes. Determine chiral spectra and RR tadpoles from wrapped-cycle data; on the Z3 orbifold, summarize entire brane orbits using effective winding numbers.

Use a causal diamond C(p,q), with endpoints on the brane, that barely contains a bulk event P. Comparing it with a slightly smaller diamond gives support S(P) contained in the brane diamond's edge E2(p,q), locating the image without determining its full field profile.

Construct orthogonal null congruences, calculate their projected null extrinsic curvature, expansion and shear, and evolve them with Raychaudhuri's equation. When shear and matter focusing are negligible, the caustic occurs at λb=λ0−(D−2)/θ0; null geodesics determine its spacetime position.

An alternative calculation expands a rotated probe's Born–Infeld plus Wess–Zumino action in a BPS brane background. The expansion uses small angle, small gradients or velocities, and inverse string-scale separation. The single-probe result carries a normalization caveat relative to the two-brane energy.

Evaluate the one-loop open-string vacuum amplitude, equivalently tree-level closed-string exchange. Winding sums and Jacobi/Dedekind functions encode compactification and oscillators; the long-distance limit retains massless closed strings and gives a 1/y² interaction in four transverse dimensions.

At short distances use the T-dual magnetic-flux/Landau-level spectrum and the Coleman–Weinberg sum Σ(−1)^F m⁴ log(m²)/(64π²). Supertrace cancellations through m⁶ control one-loop finiteness. Analytic continuation past the tachyon threshold produces an imaginary part signaling instability.

The authors expand an S-dual nonabelian Born–Infeld action and use SU(2) matrix representations to describe dielectric polarization. They compare its preferred irreducible fuzzy-sphere configuration with an NS5 worldvolume calculation using magnetic flux and a polar-angle effective potential.

Static first-order NS5 domain-wall equations provide a supersymmetric comparison. Vacuum decay is treated with a radially symmetric Euclidean NS5 trajectory, Hamilton equations, and a small-p/M thin-wall approximation using the supersymmetric wall tension.

For the proposed field-theory description at p=1, a massive flavor pair temporarily raises the flavor number to the color number. Integrating it out motivates a superpotential retaining color-charged baryonic fields; extension to general p is explicitly a guess.

For two fields, impose power-law a(η) and logarithmic ϕ(η), integrate the σ equation once, and require consistent time dependence in the remaining background equations to constrain exponents and integration constants.

Quantize the canonical scalar perturbation v=aQ in its sub-Hubble vacuum. For the power-law backgrounds, solve its mode equation using Bessel/Hankel functions, with z=aϕ̇/H and ζ=v/z, then extract the long-wavelength curvature power spectrum.

Model the short bounce by matching induced metric and extrinsic curvature, giving continuity of Φ and ζ on a constant-density surface. Track ζ=D+S∫dη/z² and the associated Φ modes to determine whether the contracting growing mode feeds the expanding constant mode.

Compute W=∫G3∧Ω explicitly from torus periods and integral flux coefficients. Requiring G3 to have type (2,1) becomes W=∂φW=∂τijW=0: eleven equations for ten complex variables, explaining why generic flux choices fail to preserve supersymmetry.

Solve restricted flux families using common quadratic factors of two integer cubic polynomials; also approach the inverse problem by choosing moduli first. A broader algebraic reduction produces a quartic for the axion-dilaton, followed by a nonlinear integer consistency condition.

Apply Killing-spinor conditions and primitivity J∧G3=0. Once complex structure is selected, primitivity supplies up to six real linear constraints on nine Kähler metric components. Representation analysis supplies additional restrictions for enhanced supersymmetry.

Dimensionally reduce the large-radius bulk and D3 DBI actions, treating four-form periodicity and gauge identifications explicitly. Analyze wrapped-brane BPS masses, Higgs screening, worldvolume Bianchi identities, and instanton phases to constrain possible discrete dualities.
Count surviving Killing spinors using Gχ=Gχ*=Gγmχ*=0. Identify three alternative complex structures in which the same flux is primitive (2,1).
Analyze orientifold flux quantization through charged-particle quantum mechanics on T2/Z2, then extend the fixed-point argument to wrapped fundamental and D-strings probing three-form flux.
Euclidean Kerr bounce solutions, decay estimates Γ ∼ exp(−I), and analytic continuation from a zero-momentum surface to study Lorentzian bubble expansion.
String quantization on globally twisted flat backgrounds; winding energies and a gyromagnetic angular-momentum coupling diagnose tachyon onset and localization.

Membrane worldvolume gravitational-anomaly cancellation requires left-moving current algebra with c = 16 distributed between boundaries; worldsheet GSO comparisons constrain candidate heterotic limits.

Use a generalized Kaluza–Klein ansatz A(0)m(x,y)=am(x)−wmn yn/2 for the RR potentials. Linear internal-coordinate dependence generates constant RR flux and covariant derivatives involving the torus KK vectors.

Rotate mass and flux parameters with a specific SL(2,R) element, lift the rotated four-dimensional solution to ordinary six-dimensional IIA, then apply the imported IIA/K3–heterotic/T4 duality and oxidize the heterotic solution to ten dimensions.

Combine the RR vector equations of motion and Bianchi identities into an SL(2,R) doublet by introducing dual field strengths. This establishes the electric-magnetic part of the proposed duality at field-equation level.
